method: blind back-translation by fresh-context language agents (one per batch, English opened only after the back-translation was written), verdict MATCH/DRIFT/MISMATCH against the keyed English; wrong-source probe by word overlap against sibling lines; lang-check.mjs findings as corpus support

rows.en: That is the first hadeda up and the entire valley is about to know.
rows.text: Daar's die eerste hadeda op, en nou gaan die hele vallei dit weet.
rows.back: There's the first hadeda up, and now the whole valley's going to know about it.

rows.en: Monday, and the alarm on this farm has feathers and no snooze button.
rows.text: Maandag, en die wekker op hierdie plaas het vere en geen snooze nie.
rows.back: Monday, and the alarm clock on this farm has feathers and no snooze.

rows.en: That sky lasts about six minutes and the bird is the only one watching.
rows.text: Daardie lug hou omtrent ses minute, en die voël is die enigste een wat kyk.
rows.back: That sky lasts about six minutes, and the bird is the only one watching.

rows.en: Even the hadedas sound happy.
rows.text: Selfs die hadedas klink gelukkig.
rows.back: Even the hadedas sound happy.

rows.en: Africa's sky just hits different.
rows.text: Afrika se lug tref net anders.
rows.back: African sky just hits different.

rows.en: The sun woke up and chose glorious.
rows.text: Vandag se son het opgedaag met attitude.
rows.back: Today's sun showed up with attitude.
rows.reason: EN meme punchline 'woke up and chose glorious' is gone; 'opgedaag met attitude' (showed up with attitude) reads sassy rather than glorious.

wrongSource.en: The Helderberg is showing off today.

reasons: DRIFT: EN meme punchline 'woke up and chose glorious' is gone; 'opgedaag met attitude' (showed up with attitude) reads sassy rather than glorious.
WRONG SOURCE? The back-translation is closer to another line of the same photograph: "The Helderberg is showing off today."

rows.en: Somewhere an estate agent is saying 'lifestyle'.
rows.text: Iewers sê 'n eiendomsagent 'lifestyle'.
rows.back: Somewhere an estate agent is saying 'lifestyle'.

rows.en: Bottle this one. Open it in winter.
rows.text: Bottel hierdie een. Maak hom oop in die winter.
rows.back: Bottle this one. Open it in winter.

rows.en: This is the weather we brag about overseas.
rows.text: Dit is die weer waaroor ons oorsee spog.
rows.back: This is the weather we brag about overseas.
rows.note: unsure: 'oorsee spog' - brag about when we're overseas, or brag to people overseas

rows.en: Not a breath of haze this morning; even the mountain got up early.
rows.text: Nie 'n sweempie wasigheid vanoggend nie; selfs die berg het vroeg opgestaan.
rows.back: Not a hint of haze this morning; even the mountain got up early.

rows.en: This light lasts about twenty minutes and the walk to school gets all of it.
rows.text: Hierdie lig hou omtrent twintig minute, en die stap skool toe kry alles.
rows.back: This light lasts about twenty minutes, and the walk to school gets all of it.

rows.en: He will move twice before lunch and both times by about a metre.
rows.text: Hy gaan twee keer skuif voor middagete, en altwee keer omtrent 'n meter.
rows.back: He's going to move twice before lunch, and both times about a metre.
rows.note: unsure: who 'hy' is (a dog, a person chasing shade?) - not clear from the text

rows.en: The sun took its time this morning. Worth the wait.
rows.text: Die son vat sy tyd vanoggend, en dit wys.
rows.back: The sun's taking its time this morning, and it shows.
rows.reason: EN payoff 'Worth the wait' is lost; 'en dit wys' (and it shows) makes the slow sun sound sluggish, flipping the positive note.
reasons: DRIFT: EN payoff 'Worth the wait' is lost; 'en dit wys' (and it shows) makes the slow sun sound sluggish, flipping the positive note.

rows.en: Enjoy it. There's a cold front out there doing warm-ups.
rows.text: Geniet dit. Die koue front het klaar sy tasse gepak.
rows.back: Enjoy it. The cold front has already packed its bags.
rows.reason: EN 'a cold front out there doing warm-ups' (coming); 'het klaar sy tasse gepak' can easily read as the front having already left, the opposite claim.
reasons: DRIFT: EN 'a cold front out there doing warm-ups' (coming); 'het klaar sy tasse gepak' can easily read as the front having already left, the opposite claim.

rows.en: The sun cleared the roof about ten minutes ago and the tiles are already warm.
rows.text: Die son is omtrent tien minute gelede oor die dak, en die teëls is klaar warm.
rows.back: The sun cleared the roof about ten minutes ago, and the tiles are already warm.

rows.en: Nothing in the sky to slow the sun down, so the stoep warmed up before seven.
rows.text: Niks in die lug om die son te vertraag nie, so die stoep was voor sewe al warm.
rows.back: Nothing in the sky to slow the sun down, so the stoep was already warm before seven.

rows.en: She is watering at seven because by nine it would be a waste.
rows.text: Sy gee sewe-uur water, want teen nege-uur is dit gemors.
rows.back: She waters at seven, because by nine it's a waste.
rows.note: 'gemors' - waste/mess; read as the water being wasted (evaporates)

rows.en: Not one cloud, which means those geraniums will need this again tonight.
rows.text: Nie een wolk nie, wat beteken daardie malvas gaan dit vanaand weer nodig hê.
rows.back: Not one cloud, which means those malvas are going to need it again tonight.
rows.note: unsure: 'malvas' - pelargoniums (the plant) most likely, not malva pudding; 'dit' presumably water

rows.en: Mornings like this are why Capetonians never stop mentioning it.
rows.text: Oggende soos dié is hoekom Kapenaars nooit ophou spog nie.
rows.back: Mornings like this are why Capetonians never stop bragging.

rows.en: Zero drama in the sky. Highly unusual. Gladly accepted.
rows.text: Die dag begin sonder drama. Verdag, maar ons vat dit.
rows.back: The day starts without drama. Suspicious, but we'll take it.

rows.en: Not one metre of shade on this promenade, which is why they are out at six.
rows.text: Nie een meter skaduwee op hierdie promenade nie — dis hoekom hulle sesuur al uit is.
rows.back: Not one metre of shade on this promenade - that's why they're out by six already.

rows.en: The sea is that flat about nine mornings a year and this is one of them.
rows.text: Die see is omtrent nege oggende 'n jaar so plat, en dit is een van hulle.
rows.back: The sea is this flat about nine mornings a year, and this is one of them.

rows.en: That mountain is that sharp because there is nothing at all in the air today.
rows.text: Daardie berg is so skerp omdat daar vandag absoluut niks in die lug is nie.
rows.back: That mountain is so sharp because there's absolutely nothing in the air today.

rows.en: The sky is completely empty, which means this is as cool as today gets.
rows.text: Die lug is heeltemal leeg, so koeler as nou word dit vandag nie.
rows.back: The sky is completely empty, so today it won't get any cooler than it is now.

rows.en: Friday, and by noon that paving is going to be too hot to stand on.
rows.text: Vrydag, en teen twaalfuur gaan daardie plaveisel te warm wees om op te staan.
rows.back: Friday, and by noon that paving is going to be too hot to stand on.

rows.en: Days like this should come with a soundtrack.
rows.text: Dae soos hierdie behoort 'n klankbaan te hê.
rows.back: Days like this should have a soundtrack.

rows.en: The type of day that makes people text 'lekker dag hey'.
rows.text: Die soort dag wat mense laat 'lekker dag ne' stuur.
rows.back: The kind of day that makes people send 'lekker day, hey'.

rows.en: Morning people might be onto something. Don't tell them.
rows.text: Oggendmense is dalk oor iets reg. Sê dit net vir niemand nie.
rows.back: Morning people might be right about something. Just don't tell anyone.

rows.en: The weekend doesn't get better than this.
rows.text: Die naweek word nie beter as dit nie.
rows.back: The weekend doesn't get better than this.

rows.en: 'One hour at the beach.' History's most confident lie.
rows.text: 'Net 'n uurtjie strand toe.' Vier uur later...
rows.back: 'Just an hour at the beach.' Four hours later...

rows.en: Not enough wind this morning to put one wrinkle on that water.
rows.text: Nie genoeg wind vanoggend om een plooi op daardie water te sit nie.
rows.back: Not enough wind this morning to put one wrinkle on that water.

rows.en: The beach is doubling as a mirror, which takes one morning of absolutely no wind.
rows.text: Die strand is ook 'n spieël, en dit vat een oggend van absoluut geen wind nie.
rows.back: The beach is also a mirror, and it takes one morning of absolutely no wind.
rows.note: 'ook' reads oddly - 'is a mirror too' vs 'can be a mirror'; feels like 'only takes' is missing

rows.en: One sunrise, used twice — once in the sky and once off the wet sand.
rows.text: Een sonsopkoms, twee keer gebruik — een keer in die lug en een keer van die nat sand af.
rows.back: One sunrise, used twice - once in the sky and once off the wet sand.

rows.en: The Weber has been watching him water that lawn for twenty minutes now.
rows.text: Die Weber kyk nou al twintig minute hoe hy daardie grasperk natmaak.
rows.back: The Weber has been watching him water that lawn for twenty minutes now.

rows.en: Coffee in one hand, hose in the other, and the whole day still ahead.
rows.text: Koffie in die een hand, tuinslang in die ander, en die hele dag lê nog voor.
rows.back: Coffee in one hand, hosepipe in the other, and the whole day still ahead.

rows.en: This is the only twenty minutes of the day that belong to him.
rows.text: Dit is die enigste twintig minute van die dag wat aan hom behoort.
rows.back: These are the only twenty minutes of the day that belong to him.

rows.en: The jacaranda is dropping purple on a lawn he has just finished watering.
rows.text: Die jakaranda laat pers val op 'n grasperk wat hy pas natgemaak het.
rows.back: The jacaranda is dropping purple onto a lawn he's just watered.

rows.en: Nobody inside that house is awake yet and that is entirely the plan.
rows.text: Niemand in daardie huis is al wakker nie, en dit is presies die plan.
rows.back: Nobody in that house is awake yet, and that's exactly the plan.

rows.en: This is the weather the weekend was invented for.
rows.text: Dit is die weer waarvoor naweke geskep is.
rows.back: This is the weather weekends were made for.

rows.en: Weather this perfect is on loan. The southeaster keeps receipts.
rows.text: Weer só mooi is nie gratis nie. Iewers wag 'n suidooster.
rows.back: Weather this beautiful isn't free. Somewhere a south-easter is waiting.

rows.en: That dry patch is what a week of cloudless skies does to a lawn.
rows.text: Daardie droë kol is wat 'n week van wolklose lug aan 'n grasperk doen.
rows.back: That dry patch is what a week of cloudless sky does to a lawn.

rows.en: A sky this clear hands you one cool hour, and this is it.
rows.text: 'n Lug só helder gee jou een koel uur, en dit is hy.
rows.back: A sky this clear gives you one cool hour, and this is it.

rows.en: The Weber's been waiting all week for this.
rows.text: Die Weber het die hele week hiervoor gewag.
rows.back: The Weber has been waiting for this all week.

rows.en: When the weather behaves this well, so do we. Roughly.
rows.text: As die weer só gedra, gedra ons ook. Min of meer.
rows.back: If the weather behaves like this, we behave too. More or less.

rows.en: Even Monday looks photogenic in this light.
rows.text: Oggendson wat só lyk maak selfs Maandag draaglik.
rows.back: Morning sun that looks like this makes even Monday bearable.
rows.reason: EN says Monday 'looks photogenic in this light'; AF says morning sun makes Monday 'draaglik' (bearable) - different claim, photo joke lost.
reasons: DRIFT: EN says Monday 'looks photogenic in this light'; AF says morning sun makes Monday 'draaglik' (bearable) - different claim, photo joke lost.

rows.en: Perfect day. No excuses. Get out.
rows.text: Perfekte dag. Geen verskonings nie. Gaan uit.
rows.back: Perfect day. No excuses. Get out.

rows.en: The sky made the dress-code decision this morning and he just obeyed it.
rows.text: Die lug het vanoggend oor die kleredrag besluit, en hy het net gehoorsaam.
rows.back: The sky decided the dress code this morning, and he just obeyed.

rows.en: A sky like that overrules HR, and everybody at reception knows it.
rows.text: 'n Lug soos daardie oorheers HR, en almal by ontvangs weet dit.
rows.back: A sky like that overrules HR, and everyone at reception knows it.
rows.note: unsure: 'oorheers' - dominates/overrules; the HR/reception joke is unclear to me

rows.en: Summer filed its arrival notice this morning; the shirt is the paperwork.
rows.text: Die somer het vanoggend sy aankomskennisgewing ingedien; die hemp is die papierwerk.
rows.back: Summer filed its notice of arrival this morning; the shirt is the paperwork.

rows.en: Everything looks 4K today. The sky's in ultra mode.
rows.text: Alles lyk 4K vandag. Die lug is in ultra modus.
rows.back: Everything looks 4K today. The sky is in ultra mode.

rows.en: Your excuse to stay inside just expired.
rows.text: Jou verskoning om binne te bly het pas verval.
rows.back: Your excuse to stay inside just expired.

rows.en: The only rain this garden has seen all month comes out of a pipe.
rows.text: Die enigste reën wat hierdie tuin die hele maand gesien het, kom uit 'n pyp.
rows.back: The only rain this garden has seen all month comes out of a pipe.

rows.en: Weeks of nothing but blue, and even the hadeda has to queue at the sprinkler.
rows.text: Weke van niks behalwe blou nie, en selfs die hadeda moet by die sproeier toustaan.
rows.back: Weeks of nothing but blue, and even the hadeda has to queue at the sprinkler.

rows.en: The sun has had this lawn to itself for a month and it is winning.
rows.text: Die son het hierdie grasperk al 'n maand vir homself, en hy wen.
rows.back: The sun has had this lawn to itself for a month now, and it's winning.

rows.en: One perfect day issued. Non-transferable. Spend it wisely.
rows.text: Een perfekte dag uitgereik. Moet hom nie op admin mors nie.
rows.back: One perfect day issued. Don't waste it on admin.

rows.en: If you're working today, we feel sorry for you.
rows.text: As jy vandag werk, jammer vir jou.
rows.back: If you're working today, shame, sorry for you.

rows.en: If you're inside, you're doing it wrong.
rows.text: As jy binne is, doen jy dit verkeerd.
rows.back: If you're inside, you're doing it wrong.

rows.en: The weather moved the office to the roof and productivity can argue later.
rows.text: Die weer het die kantoor dak toe geskuif, en produktiwiteit kan later stry.
rows.back: The weather moved the office to the roof, and productivity can argue later.

rows.en: Wednesday this warm turns every roof in Joburg into a second office.
rows.text: 'n Woensdag só warm maak van elke dak in Joburg 'n tweede kantoor.
rows.back: A Wednesday this warm turns every roof in Joburg into a second office.

rows.en: The sun took the direct route today: straight down, no traffic.
rows.text: Die son het vandag die direkte roete gevat: reguit af, geen verkeer nie.
rows.back: The sun took the direct route today: straight down, no traffic.

rows.en: The sky's giving everything today.
rows.text: Die lug gee alles vandag.
rows.back: The sky is giving it everything today.

rows.en: Weather this well-behaved is definitely up to something.
rows.text: Als dié blou, dié vroeg? Iets broei.
rows.back: All this blue, this early? Something's brewing.

rows.en: The sun stayed out for the whole match and is hanging around for the chips.
rows.text: Die son het vir die hele wedstryd uitgebly en draai nog rond vir die tjips.
rows.back: The sun stayed out for the whole match and is still hanging around for the chips.

rows.en: Match played, chips out, and the sky never once threatened the fixture.
rows.text: Wedstryd gespeel, tjips uit, en die lug het nie een keer die wedstryd bedreig nie.
rows.back: Match played, chips out, and the sky didn't threaten the game once.

rows.en: The sort of afternoon that keeps a whole soccer team sitting on a curb.
rows.text: Die soort middag wat 'n hele sokkerspan op 'n randsteen laat sit.
rows.back: The kind of afternoon that sits a whole soccer team down on a kerb.

rows.en: Whoever booked the four o'clock meeting is going to be sitting in it alone.
rows.text: Wie ook al die vieruur-vergadering bespreek het, gaan alleen daarin sit.
rows.back: Whoever booked the four o'clock meeting is going to sit in it alone.

rows.en: Absolutely beautiful out there.
rows.text: Absoluut pragtig daar buite.
rows.back: Absolutely beautiful out there.

rows.en: Forty floors of glass and every one of them is showing the same blue.
rows.text: Veertig verdiepings glas, en elkeen wys dieselfde blou.
rows.back: Forty storeys of glass, and every one shows the same blue.

rows.en: The afternoon held exactly like the morning promised, which almost never happens.
rows.text: Die middag het presies gehou soos die oggend belowe het, wat amper nooit gebeur nie.
rows.back: The afternoon held up exactly as the morning promised, which almost never happens.

rows.en: Saturday energy: maximum. Responsibilities: minimum.
rows.text: Saterdagenergie: maksimum. Verantwoordelikhede: minimum.
rows.back: Saturday energy: maximum. Responsibilities: minimum.

rows.en: Perfect for doing absolutely nothing.
rows.text: Perfek om absoluut niks te doen nie.
rows.back: Perfect for doing absolutely nothing.

rows.en: Be honest — you opened this app to confirm Saturday's braai.
rows.text: Check jy die weer, of check jy of Saterdag se braai aan is? Presies.
rows.back: Are you checking the weather, or checking if Saturday's braai is on? Exactly.

rows.en: That lawn stopped asking the sky for rain somewhere around the start of November.
rows.text: Daardie grasperk het êrens teen die begin van November opgehou om die lug vir reën te vra.
rows.back: That lawn stopped asking the sky for rain somewhere around the start of November.

rows.en: The sun has done more to that lawn this month than any mower ever will.
rows.text: Die son het hierdie maand meer aan daardie grasperk gedoen as wat enige grassnyer ooit sal.
rows.back: The sun has done more to that lawn this month than any lawnmower ever will.

rows.en: Today's plans: exist outside.
rows.text: Vandag se planne: bestaan buitentoe.
rows.back: Today's plans: exist outdoors.

rows.en: Main character weather right here.
rows.text: Hoofkarakter weer reg hier.
rows.back: Main character weather right here.
rows.note: unsure: 'weer' - 'weather' (main-character weather) or 'again' (main character again, right here)

rows.en: Jacarandas only do this three weeks a year, and the sky decided to match.
rows.text: Jakarandas doen dit net drie weke 'n jaar, en die lug het besluit om te pas.
rows.back: Jacarandas only do this three weeks a year, and the sky decided to match.

rows.en: Grass warm, sky empty — the kind of Sunday that resets a whole family.
rows.text: Gras warm, lug leeg — die soort Sondag wat 'n hele gesin herlaai.
rows.back: Grass warm, sky empty - the kind of Sunday that recharges a whole family.

rows.en: The sun is really milking this exit. Honestly, deserved.
rows.text: Die son gaan af soos hy weet ons kyk.
rows.back: The sun goes down like he knows we're watching.

rows.en: Cirrus this pink means the sky is completely dry all the way up.
rows.text: Veerwolke só pienk beteken die lug is heeltemal droog, tot bo.
rows.back: Cirrus this pink means the air is completely dry, all the way up.

rows.en: A sunset like this pulls an audience, and tonight it is two birds on a wire.
rows.text: 'n Sonsondergang soos dié trek 'n gehoor, en vanaand is dit twee voëls op 'n draad.
rows.back: A sunset like this draws a crowd, and tonight it's two birds on a wire.

rows.en: Monday got the best sky of the week and is wasting it on a farm road.
rows.text: Maandag het die mooiste lug van die week gekry en mors dit op 'n plaaspad.
rows.back: Monday got the prettiest sky of the week and is wasting it on a farm road.

rows.en: This is the day the brochure was talking about.
rows.text: Dit is die dag waaroor die brosjure gepraat het.
rows.back: This is the day the brochure was talking about.

rows.en: A gradient that clean means not one cloud between here and tomorrow.
rows.text: 'n Kleurverloop só skoon beteken nie een wolk tussen hier en môre nie.
rows.back: A gradient this clean means not one cloud between here and tomorrow.

rows.en: Orange to navy with nothing in between — the walk home slowed down for it.
rows.text: Oranje tot donkerblou met niks tussenin nie — die stap huis toe het stadiger geword daarvoor.
rows.back: Orange to dark blue with nothing in between - the walk home slowed down for it.

rows.en: The day used up every hour of light and still had this left over.
rows.text: Die dag het elke uur lig opgebruik en het steeds dít oorgehad.
rows.back: The day used up every hour of light and still had this left over.

rows.en: Clear dusk. Use it before it clocks off.
rows.text: Skoon skemer. Gebruik dit voor dit uitklok.
rows.back: Clear dusk. Use it before it clocks out.

rows.en: The weather said yes. That’s on you now.
rows.text: Die weer het ja gesê. Nou lê dit by jou.
rows.back: The weather said yes. Now it's up to you.

rows.en: That dust is hanging in the air because there is no wind to take it anywhere.
rows.text: Daardie stof hang in die lug, want daar is geen wind om dit êrens heen te vat nie.
rows.back: That dust is hanging in the air because there's no wind to take it anywhere.

rows.en: You can see three ridgelines from here, which is what no-haze evenings are for.
rows.text: Jy kan drie bergrûe van hier af sien, en dis waarvoor aande sonder wasigheid is.
rows.back: You can see three mountain ridges from here, and that's what haze-free evenings are for.

rows.en: The sun is at the exact height where the whole veld goes gold.
rows.text: Die son is op presies die hoogte waar die hele veld goud word.
rows.back: The sun is at exactly the height where the whole veld turns gold.

rows.en: Golden hour turns even the dust into a special effect.
rows.text: Golden hour maak selfs die stof 'n spesiale effek.
rows.back: Golden hour makes even the dust a special effect.
rows.note: grammar odd: 'maak selfs die stof 'n spesiale effek' - reads as 'makes the dust (into) a special effect', a 'van' seems missing

rows.en: An evening this clear pays out its last hour in gold. Spend all of it.
rows.text: 'n Aand só helder betaal sy laaste uur in goud uit. Spandeer alles.
rows.back: An evening this clear pays out its last hour in gold. Spend it all.

rows.en: Clear evening. The grass has no excuse.
rows.text: Skoon aand. Die gras het geen verskoning nie.
rows.back: Clear evening. The grass has no excuse.
rows.note: unsure: joke unclear - maybe no excuse not to mow, or 'the lawn has no excuse' for something else

rows.en: Good weather. Unfortunately.
rows.text: Goeie weer. Ongelukkig.
rows.back: Good weather. Unfortunately.
rows.note: unsure: the joke is not clear from the Afrikaans - 'unfortunately' for whom?

rows.en: The sky behaved. So must you.
rows.text: Die lug het hom gedra. Nou jy.
rows.back: The sky behaved itself. Now you.

rows.en: This is the first hour since breakfast that lawn work has been survivable.
rows.text: Dit is die eerste uur sedert ontbyt dat tuinwerk oorleefbaar is.
rows.back: This is the first hour since breakfast that garden work is survivable.

rows.en: A clear evening pays out about forty minutes of gold, and it has just started.
rows.text: 'n Helder aand betaal omtrent veertig minute goud uit, en dit het pas begin.
rows.back: A clear evening pays out about forty minutes of gold, and it's only just started.

rows.en: Not a leaf moving — the day is closing as calm as it opened.
rows.text: Nie 'n blaar wat roer nie — die dag sluit net so kalm as wat hy oopgemaak het.
rows.back: Not a leaf stirring - the day is closing as calmly as it opened.

rows.en: Kuier weather. Get the people together.
rows.text: Kuierweer. Kry die mense bymekaar.
rows.back: Kuier weather. Get the people together.
rows.note: 'kuierweer' = weather for visiting/hanging out with people

rows.en: Cricket till the light goes, and light like this takes its time going.
rows.text: Krieket tot die lig weg is, en lig soos dié vat sy tyd om te gaan.
rows.back: Cricket till the light's gone, and light like this takes its time leaving.

rows.en: One planet up, no clouds coming, and the whole dorp still outside.
rows.text: Een planeet op, geen wolke op pad nie, en die hele dorp is nog buite.
rows.back: One planet up, no clouds on the way, and the whole town is still outside.

rows.en: The Karoo cools fast under a clear sky, but nobody has noticed yet.
rows.text: Die Karoo koel vinnig af onder 'n skoon lug, maar niemand het dit nog agtergekom nie.
rows.back: The Karoo cools down fast under a clear sky, but nobody's noticed yet.

rows.en: That fire was lit before anybody needed it, which is what a clear evening does.
rows.text: Daardie vuur is aangesteek voor iemand dit nodig gehad het — dis wat 'n skoon aand doen.
rows.back: That fire was lit before anyone needed it - that's what a clear evening does.

rows.en: Saturday, and the sky went from orange to blue without one cloud interrupting.
rows.text: Saterdag, en die lug het van oranje na blou gegaan sonder dat een wolk hom gesteur het.
rows.back: Saturday, and the sky went from orange to blue without a single cloud bothering it.

rows.en: The coals aren't going to light themselves.
rows.text: Die kole gaan nie hulself aansteek nie.
rows.back: The coals aren't going to light themselves.

rows.en: Call the mates. Get the meat. Let's go.
rows.text: Bel die tjommies. Kry die vleis. Kom ons gaan.
rows.back: Call the tjommies. Get the meat. Let's go.

rows.en: Fire up the Weber. It's the law.
rows.text: Steek die Weber aan. Dit is die wet.
rows.back: Light the Weber. It's the law.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'wet' is core English weather vocabulary left untranslated

rows.en: The first star is out before the last of the sunset has even left.
rows.text: Die eerste ster is uit voor die laaste van die sonsondergang eers weg is.
rows.back: The first star is out before the last of the sunset is even gone.

rows.en: The weather gods are showing off.
rows.text: Die weergode pronk vandag.
rows.back: The weather gods are showing off today.

rows.en: Weekend vibes so strong they need their own playlist.
rows.text: Naweek vibes so sterk hulle het hul eie playlist nodig.
rows.back: Weekend vibes so strong they need their own playlist.

rows.en: The evening showed up in its Sunday best.
rows.text: Die aand het opgedaag met sy Sondagklere aan.
rows.back: The evening showed up in its Sunday best.

rows.en: Flat sea, spent sun, and air still warm enough to sit around in a wet wetsuit.
rows.text: Plat see, moeë son, en die lug nog warm genoeg om in 'n nat wetsuit rond te sit.
rows.back: Flat sea, tired sun, and the air still warm enough to sit around in a wet wetsuit.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'wetsuit' means 'law; act; ordinance' — nothing in the English source; it is 1 letter from 'het', the usual word for 'spent'

rows.en: The wind that usually owns this coast has taken the evening off.
rows.text: Die wind wat gewoonlik hierdie kus besit, het vanaand af.
rows.back: The wind that usually owns this coast has the evening off.

rows.en: That sky is doing its whole show over a sea too flat to interrupt it.
rows.text: Daardie lug doen sy hele vertoning oor 'n see te plat om hom te steur.
rows.back: That sky is putting on its whole show over a sea too flat to disturb it.
rows.note: unsure: 'om hom te steur' - too flat to disturb it (the reflection) or too flat to care

rows.en: The hadedas are sleeping. Finally.
rows.text: Die hadedas slaap. Uiteindelik.
rows.back: The hadedas are asleep. Finally.

rows.en: Somewhere a cricket is really giving it.
rows.text: Iewers is 'n kriek besig om sy hart uit te sing.
rows.back: Somewhere a cricket is singing its heart out.

rows.en: Warm, still and clear: every insect in the province is at this one lamp.
rows.text: Warm, stil en helder: elke insek in die provinsie is by hierdie een lamp.
rows.back: Warm, still and clear: every insect in the province is at this one lamp.

rows.en: Windows-open weather has arrived, and word has reached the moths.
rows.text: Vensters-oop-weer het aangebreek, en die nuus het die motte bereik.
rows.back: Windows-open weather has arrived, and the news has reached the moths.

rows.en: Not a breath of wind, or that lantern would be having a quieter evening.
rows.text: Nie 'n luggie nie, anders sou daardie lantern 'n rustiger aand hê.
rows.back: Not a breath of wind, otherwise that lantern would be having a calmer evening.

rows.en: There is enough moon out there to hang washing by, and somebody did.
rows.text: Die maan skyn helder genoeg om wasgoed op te hang, en iemand het dit gedoen.
rows.back: The moon is bright enough to hang washing by, and someone has.

rows.en: It will be dry by morning and damp again by six, which is the deal.
rows.text: Teen die oggend is dit droog en teen sesuur weer klam — so werk dit maar.
rows.back: By morning it's dry and by six it's damp again - that's just how it goes.
rows.note: unsure: what 'dit' is (the washing?) and whether 'sesuur' is 6am or 6pm - sequence reads confusingly

rows.en: The moon's doing the most tonight.
rows.text: Die maan doen sy bes vanaand.
rows.back: The moon is doing its best tonight.
rows.reason: EN slang 'doing the most' (showing off, extra) became 'doen sy bes' (doing its best), which reads as effort/trying, not excess.
reasons: DRIFT: EN slang 'doing the most' (showing off, extra) became 'doen sy bes' (doing its best), which reads as effort/trying, not excess.

rows.en: Quiet out there. Almost suspicious.
rows.text: Stil daarbuite. Byna verdag.
rows.back: Quiet out there. Almost suspicious.

rows.en: Good night, South Africa.
rows.text: Goeienag, Suid-Afrika.
rows.back: Goodnight, South Africa.

rows.en: Sky this clear means tomorrow's a scorcher. Stay a while.
rows.text: Lug só helder beteken môre skroei. Sit gerus nog 'n rukkie.
rows.back: A sky this clear means tomorrow scorches. Go ahead, sit a while longer.

rows.en: Ten thousand streetlights down there and the sky is still winning tonight.
rows.text: Tienduisend straatligte daar onder, en die lug wen vanaand steeds.
rows.back: Ten thousand streetlights down there, and the sky still wins tonight.

rows.en: Tomorrow's weather is tomorrow's problem.
rows.text: Môre se weer is môre se probleem.
rows.back: Tomorrow's weather is tomorrow's problem.

rows.en: Verandah weather. The couch will understand.
rows.text: Stoepsit-weer. Die TV kan maar wag.
rows.back: Stoep-sitting weather. The TV can wait.

rows.en: The moon is out and somebody small is hearing about it for the first time.
rows.text: Die maan is uit, en iemand kleintjies hoor vir die eerste keer daarvan.
rows.back: The moon is out, and somebody's little ones are hearing about it for the first time.
rows.note: garbled: 'iemand kleintjies' is ungrammatical - reads as missing 'se' (someone's little ones)
rows.reason: 'iemand kleintjies' is ungrammatical (missing 'se') and turns EN 'somebody small' (one child) into 'someone's little ones'.
reasons: DRIFT: 'iemand kleintjies' is ungrammatical (missing 'se') and turns EN 'somebody small' (one child) into 'someone's little ones'.

rows.en: Not a cloud. Just you and the Southern Cross.
rows.text: Nie 'n wolk nie. Net jy en die Suiderkruis.
rows.back: Not a cloud. Just you and the Southern Cross.

rows.en: Clear enough that even the cat is checking the sky.
rows.text: Helder genoeg dat selfs die kat die lug nagaan.
rows.back: Clear enough that even the cat is checking the sky.

rows.en: Braai weather, boet! No excuses.
rows.text: Braaiweer, boet! Geen verskonings nie.
rows.back: Braai weather, boet! No excuses.

rows.en: 'Just one sundowner' — famous last words, every single time.
rows.text: 'Een sundowner,' sê die mense wat die sterre gaan sien uitkom.
rows.back: 'One sundowner,' say the people who are going to watch the stars come out.

rows.en: A Friday night warm enough that the table walked itself outside.
rows.text: 'n Vrydagaand warm genoeg dat die tafel self buitentoe geloop het.
rows.back: A Friday night warm enough that the table walked itself outside.

rows.en: Nothing up there but stars, which is how supper ends up under them.
rows.text: Niks daarbo behalwe sterre nie, en so beland aandete onder hulle.
rows.back: Nothing up there but stars, and that's how supper ends up under them.

rows.en: The evening is holding at exactly the temperature nobody talks about.
rows.text: Die aand bly presies op die temperatuur waaroor niemand praat nie.
rows.back: The evening is staying at exactly the temperature nobody talks about.

rows.en: You have to drive two hours from anywhere to get a sky like that.
rows.text: Jy moet twee uur van enige plek af ry om so 'n lug te kry.
rows.back: You have to drive two hours from anywhere to get a sky like this.

rows.en: Saturday night, and the entertainment is free and about four billion years old.
rows.text: Saterdagaand, en die vermaak is verniet en omtrent vier miljard jaar oud.
rows.back: Saturday night, and the entertainment is free and about four billion years old.

rows.en: Perfect night to actually see the Milky Way.
rows.text: Perfekte nag om die Melkweg te sien.
rows.back: Perfect night to see the Milky Way.

rows.en: No alarm. No agenda. Just vibes.
rows.text: Geen alarm. Geen agenda. Net vibes.
rows.back: No alarm. No agenda. Just vibes.

rows.en: That is the centre of the galaxy and it is coming up behind a koppie.
rows.text: Dit is die middel van die sterrestelsel, en dit kom op agter 'n koppie.
rows.back: That's the middle of the galaxy, and it's coming up behind a koppie.

rows.en: Sunday night, and the best thing on tonight is not on a screen.
rows.text: Sondagaand, en die beste program vanaand is nie op 'n skerm nie.
rows.back: Sunday night, and the best show tonight isn't on a screen.

rows.en: The sky looks like it's showing off.
rows.text: Die lug lyk of dit pronk.
rows.back: The sky looks like it's showing off.

rows.en: Someone turned the stars up to full volume.
rows.text: Iemand het die sterre se volume opgedraai.
rows.back: Someone turned up the stars' volume.

rows.en: Cancel everything. This is THE day winter was hiding.
rows.text: Kanselleer alles. Dis DIÉ dag.
rows.back: Cancel everything. It's THE day.
rows.reason: EN 'THE day winter was hiding' - the winter/season hook is dropped; AF is just 'Dis DIÉ dag'.
reasons: DRIFT: EN 'THE day winter was hiding' - the winter/season hook is dropped; AF is just 'Dis DIÉ dag'.

rows.en: Nature's flexing and we're here for it.
rows.text: Natuur pronk en ons is hier daarvoor.
rows.back: Nature's showing off and we're here for it.

rows.en: Africa showing off again. Quietly devastating.
rows.text: Afrika pronk weer. Dit mag maar.
rows.back: Africa's showing off again. It's allowed.
rows.reason: EN punchline 'Quietly devastating' replaced by 'Dit mag maar' (it's allowed) - different, flatter payoff.
reasons: DRIFT: EN punchline 'Quietly devastating' replaced by 'Dit mag maar' (it's allowed) - different, flatter payoff.

rows.en: Agapanthus out, hadeda busy, sky empty: high summer is running on schedule.
rows.text: Agapante oop, hadeda besig, lug leeg: hoogsomer loop volgens skedule.
rows.back: Agapanthus open, hadeda busy, sky empty: midsummer is running on schedule.

rows.en: The agapanthus open for exactly this kind of sky, and they got it.
rows.text: Die agapante gaan oop vir presies hierdie soort lug, en hulle het dit gekry.
rows.back: The agapanthus opens for exactly this kind of sky, and they got it.

rows.en: Not a cloud to slow the sun, and the whole garden is making the most of it.
rows.text: Nie een wolk om die son te vertraag nie, en die hele tuin maak die meeste daarvan.
rows.back: Not one cloud to slow the sun down, and the whole garden is making the most of it.

rows.en: Take your coffee outside. You deserve it.
rows.text: Vat jou koffie buitentoe. Jy verdien dit.
rows.back: Take your coffee outside. You deserve it.

rows.en: This is why we live in South Africa.
rows.text: Dis hoekom ons in Suid-Afrika bly.
rows.back: This is why we live in South Africa.

rows.en: Take a moment. Look up. You're welcome.
rows.text: Neem 'n oomblik. Kyk op. Plesier.
rows.back: Take a moment. Look up. You're welcome.

rows.en: The sky has gone that deep blue you only get this high above sea level.
rows.text: Die lug het daardie diep blou geword wat jy net so hoog bo seespieël kry.
rows.back: The sky has gone that deep blue you only get this high above sea level.

rows.en: Blue sky, warm breeze. The simple stuff.
rows.text: Blou lug, warm briesie. Die eenvoudige goed.
rows.back: Blue sky, warm breeze. The simple things.

rows.en: The kind of sky that makes you grateful for free things.
rows.text: Die soort lug wat jou dankbaar laat voel vir gratis goed.
rows.back: The kind of sky that makes you feel grateful for free stuff.

rows.en: The kind of sun that turns one tennis ball into a whole afternoon.
rows.text: Die soort son wat een tennisbal in 'n hele middag verander.
rows.back: The kind of sun that turns one tennis ball into a whole afternoon.

rows.en: That farmhouse has seen a few centuries of days like this and still gets them free.
rows.text: Daardie plaashuis het al 'n paar eeue se dae soos dié gesien en kry hulle steeds verniet.
rows.back: That farmhouse has seen a few centuries' worth of days like this and still gets them for free.

rows.en: Full sun, soft lawn, and homework has officially lost its audience.
rows.text: Vol son, sagte gras, en huiswerk het amptelik sy gehoor verloor.
rows.back: Full sun, soft grass, and homework has officially lost its audience.

rows.en: Today's forecast: medium rare.
rows.text: Vandag se voorspelling: medium gaar.
rows.back: Today's forecast: medium done.
rows.reason: 'medium gaar' is medium rather than medium rare; joke intact.

rows.en: The deck reached golden-retriever temperature about an hour ago.
rows.text: Die dek het omtrent 'n uur gelede golden retriever-temperatuur bereik.
rows.back: The deck hit golden-retriever temperature about an hour ago.

rows.en: The sun has been on those boards since morning and the dog is doing the audit.
rows.text: Die son lê al van vanoggend af op daardie planke, en die hond doen die oudit.
rows.back: The sun has been lying on those planks since this morning, and the dog is doing the audit.

rows.en: Thursday's forecast, as read by the dog: warm boards until further notice.
rows.text: Donderdag se voorspelling, soos die hond dit lees: warm planke tot verdere kennisgewing.
rows.back: Thursday's forecast, as the dog reads it: warm planks until further notice.

rows.en: Postcard weather. You're welcome.
rows.text: Poskaart weer. Plesier.
rows.back: Postcard weather. You're welcome.

rows.en: Your vitamin D levels are thanking you.
rows.text: Jou vitamien D-vlakke bedank jou.
rows.back: Your vitamin D levels thank you.

rows.en: Air this clear should come with a warning: plans will be made.
rows.text: Lug so skoon, jy kan amper tot môre toe sien.
rows.back: Sky so clear you can almost see all the way to tomorrow.
rows.reason: EN joke is 'should come with a warning: plans will be made'; AF says 'you can almost see all the way to tomorrow' - a different joke, looks keyed to another line.
reasons: MISMATCH: EN joke is 'should come with a warning: plans will be made'; AF says 'you can almost see all the way to tomorrow' - a different joke, looks keyed to another line.

rows.en: The sky checked in at seven, went nowhere all day, and is staying for the weekend.
rows.text: Die lug het sewe-uur ingeboek, die hele dag nêrens heen gegaan nie, en bly vir die naweek.
rows.back: The sky checked in at seven, went nowhere all day, and is staying for the weekend.

rows.en: The pool is that blue because the sky is doing all of it.
rows.text: Die swembad is so blou omdat die lug al die werk doen.
rows.back: The pool is that blue because the sky is doing all the work.

rows.en: The braai is the social calendar. Show up.
rows.text: Die braai is die sosiale kalender. Daag op.
rows.back: The braai is the social calendar. Pitch up.

rows.en: Your only responsibility is choosing charcoal or wood.
rows.text: Jou enigste verantwoordelikheid is kies houtskool of hout.
rows.back: Your only responsibility is choosing charcoal or wood.

rows.en: Wors on, sun low, wind nowhere: Saturday is doing everything right.
rows.text: Wors op, son laag, wind nêrens: Saterdag doen alles reg.
rows.back: Wors on, sun low, wind nowhere: Saturday is doing everything right.

rows.en: The smoke is going straight up, which is the sky's way of approving a braai.
rows.text: Die rook gaan reguit op, en dis die lug se manier om 'n braai goed te keur.
rows.back: The smoke is going straight up, and that's the sky's way of approving a braai.

rows.en: Beach or braai? Yes.
rows.text: Strand of braai? Ja.
rows.back: Beach or braai? Yes.

rows.en: The sea has gone the colour it only goes when the sky is this empty.
rows.text: Die see het die kleur gekry wat hy net kry as die lug só leeg is.
rows.back: The sea has turned the colour it only gets when the sky is this empty.

rows.en: Sunday, and the sky has cleared its whole diary for this.
rows.text: Sondag, en die lug het sy hele dagboek hiervoor skoongemaak.
rows.back: Sunday, and the sky cleared its whole diary for this.

rows.en: The sky's on mute. Nobody's complaining.
rows.text: Die lug is op mute. Niemand kla nie.
rows.back: The sky is on mute. Nobody's complaining.

rows.en: Grey vibes. The sky matched my Monday.
rows.text: Grys vibes. Die lug pas by my Maandag.
rows.back: Grey vibes. The sky matches my Monday.

rows.en: Grey sky, flat sea, visible breath: the exact morning the fish expect them.
rows.text: Grys lug, plat see, sigbare asem: presies die oggend wat die visse hulle verwag.
rows.back: Grey sky, flat sea, visible breath: exactly the morning the fish expect them.
rows.note: unsure/garbled: 'wat die visse hulle verwag' - 'the fish expect them' (the anglers?); the 'hulle' is odd

rows.en: The cloud is sitting right on the mountains and the sea has gone pewter.
rows.text: Die wolke sit reg op die berge, en die see het tingrys geword.
rows.back: The clouds are sitting right on the mountains, and the sea has gone tin-grey.

rows.en: No wind on the water this morning, which is worth more than sunshine out there.
rows.text: Geen wind op die water vanoggend nie, en dit is daar buite meer werd as sonskyn.
rows.back: No wind on the water this morning, and out there that's worth more than sunshine.

rows.en: The sun sent an out-of-office reply.
rows.text: Die son het 'n out-of-office gestuur.
rows.back: The sun sent an out-of-office.

rows.en: The sky's curtains are drawn. Privacy, please.
rows.text: Die hemel se gordyne is toe. Privaatheid, asseblief.
rows.back: Heaven's curtains are closed. Privacy, please.

rows.en: Flat grey light, no glare, no wind: perfect painting weather, and he knows it.
rows.text: Plat grys lig, geen glans, geen wind: perfekte verfweer, en hy weet dit.
rows.back: Flat grey light, no glare, no wind: perfect painting weather, and he knows it.

rows.en: An overcast sky is a painter's softbox — not one hard shadow on that wall.
rows.text: 'n Bewolkte lug is 'n skilder se softbox — nie een harde skaduwee op daardie muur nie.
rows.back: An overcast sky is a painter's softbox - not one hard shadow on that wall.

rows.en: The cloud came in overnight and parked; nothing under it is in a hurry.
rows.text: Die wolk het oornag ingekom en geparkeer; niks daaronder is haastig nie.
rows.back: The cloud came in overnight and parked; nothing underneath it is in a hurry.

rows.en: Not Instagram weather. Not the end of the world.
rows.text: Nie troufoto weer nie. Nie die einde van die wêreld nie.
rows.back: Not wedding-photo weather. Not the end of the world.
rows.reason: EN 'Not Instagram weather' became 'Nie troufoto weer nie' (not wedding-photo weather), introducing a wedding the English doesn't have.
reasons: DRIFT: EN 'Not Instagram weather' became 'Nie troufoto weer nie' (not wedding-photo weather), introducing a wedding the English doesn't have.

rows.en: Clouds rolling in like family — no phone call first.
rows.text: Wolke rol in soos familie — sonder om eers te bel.
rows.back: Clouds roll in like family - without even phoning first.

rows.en: The sky brought its full weight this morning and the sea rose to meet it.
rows.text: Die lug het vanoggend sy volle gewig gebring, en die see het opgestaan om hom te ontmoet.
rows.back: The sky brought its full weight this morning, and the sea got up to meet it.

rows.en: One thin line of light at the horizon, and the whole sky leaning on it.
rows.text: Een dun streep lig op die horison, en die hele lug leun daarop.
rows.back: One thin strip of light on the horizon, and the whole sky is leaning on it.

rows.en: Running weather, honestly: cool, grey, and the sea doing the soundtrack.
rows.text: Drafweer, eerlikwaar: koel, grys, en die see doen die klankbaan.
rows.back: Running weather, honestly: cool, grey, and the sea is doing the soundtrack.

rows.en: Could be worse. Could also be better.
rows.text: Kon erger gewees het. Kon ook beter gewees het.
rows.back: Could have been worse. Could also have been better.

rows.en: The sun hit snooze again. Honestly? Same.
rows.text: Die son het snooze gedruk. Weer.
rows.back: The sun hit snooze. Again.
rows.reason: EN relatable punchline 'Honestly? Same.' is dropped; AF stops at 'Weer.' (Again).
reasons: DRIFT: EN relatable punchline 'Honestly? Same.' is dropped; AF stops at 'Weer.' (Again).

rows.en: The sun is trying its luck at the horizon and the cloud is unmoved.
rows.text: Die son probeer sy geluk op die horison, en die wolke is onbeïndruk.
rows.back: The sun is trying its luck on the horizon, and the clouds are unimpressed.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'onbeïndruk' — not found in any external source; closest attested: 'onbedruk' (0× hunspell, distance 2)

rows.en: The sea keeps its winter colour under a sky like this, whatever the calendar says.
rows.text: Die see hou sy winterkleur onder so 'n lug, wat die kalender ook al sê.
rows.back: The sea keeps its winter colour under a sky like this, whatever the calendar says.

rows.en: A grey start on the coast usually burns off by ten. Usually.
rows.text: 'n Grys begin aan die kus brand gewoonlik teen tienuur af. Gewoonlik.
rows.back: A grey start on the coast usually burns off by ten. Usually.

rows.en: The sun's on a tea break. No ETA.
rows.text: Die son is op teebreek. Geen ETA nie.
rows.back: The sun is on tea break. No ETA.

rows.en: At least it's not raining. That's the bar.
rows.text: Ten minste reën dit nie. Dis die standaard.
rows.back: At least it's not raining. That's the bar.

rows.en: That mug is steaming because Joburg mornings under cloud start at about four degrees.
rows.text: Daardie beker stoom, want in Joburg begin bewolkte oggende by omtrent vier grade.
rows.back: That mug is steaming, because in Joburg cloudy mornings start at about four degrees.

rows.en: The cloud kept the frost off the windscreens, which is the one favour it does.
rows.text: Die wolke het die ryp van die voorruite afgehou, en dis die een guns wat hulle doen.
rows.back: The clouds kept the frost off the windscreens, and that's the one favour they do.

rows.en: Pink-grey sky over the robots: winter is on the morning shift too.
rows.text: Pienkgrys lug oor die robotte: die winter werk ook die oggendskof.
rows.back: Pinkish-grey sky over the robots: winter works the morning shift too.

rows.en: Not bad, not great. Like a 6/10 date.
rows.text: Nie sleg nie, nie great nie. Soos 'n 6/10 date.
rows.back: Not bad, not great. Like a 6/10 date.

rows.en: The sun is up there somewhere behind three layers of Saturday-morning grey.
rows.text: Die son is êrens daarbo, agter drie lae Saterdagoggend-grys.
rows.back: The sun is somewhere up there, behind three layers of Saturday-morning grey.

rows.en: The Bo-Kaap does the colour this morning because the sky refuses to.
rows.text: Die Bo-Kaap sorg vanoggend vir die kleur, want die lug weier.
rows.back: The Bo-Kaap is supplying the colour this morning, because the sky refuses to.

rows.en: Cool, grey and windless — honestly the best running weather this city sells.
rows.text: Koel, grys en windstil — eerlikwaar die beste drafweer wat hierdie stad verkoop.
rows.back: Cool, grey and windless - honestly the best running weather this city sells.

rows.en: The app says cloudy. Aunty's knee says rain. We trust the knee.
rows.text: Die app sê bewolk. Tannie se knie sê reën. Ons vertrou die knie.
rows.back: The app says cloudy. Tannie's knee says rain. We trust the knee.

rows.en: The whole city is under one grey blanket and somebody just noticed.
rows.text: Die hele stad is onder een grys kombers, en iemand het dit pas agtergekom.
rows.back: The whole city is under one grey blanket, and someone has only just noticed.

rows.en: A lid like that takes until about eleven to lift, if it lifts at all.
rows.text: 'n Deksel soos daardie lig eers teen elfuur, as dit enigsins lig.
rows.back: A lid like that only lifts around eleven, if it lifts at all.

rows.en: The sky is buffering.
rows.text: Die lug hakkel.
rows.back: The sky is stuttering.
rows.reason: 'buffering' rebuilt as 'hakkel' (stuttering) - different image, same stop-start sky.

rows.en: The sky is the colour of an old Tupperware lid.
rows.text: Die lug is die kleur van 'n ou Tupperware-deksel.
rows.back: The sky is the colour of an old Tupperware lid.

rows.en: The sun's on airplane mode.
rows.text: Die son is op airplane mode.
rows.back: The sun is on airplane mode.

rows.en: Forecast says maybe. We say probably.
rows.text: Voorspelling sê miskien. Ons sê waarskynlik.
rows.back: Forecast says maybe. We say probably.

rows.en: Half the sky has an opinion and the other half is about to hear it.
rows.text: Die helfte van die lug het 'n mening, en die ander helfte gaan dit nou-nou hoor.
rows.back: Half the sky has an opinion, and the other half is about to hear it.

rows.en: The week's weather is changing hands right there, in one straight line.
rows.text: Die week se weer ruil net daar van hande, in een reguit lyn.
rows.back: The week's weather is changing hands right there, in one straight line.

rows.en: Blue on the left, business on the right, and the line is moving your way.
rows.text: Blou links, ernstige besigheid regs, en die lyn skuif na jou kant toe.
rows.back: Blue on the left, serious business on the right, and the line is moving your way.

rows.en: Even the weather can't be bothered today.
rows.text: Selfs die weer kan nie gepla wees vandag nie.
rows.back: Even the weather can't be bothered today.

rows.en: The sky's giving 'I'll try again tomorrow' energy.
rows.text: Die lug gee 'ek probeer weer môre' energie.
rows.back: The sky is giving 'I'll try again tomorrow' energy.

rows.en: Perfect weather for existing without enthusiasm.
rows.text: Perfekte weer vir bestaan sonder entoesiasme.
rows.back: Perfect weather for existing without enthusiasm.

rows.en: A grey day reads the same in any language: blanket, stoep, minimal ambition.
rows.text: 'n Grys dag lees dieselfde in enige taal: kombers, stoep, minimale ambisie.
rows.back: A grey day reads the same in any language: blanket, stoep, minimal ambition.

rows.en: The concrete is still damp and the sky looks like it isn't finished.
rows.text: Die beton is nog klam, en die lug lyk nie of hy klaar is nie.
rows.back: The concrete is still damp, and the sky doesn't look like it's finished.

rows.en: Under a sky like this the whole garden runs at half-speed, dog included.
rows.text: Onder so 'n lug werk die hele tuin teen halwe spoed, die hond ingesluit.
rows.back: Under a sky like this the whole garden works at half speed, dog included.

rows.en: The sun's bunking today.
rows.text: Die son speel siek vandag.
rows.back: The sun is bunking today.
rows.note: 'speel siek' = playing sick / pulling a sickie

rows.en: The clouds are here but they're not doing anything.
rows.text: Die wolke is hier maar hulle doen niks.
rows.back: The clouds are here but they're not doing anything.

rows.en: Flat grey over the rugby field: perfect kicking weather, no wind to blame.
rows.text: Plat grys oor die rugbyveld: perfekte skopweer, geen wind om te blameer nie.
rows.back: Flat grey over the rugby field: perfect kicking weather, no wind to blame.

rows.en: The sky has gone the colour of the staff-room ceiling and settled in.
rows.text: Die lug het die kleur van die personeelkamer se plafon gekry en maak hom tuis.
rows.back: The sky has gone the colour of the staffroom ceiling and is making itself at home.

rows.en: A perfectly average sky doing perfectly average things.
rows.text: 'n Doodgewone lug wat doodgewone dinge doen.
rows.back: A dead-ordinary sky doing dead-ordinary things.

rows.en: Take a brolly just in case, hey.
rows.text: Vat n sambreel net vir ingeval, ne.
rows.back: Take an umbrella just in case, hey.
rows.reason: typo: 'n without apostrophe.

rows.en: 50/50 on getting wet. Like a coin toss.
rows.text: 50/50 kans om nat te word. Better odds as om die Lotto te wen...
rows.back: 50/50 chance of getting wet. Better odds than winning the Lotto...
rows.reason: EN punchline 'Like a coin toss' replaced by 'Better odds as om die Lotto te wen' - different gag (reads like another variant) with a half-English phrase.
reasons: DRIFT: EN punchline 'Like a coin toss' replaced by 'Better odds as om die Lotto te wen' - different gag (reads like another variant) with a half-English phrase.

rows.en: Pack an umbrella. Or don't. We don't know either.
rows.text: Pak 'n sambreel. Of moenie. Ons weet ook nie.
rows.back: Pack an umbrella. Or don't. We don't know either.

rows.en: Umbrella in one hand, sunglasses in the other — he has met this sky before.
rows.text: Sambreel in die een hand, sonbril in die ander — hy het hierdie lug al ontmoet.
rows.back: Umbrella in one hand, sunglasses in the other - he's met this sky before.

rows.en: That sky refuses to commit, so he came prepared for both of its moods.
rows.text: Daardie lug weier om kleur te beken, so hy het vir albei sy buie voorberei gekom.
rows.back: That sky won't show its colours, so he came prepared for both its moods.

rows.en: Bring a jacket. Or sunscreen. Or both.
rows.text: Bring 'n baadjie. Of sonroom. Of albei.
rows.back: Bring a jacket. Or sunscreen. Or both.

rows.en: Grey is also a colour, says my ma. Today I believe her.
rows.text: Grys is ook 'n kleur, sê my ma. Vandag glo ek haar.
rows.back: Grey is also a colour, my mom says. Today I believe her.

rows.en: The sun is technically present. Spiritually elsewhere.
rows.text: Die son is tegnies hier. Geestelik elders.
rows.back: The sun is technically here. Mentally elsewhere.

rows.en: This weather has 'meh' written all over it.
rows.text: Hierdie weer het 'n 'meh' houding.
rows.back: This weather has a 'meh' attitude.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'meh' is an English word with no af attestation and is not in the English source line

rows.en: The one animal that can match the sky's mood is having no trouble today.
rows.text: Die een dier wat by die lug se bui kan pas, het vandag geen moeite nie.
rows.back: The one animal that can match the sky's mood is having no trouble today.
rows.note: unsure: which animal and what the joke is - 'geen moeite nie' = no trouble/effort

rows.en: Every leaf is holding still; the whole garden is waiting to see what the sky decides.
rows.text: Elke blaar hou stil; die hele tuin wag om te sien wat die lug besluit.
rows.back: Every leaf is holding still; the whole garden is waiting to see what the sky decides.

rows.en: Weather's being more indecisive than you at Spur.
rows.text: Die weer is meer besluiteloos as jy by Spur.
rows.back: The weather is more indecisive than you at Spur.

rows.en: Some clouds. Some sun. South African summer admin.
rows.text: Sonnig met n spatsel wolke. SA somer in een prentjie.
rows.back: Sunny with a sprinkle of clouds. SA summer in one picture.
rows.reason: EN 'South African summer admin' punchline lost; AF 'SA somer in een prentjie' (SA summer in one picture) is a different, flatter close; also 'n typo.
reasons: DRIFT: EN 'South African summer admin' punchline lost; AF 'SA somer in een prentjie' (SA summer in one picture) is a different, flatter close; also 'n typo.

rows.en: Half a lawn mowed, and now the negotiation with the sky begins.
rows.text: Die halwe grasperk gesny, en nou begin die onderhandeling met die lug.
rows.back: Half the lawn mowed, and now the negotiations with the sky begin.

rows.en: The sky is deciding whether the second half of that lawn happens today.
rows.text: Die lug besluit of die tweede helfte van daardie grasperk vandag gebeur.
rows.back: The sky is deciding whether the second half of that lawn happens today.

rows.en: That look is a man asking the clouds for forty-five more minutes.
rows.text: Daardie kyk is 'n man wat die wolke vir nog vyf-en-veertig minute vra.
rows.back: That look is a man asking the clouds for another forty-five minutes.

rows.en: The chops don't know it's cloudy. The braai proceeds.
rows.text: Die tjops weet nie dis bewolk nie. Die braai gaan voort.
rows.back: The chops don't know it's cloudy. The braai goes on.

rows.en: Cloudy enough to comment, sunny enough to ignore.
rows.text: Bewolk genoeg om te kla, sonnig genoeg om jou te maak hoop.
rows.back: Cloudy enough to complain, sunny enough to make you hope.
rows.reason: EN 'sunny enough to ignore' became 'sonnig genoeg om jou te maak hoop' (sunny enough to make you hope) - second half of the claim changed.
reasons: DRIFT: EN 'sunny enough to ignore' became 'sonnig genoeg om jou te maak hoop' (sunny enough to make you hope) - second half of the claim changed.

rows.en: That sky can do what it wants; the wors is already on.
rows.text: Daardie lug kan doen wat hy wil; die wors is klaar op die vuur.
rows.back: That sky can do what it likes; the wors is already on the fire.

rows.en: The sky is threatening, the firelighters are answering: a very South African standoff.
rows.text: Die lug dreig, die aanmaakblokkies antwoord: 'n baie Suid-Afrikaanse kragmeting.
rows.back: The sky threatens, the firelighters answer: a very South African trial of strength.

rows.en: Paving wet, clouds low, fire going anyway — this braai has been through worse.
rows.text: Plaveisel nat, wolke laag, vuur brand in elk geval — hierdie braai het al erger oorleef.
rows.back: Paving wet, clouds low, fire burning anyway - this braai has survived worse.

rows.en: Not rain. Just atmosphere with opinions.
rows.text: Nie reën nie. Net atmosfeer met menings.
rows.back: Not rain. Just atmosphere with opinions.

rows.en: The sky’s overdressed. The weather’s still fine.
rows.text: Die lug het te veel aangetrek. Die weer is nog heeltemal reg.
rows.back: The sky has overdressed. The weather is still perfectly fine.

rows.en: The sky saved its best ten minutes for the top of the climb.
rows.text: Die lug het sy beste tien minute vir bo-op die klim gehou.
rows.back: The sky saved its best ten minutes for the top of the climb.

rows.en: Cloud all afternoon, and now this — the sky apologising in gold.
rows.text: Die hele middag wolke, en nou dít — die lug wat in goud om verskoning vra.
rows.back: Clouds all afternoon, and now this - the sky apologising in gold.

rows.en: That gap in the cloud is worth more than the whole clear day it replaced.
rows.text: Daardie gaping in die wolke is meer werd as die hele skoon dag wat dit vervang het.
rows.back: That gap in the clouds is worth more than the whole clear day it replaced.

rows.en: The sky can’t decide between golden hour and going home early. Neither can anyone else.
rows.text: Die lug kan nie tussen golden hour en vroeg huis toe gaan besluit nie. Niemand anders ook nie.
rows.back: The sky can't decide between golden hour and going home early. Neither can anyone else.

rows.en: The sun clocked out without saying bye. Rude, but relatable.
rows.text: Die son het uitgeklok sonder om te groet. Onbeskof, maar relatable.
rows.back: The sun clocked out without saying goodbye. Rude, but relatable.

rows.en: The dog is wearing a jersey, which is all the forecast anybody here needs.
rows.text: Die hond dra 'n trui, en dis al die voorspelling wat enigiemand hier nodig het.
rows.back: The dog is wearing a jersey, and that's all the forecast anyone here needs.

rows.en: Grey sky, grey jersey: the whole stoep is colour-coordinated with the weather.
rows.text: Grys lug, grys trui: die hele stoep pas by die weer.
rows.back: Grey sky, grey jersey: the whole stoep matches the weather.

rows.en: The day never warmed up, and one resident has stopped waiting for it to.
rows.text: Die dag het nooit warm geword nie, en een inwoner het opgehou wag.
rows.back: The day never warmed up, and one resident stopped waiting.

rows.en: Cloudy dusk. Pretty, not promising.
rows.text: Bewolkte skemer. Mooi, maar belowe niks.
rows.back: Cloudy dusk. Pretty, but promises nothing.

rows.en: The sky did extras. The forecast didn’t.
rows.text: Die lug het ekstra gedoen. Die voorspelling nie.
rows.back: The sky went extra. The forecast didn't.

rows.en: The sky left a two-finger gap for the sunset and the sunset took it.
rows.text: Die wolke het twee vingers plek gelos, en die sonsondergang het dit gevat.
rows.back: The clouds left two fingers of space, and the sunset took it.

rows.en: All that cloud, and the sun still found the letterbox at the bottom.
rows.text: Al daardie wolke, en die son het steeds die briewebus onderaan gekry.
rows.back: All those clouds, and the sun still got the postbox at the bottom.
rows.note: unsure: 'onderaan' - at the bottom of what (the street, the frame)?

rows.en: The suburb is going to bed under a lid, with one orange nightlight left on.
rows.text: Die voorstad gaan slaap onder 'n deksel, met een oranje naglampie wat nog brand.
rows.back: The suburb goes to sleep under a lid, with one orange nightlight still on.

rows.en: Cloud cover. The night shift starts early.
rows.text: Wolkdek. Die nagskof begin vroeg.
rows.back: Cloud cover. The night shift starts early.

rows.en: Cloudy. Stay in if you were looking for a reason.
rows.text: Bewolk. Bly binne as jy 'n rede gesoek het.
rows.back: Cloudy. Stay inside if you were looking for a reason.

rows.en: The clouds took the sunset and left the suburb the pink change.
rows.text: Die wolke het die sonsondergang gevat en die voorstad die pienk kleingeld gelos.
rows.back: The clouds took the sunset and left the suburb the pink small change.

rows.en: The aerials have the best view of a sky doing its quiet closing number.
rows.text: Die antennas het die beste uitsig op 'n lug wat sy stil slotnommer doen.
rows.back: The antennas have the best view of a sky doing its quiet closing number.

rows.en: A grey dusk brings the evening forward, and the windows have already agreed.
rows.text: 'n Grys skemer bring die aand vroeër, en die vensters stem klaar saam.
rows.back: A grey dusk brings the evening in earlier, and the windows already agree.

rows.en: Maybe rain, maybe not. Classic.
rows.text: Miskien reën, miskien nie. Klassiek.
rows.back: Maybe rain, maybe not. Classic.

rows.en: Rain? Possibly. Commitment? Never.
rows.text: Reën? Moontlik. Sal ek my lewe daar op wed? Nooit.
rows.back: Rain? Possibly. Would I bet my life on it? Never.
rows.reason: EN 'Commitment? Never.' (the sky won't commit) became 'Sal ek my lewe daar op wed? Nooit.' (would I bet my life on it) - different, longer gag.
reasons: DRIFT: EN 'Commitment? Never.' (the sky won't commit) became 'Sal ek my lewe daar op wed? Nooit.' (would I bet my life on it) - different, longer gag.

rows.en: Looks like the clouds are staying for supper.
rows.text: Die wolke bly oor vir aandete, lyk dit.
rows.back: The clouds are staying for supper, it looks like.

rows.en: The charcoal is out, the sky is undecided, and neither is backing down.
rows.text: Die houtskool is uit, die lug is onbeslis, en nie een gee kop nie.
rows.back: The charcoal is out, the sky is undecided, and neither one is giving in.
rows.note: unsure: 'gee kop' - 'kop gee' usually = give in/yield; could be read as 'neither cares'

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'lug' means 'air' — nothing in the English source; it is 1 letter from 'rug', the usual word for 'backing'

rows.en: That cloud has been rehearsing all afternoon and still hasn't said its line.
rows.text: Daardie wolk oefen al die hele middag en het nog steeds nie sy reël gesê nie.
rows.back: That cloud has been rehearsing all afternoon and still hasn't said its line.

rows.en: The horizon kept one strip of orange as proof the sun was here.
rows.text: Die horison het een strokie oranje behou as bewys dat die son hier was.
rows.back: The horizon kept one little strip of orange as proof the sun was here.

rows.en: Nobody's posting this sunset on Instagram.
rows.text: Niemand gaan hierdie sononder op Instagram sit nie.
rows.back: Nobody's going to put this sunset on Instagram.

rows.en: Don't trust those clouds. They're plotting.
rows.text: Moenie daai wolke vertrou nie. Hulle beplan.
rows.back: Don't trust those clouds. They're planning something.

rows.en: One person at this wedding is checking the sky, and she has been right before.
rows.text: Een persoon by hierdie troue hou die lug dop, en sy was al voorheen reg.
rows.back: One person at this wedding is watching the sky, and she's been right before.

rows.en: The clouds came dressed in pink for the occasion and are behaving so far.
rows.text: Die wolke het pienk aangetrek vir die geleentheid en gedra hulle tot dusver.
rows.back: The clouds dressed in pink for the occasion and have behaved so far.

rows.en: That sky will hold for the photographs — after that, no promises.
rows.text: Daardie lug sal hou vir die foto's — daarna, geen beloftes nie.
rows.back: That sky will hold for the photos - after that, no promises.

rows.en: Sky's doing the most, but only a little.
rows.text: Die lug wen, maar dis nie veel van n kompetisie nie.
rows.back: The sky wins, but it's not much of a competition.
rows.reason: EN 'Sky's doing the most, but only a little' (extra, but barely); AF 'Die lug wen, maar dis nie veel van n kompetisie nie' (the sky wins, not much of a competition) is a different joke - looks keyed to another line; also 'n typo.
reasons: MISMATCH: EN 'Sky's doing the most, but only a little' (extra, but barely); AF 'Die lug wen, maar dis nie veel van n kompetisie nie' (the sky wins, not much of a competition) is a different joke - looks keyed to another line; also 'n typo.

rows.en: Cloud is what a sunset needs, and tonight the sky brought exactly enough.
rows.text: Wolke is wat 'n sonsondergang nodig het, en vanaand het die lug presies genoeg gebring.
rows.back: Clouds are what a sunset needs, and tonight the sky brought exactly enough.

rows.en: Table Mountain gets the silhouette; the clouds get the whole colour budget.
rows.text: Tafelberg kry die silhoeët; die wolke kry die hele kleurbegroting.
rows.back: Table Mountain gets the silhouette; the clouds get the whole colour budget.

rows.en: Red sky at night, shepherd's delight — tomorrow just got a good reference.
rows.text: Rooi lug saans, mooi weer môre — môre het pas 'n goeie verwysing gekry.
rows.back: Red sky at night, fine weather tomorrow - tomorrow just got a good reference.

rows.en: The moon has hung out a do-not-disturb sign.
rows.text: Die maan het 'n 'moenie steur nie'-bordjie opgehang.
rows.back: The moon has hung up a 'do not disturb' sign.

findings: MEDIUM morphology: negation 'moenie' without the closing 'nie' at the end of the clause

rows.en: The moon is down to one small window and it is using all of it.
rows.text: Die maan is af tot een klein venster, en hy gebruik dit alles.
rows.back: The moon is down to one small window, and he's using all of it.

rows.en: The clouds are winning tonight, about nine rounds to one.
rows.text: Die wolke wen vanaand, omtrent nege rondtes teen een.
rows.back: The clouds are winning tonight, about nine rounds to one.

rows.en: A sky like that keeps the heat in — the frost can stand down tonight.
rows.text: 'n Lug soos daardie hou die warmte in — die ryp is vanaand van diens onthef.
rows.back: A sky like that holds the warmth in - the frost is relieved of duty tonight.

rows.en: Night-shift clouds: just keeping the place warm till the sun gets back.
rows.text: Nagskof-wolke: hulle hou net die plek warm tot die son terug is.
rows.back: Night-shift clouds: they're just keeping the place warm till the sun's back.

rows.en: The moon has enough cloud to fight through that the torch got the job.
rows.text: Die maan het soveel wolke om deur te veg dat die flits die werk gekry het.
rows.back: The moon has so many clouds to fight through that the torch got the job.

rows.en: Cloud like fish scales means the weather is thinking about changing its mind.
rows.text: Wolke soos visskubbe beteken die weer dink daaraan om van plan te verander.
rows.back: Clouds like fish scales mean the weather is thinking of changing its mind.

rows.en: That cloud is just thick enough to make the moon count for nothing on the ground.
rows.text: Daardie wolk is net dik genoeg om die maan op die grond niks te laat tel nie.
rows.back: That cloud is just thick enough to make the moon count for nothing on the ground.

rows.en: Cloudy night. Nobody’s going out, officially.
rows.text: Bewolkte nag. Niemand gaan uit nie, amptelik.
rows.back: Cloudy night. Nobody's going out, officially.

rows.en: The weather chose indoors. Correctly.
rows.text: Die weer het binne gekies. Heeltemal reg ook.
rows.back: The weather chose indoors. Quite right too.

rows.en: Cloud right down to the rooftops, and every sensible mammal is indoors under a lamp.
rows.text: Wolke tot op die dakke, en elke verstandige soogdier is binne onder 'n lamp.
rows.back: Clouds down to the rooftops, and every sensible mammal is inside under a lamp.

rows.en: Nothing is falling and nothing is shining; it is that kind of night.
rows.text: Niks val nie en niks skyn nie; dis daai soort nag.
rows.back: Nothing's falling and nothing's shining; it's that kind of night.

rows.en: A sky with no stars is the sky's way of saying go to bed.
rows.text: 'n Lug sonder sterre is die lug se manier om te sê gaan slaap.
rows.back: A sky without stars is the sky's way of saying go to sleep.

rows.en: No stars tonight, but the neighbourhood dogs still have opinions.
rows.text: Geen sterre nie, maar die buurt se honde het steeds opinies.
rows.back: No stars, but the neighbourhood dogs still have opinions.

rows.en: The cloud is coming over the mountain like it pays rent here.
rows.text: Die wolk kom oor die berg asof hy hier huur betaal.
rows.back: The cloud comes over the mountain like it pays rent here.

rows.en: That cloud will be down on the streetlights before the walk is done.
rows.text: Daardie wolk sal op die straatligte sit voor die stap verby is.
rows.back: That cloud will be sitting on the streetlights before the walk is done.

rows.en: Low cloud at night keeps the cold off the promenade, and the regulars know it.
rows.text: Lae wolke in die nag hou die koue van die promenade af, en die gereelde stappers weet dit.
rows.back: Low cloud at night keeps the cold off the promenade, and the regular walkers know it.

rows.en: Night clouds are the sky's way of saying: let's talk tomorrow.
rows.text: Nagwolke is die hemel se manier van sê: ons praat môre weer.
rows.back: Night clouds are heaven's way of saying: we'll talk again tomorrow.

rows.en: No moon, no stars, no streetlights: tonight the headlights are the whole sky.
rows.text: Geen maan, geen sterre, geen straatligte nie: vanaand is die kopligte die hele lug.
rows.back: No moon, no stars, no streetlights: tonight the headlights are the whole sky.

rows.en: The sky has switched itself off for the night; the bakkie disagrees.
rows.text: Die lug het homself vir die nag afgeskakel; die bakkie stem nie saam nie.
rows.back: The sky switched itself off for the night; the bakkie disagrees.

rows.en: Overcast this thick turns the Karoo into a corridor, and he is halfway down it.
rows.text: Wolke só dik maak van die Karoo 'n gang, en hy is halfpad daarin af.
rows.back: Clouds this thick turn the Karoo into a corridor, and he's halfway down it.

rows.en: Cloudy night. Bravery in blanket form.
rows.text: Bewolkte nag. Dapperheid in kombersvorm.
rows.back: Cloudy night. Courage in blanket form.
rows.note: unsure: joke unclear - 'dapperheid in kombersvorm' = bravery in the shape of a blanket

rows.en: The sky closed. The evening didn’t.
rows.text: Die lug het toegemaak. Die aand nie.
rows.back: The sky closed up. The evening didn't.

rows.en: The sky brought nothing tonight, so the lantern is carrying the whole evening.
rows.text: Die lug het vanaand niks gebring nie, so die lantern dra die hele aand.
rows.back: The sky brought nothing tonight, so the lantern is carrying the whole evening.

rows.en: Blankets outside in the dark: the evening is cold, the company is not.
rows.text: Komberse buite in die donker: die aand is koud, die geselskap nie.
rows.back: Blankets outside in the dark: the evening is cold, the company isn't.

rows.en: Not one star made it through that lid, and nobody has noticed yet.
rows.text: Nie een ster het deur daardie deksel gekom nie, en niemand het dit nog agtergekom nie.
rows.back: Not one star made it through that lid, and nobody's noticed yet.

rows.en: The sky put the stars on silent. They're still up there, promise.
rows.text: Die hemel het die sterre op stil gesit. Hulle is nog daar, belowe.
rows.back: Heaven put the stars on silent. They're still there, promise.

rows.en: The cloud is holding the city's glow like a lampshade tonight.
rows.text: Die wolke hou vanaand die stad se gloed vas soos 'n lampskerm.
rows.back: The clouds are holding the city's glow tonight like a lampshade.

rows.en: No stars on offer tonight, so the city is providing its own.
rows.text: Geen sterre vanaand op die spyskaart nie, so die stad voorsien sy eie.
rows.back: No stars on the menu tonight, so the city is supplying its own.

rows.en: Schrodinger's rain. It both is and isn't.
rows.text: Schrödinger se reën. Dit is én is nie.
rows.back: Schrödinger's rain. It is and it isn't.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'Schrödinger' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source

rows.en: Even the weather apps are arguing about this one.
rows.text: Selfs die weer-apps baklei oor hierdie een.
rows.back: Even the weather apps are fighting over this one.

rows.en: Half this street is in summer and the other half is about to be somewhere else.
rows.text: Die helfte van hierdie straat is in die somer, en die ander helfte gaan nou-nou êrens anders wees.
rows.back: Half this street is in summer, and the other half is about to be somewhere else.

rows.en: That cloud line is moving in with the confidence of a Monday.
rows.text: Daardie wolklyn skuif in met die selfvertroue van 'n Maandag.
rows.back: That cloud line is moving in with the confidence of a Monday.

rows.en: The blue half of the sky is on borrowed time and the lawns know it.
rows.text: Die blou helfte van die lug leef op geleende tyd, en die grasperke weet dit.
rows.back: The blue half of the sky is living on borrowed time, and the lawns know it.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'leef' means 'to live; live' — nothing in the English source; it is 1 letter from 'leen', the usual word for 'borrowed'

rows.en: Eskom-friendly weather. No solar today.
rows.text: Eskom-vriendelike weer. Geen solar vandag nie.
rows.back: Eskom-friendly weather. No solar today.

rows.en: Sun's playing peek-a-boo.
rows.text: Son speel wegkruipertjie.
rows.back: Sun's playing hide-and-seek.

rows.en: Sun on a smoke break.
rows.text: Son is op tjailatyd.
rows.back: Sun's on smoke break.
rows.note: 'tjailatyd' = knock-off/break time; read here as a smoke/work break

rows.en: Panels installed, sun absent: the sky owes this roof an apology.
rows.text: Panele geïnstalleer, son afwesig: die lug skuld hierdie dak 'n verskoning.
rows.back: Panels installed, sun absent: the sky owes this roof an apology.

rows.en: Grey from gutter to gutter, and every kilowatt up here is on standby.
rows.text: Grys van geut tot geut, en elke kilowatt hier bo staan gereed vir niks.
rows.back: Grey from gutter to gutter, and every kilowatt up here is standing by for nothing.

rows.en: The forecast said partly sunny; the sky went with fully committed grey.
rows.text: Die voorspelling het gesê gedeeltelik sonnig; die lug het vir volle toewyding aan grys gekies.
rows.back: The forecast said partly sunny; the sky went for full commitment to grey.

rows.en: Cloud cover with a side of who-cares.
rows.text: Bewolk met n spatsel van wie-gee-om lug.
rows.back: Cloudy with a sprinkle of who-cares sky.
rows.reason: typo: 'n without apostrophe.

rows.en: The sky's giving mixed signals again.
rows.text: Die lug gee weer gemengde seine.
rows.back: The sky is giving mixed signals again.

rows.en: Sun, hide-and-seek champion of the day.
rows.text: Die lug speel kat en muis.
rows.back: The sky is playing cat and mouse.
rows.reason: EN 'Sun, hide-and-seek champion of the day'; AF 'Die lug speel kat en muis' switches subject to the sky, swaps the game and drops 'champion'.

wrongSource.en: Sky's doing the most, but only a little.

reasons: DRIFT: EN 'Sun, hide-and-seek champion of the day'; AF 'Die lug speel kat en muis' switches subject to the sky, swaps the game and drops 'champion'.
WRONG SOURCE? The back-translation is closer to another line of the same photograph: "Sky's doing the most, but only a little."

rows.en: The sun is down to one beam and the whole veld is watching where it lands.
rows.text: Die son is af tot een straal, en die hele veld kyk waar dit gaan land.
rows.back: The sun is down to one beam, and the whole veld is watching where it lands.

rows.en: The sheep bunched up an hour ago, which is the Karoo's own forecast.
rows.text: Die skape het 'n uur gelede saamgebondel, en dis die Karoo se eie voorspelling.
rows.back: The sheep bunched up an hour ago, and that's the Karoo's own forecast.

rows.en: That grey is thinking about rain and the whole district is thinking with it.
rows.text: Daardie grys dink aan reën, en die hele distrik dink saam.
rows.back: That grey is thinking about rain, and the whole district is thinking along with it.

rows.en: Clouds looking proper suspicious.
rows.text: Wolke lyk behoorlik verdag.
rows.back: The clouds look properly suspicious.

rows.en: The washing's on the line and you're feeling brave.
rows.text: Die wasgoed hang buite en jy voel dapper.
rows.back: The washing is hanging outside and you're feeling brave.

rows.en: Washing's still safe. Probably.
rows.text: Wasgoed is veilig. Hopelik.
rows.back: Washing is safe. Hopefully.
rows.reason: The brand hedge "Probably" became "Hopelik" (hopefully), and "still" is dropped; the canon uses "waarskynlik" for this hedge.
reasons: DRIFT: The brand hedge "Probably" became "Hopelik" (hopefully), and "still" is dropped; the canon uses "waarskynlik" for this hedge.

rows.en: That washing is a straight bet against that sky, and the sky looks confident.
rows.text: Daardie wasgoed is 'n reguit weddenskap teen daardie lug, en die lug lyk seker van sy saak.
rows.back: That washing is a straight bet against that sky, and the sky looks sure of itself.

rows.en: Not a breath moving those sheets, and nothing helpful coming from above either.
