rows.text: Nie 'n luggie wat daardie lakens roer nie, en van bo af kom ook geen hulp nie.
rows.back: Not a breath of air stirring those sheets, and no help coming from above either.
rows.note: unsure: 'van bo af kom ook geen hulp nie' - help from above = sun, or from the sky in general

rows.en: Grey like that can hold all day without dropping a thing — probably.
rows.text: Grys soos daardie kan die hele dag hou sonder om iets te laat val — waarskynlik.
rows.back: Grey like that can hold all day without dropping anything - probably.

rows.en: The sky can't make up its mind. Join the club.
rows.text: Die lug kan nie besluit nie. Tipies.
rows.back: The sky can't decide. Typical.
rows.reason: Punchline changed: the self-deprecating "Join the club" became "Tipies" (typical), which is exasperation instead of fellow feeling.
reasons: DRIFT: Punchline changed: the self-deprecating "Join the club" became "Tipies" (typical), which is exasperation instead of fellow feeling.

rows.en: The walk has been postponed by the committee upstairs, and the committee looks settled.
rows.text: Die stap is deur die komitee daarbo uitgestel, en die komitee lyk tevrede.
rows.back: The walk has been postponed by the committee up there, and the committee looks pleased.
rows.reason: "looks settled" became "lyk tevrede" (looks content), so the pun on settled weather is lost. The joke still holds.

rows.en: The sky is doing nothing in particular and being very thorough about it.
rows.text: Die lug doen niks besonders nie en is baie deeglik daaroor.
rows.back: The sky is doing nothing special and is being very thorough about it.

findings: MEDIUM morphology: negation 'niks' without the closing 'nie' at the end of the clause

rows.en: Good day for a walk, bad day for a tan.
rows.text: Goeie dag vir n stap, slegste dag vir n tan.
rows.back: Good day for a walk, worst day for a tan.
rows.reason: Same joke ("slegste" = worst for bad), but "n stap" and "n tan" are missing the apostrophe: write 'n.

rows.en: Sky can't make up its mind.
rows.text: Lug kan nie besluit wat dit wil wees nie.
rows.back: Sky can't decide what it wants to be.

rows.en: The cloud arrived about four minutes after the towel went down, which is policy.
rows.text: Die wolk het omtrent vier minute ná die handdoek neergesit is aangekom, en dis beleid.
rows.back: The cloud arrived about four minutes after the towel was put down, and that's policy.

rows.en: Sunscreen out, sun gone: the sky has a sense of humour today.
rows.text: Sonroom uit, son weg: die lug het vandag 'n sin vir humor.
rows.back: Sunscreen out, sun gone: the sky has a sense of humour today.

rows.en: The blue sky is still back there somewhere, but the grey has the floor.
rows.text: Die blou lug is nog êrens daaragter, maar die grys het die woord.
rows.back: The blue sky is still somewhere behind there, but the grey has the floor.
rows.note: 'het die woord' = has the floor / is doing the talking

rows.en: This weather needs a life coach.
rows.text: Hierdie weer het 'n lewensafrigter nodig.
rows.back: This weather needs a life coach.

rows.en: Durban grey is still twenty-four degrees, which is why the promenade never empties.
rows.text: Durban se grys is steeds vier-en-twintig grade, en dis hoekom die promenade nooit leeg raak nie.
rows.back: Durban's grey is still twenty-four degrees, and that's why the promenade never empties.

rows.en: The cloud is doing sunscreen duty this morning and the runners are cashing in.
rows.text: Die wolke doen vanoggend sonroomdiens, en die drawwers maak die meeste daarvan.
rows.back: The clouds are on sunscreen duty this morning, and the joggers are making the most of it.

rows.en: A pearl-grey sky and a warm sea breeze: the coast's version of mild.
rows.text: 'n Pêrelgrys lug en 'n warm seebries: die kus se weergawe van sag.
rows.back: A pearl-grey sky and a warm sea breeze: the coast's version of soft.

rows.en: The sun has arrived. It has not yet started working.
rows.text: Die son is op, maar hy werk nog nie.
rows.back: The sun is up, but he's not working yet.

rows.en: Welkom-cold today. The kind that goes through three jerseys like they aren't there.
rows.text: Welkom-koud vandag. Die soort wat deur drie truie gaan asof hulle nie daar is nie.
rows.back: Welkom-cold today. The kind that goes through three jerseys as if they aren't there.
rows.note: unsure: 'Welkom-koud' - the Free State town Welkom (Welkom-style cold) or a pun on 'welcome'

rows.en: Bin day, and the frost got to them before the truck did.
rows.text: Vullisdag, en die ryp was voor die trok daar.
rows.back: Rubbish day, and the frost got there before the truck.

rows.en: The municipality collects at seven; the frost delivered at four.
rows.text: Die munisipaliteit tel sewe-uur op; die ryp het vieruur afgelewer.
rows.back: The municipality collects at seven; the frost delivered at four.

rows.en: The lawn caught frost overnight. You're next.
rows.text: Die gras het ryp gevang. Jy is volgende.
rows.back: The grass caught frost. You're next.

rows.en: Somebody left the freezer door open overnight.
rows.text: Die Karoo het die verkoeler oopgelos.
rows.back: The Karoo left the cooler open.
rows.reason: A place is added and the subject changes: "Somebody left the freezer door open overnight" became "Die Karoo het die verkoeler oopgelos". "verkoeler" can also read as a car radiator, and "overnight" is dropped.
reasons: DRIFT: A place is added and the subject changes: "Somebody left the freezer door open overnight" became "Die Karoo het die verkoeler oopgelos". "verkoeler" can also read as a car radiator, and "overnight" is dropped.

rows.en: The hadeda has landed on frost and is already drafting a complaint.
rows.text: Die hadeda het op ryp geland en stel reeds 'n klag op.
rows.back: The hadeda landed on frost and is already drawing up a complaint.

rows.en: Frost on the lawn and the morning alarm has just landed, feathers and all.
rows.text: Ryp op die grasperk, en die oggendwekker het net geland, vere en al.
rows.back: Frost on the lawn, and the morning alarm clock has just landed, feathers and all.
rows.note: the alarm clock = a hadeda, implied

rows.en: The car's heater is the most important relationship in your life right now.
rows.text: Die kar se verwarmer is die belangrikste verhouding in jou lewe op die oomblik.
rows.back: The car's heater is the most important relationship in your life right now.

rows.en: The car coughed twice before it agreed to start.
rows.text: Die kar het twee keer gehoes voor hy besluit het om te vat.
rows.back: The car coughed twice before he decided to start.

rows.en: The Toyota started first try. You owe it a wash.
rows.text: Die Toyota het met die eerste try gevat. Jy skuld hom 'n was.
rows.back: The Toyota started on the first try. You owe him a wash.

rows.en: The windscreen kept a record of last night and she is deleting it by hand.
rows.text: Die voorruit het gisteraand se rekord behou, en sy vee dit met die hand uit.
rows.back: The windscreen kept last night's record, and she's wiping it off by hand.
rows.note: unsure: 'rekord' - a record/log of the night (frost); 'sy' = she, unclear who

rows.en: Two beanies, one scraper, minus three: the school run starts before the car agrees.
rows.text: Twee musse, een skraper, minus drie: die skoolrit begin voor die kar instem.
rows.back: Two beanies, one scraper, minus three: the school run starts before the car agrees.

rows.en: Clear skies, open roads, running nose. The full winter set.
rows.text: Die lug is oop, die pad is oop, jou neus loop.
rows.back: The sky is open, the road is open, your nose is running.
rows.reason: "The full winter set" is cut, but the oop/oop/loop rhyme rebuilds the punch.

rows.en: The bluer the sky, the colder the truth.
rows.text: Hoe blouer die lug, hoe kouer die waarheid.
rows.back: The bluer the sky, the colder the truth.

rows.en: Not one cloud, not one degree: a Highveld winter morning doing both at once.
rows.text: Nie een wolk nie, nie een graad nie: 'n Hoëveldse wintermôre doen albei gelyk.
rows.back: Not one cloud, not one degree: a Highveld winter morning does both at once.

rows.en: The kind of day Joburg pretends it doesn't have until you're standing in it.
rows.text: Die soort dag wat Joburg voorgee hy nie het nie totdat jy daarin staan.
rows.back: The kind of day Joburg pretends he doesn't have, until you're standing in it.

rows.en: The 7am sun isn't giving heat yet. Only vibes.
rows.text: Sewe-uur se son deel nog nie hitte uit nie, net vibes.
rows.back: Seven o'clock sun isn't handing out heat yet, just vibes.

rows.en: Five guinea fowl crossing in single file: the frost has everyone walking carefully.
rows.text: Vyf tarentale stap in 'n ry oor: die ryp laat almal versigtig trap.
rows.back: Five guineafowl walking across in a line: the frost has everyone stepping carefully.

rows.en: First traffic of the morning, and it walks and complains at the same time.
rows.text: Die eerste verkeer van die oggend, en dit stap en kla terselfdertyd.
rows.back: The first traffic of the morning, and it walks and complains at the same time.

rows.en: Highveld winter: the only place where you wear two jackets to fetch the post.
rows.text: Hoëveld-winter: die enigste plek waar jy twee jasse aantrek om die pos te gaan haal.
rows.back: Highveld winter: the only place where you put on two coats to go fetch the post.

rows.en: Zero wind. Zero clouds. Zero mercy.
rows.text: Nul wind, nul wolke, nul genade.
rows.back: Zero wind, zero clouds, zero mercy.

rows.en: The Free State just remembered it has a winter setting.
rows.text: Die Vrystaat het pas onthou hy het 'n winter-setting.
rows.back: The Free State has just remembered he has a winter setting.

rows.en: Frost right up to the dam wall: the Karoo did its winter thing overnight.
rows.text: Ryp tot teen die damwal: die Karoo het oornag sy winterding gedoen.
rows.back: Frost right up to the dam wall: the Karoo did its winter thing overnight.

rows.en: Not enough wind to turn one blade, which is why the frost got everything.
rows.text: Nie genoeg wind om een wiek te draai nie, en daarom het die ryp alles gevang.
rows.back: Not enough wind to turn a single windmill blade, and that's why the frost got everything.

rows.en: Pink sky, white veld: the desert runs both extremes before breakfast.
rows.text: Pienk lug, wit veld: die woestyn doen albei uiterstes voor ontbyt.
rows.back: Pink sky, white veld: the desert does both extremes before breakfast.

rows.en: Sun on your back, freezer on your face.
rows.text: Son op jou rug, vrieskas op jou gesig.
rows.back: Sun on your back, freezer on your face.

rows.en: Looks like a tourism ad. Feels like the inside of a fridge.
rows.text: Joburg lyk soos 'n advertensie en voel soos 'n yskas.
rows.back: Joburg looks like an advert and feels like a fridge.
rows.reason: A place is added: the English has no city, but the Afrikaans opens with "Joburg". "tourism ad" is flattened to "advertensie" and "the inside of" is dropped.
reasons: DRIFT: A place is added: the English has no city, but the Afrikaans opens with "Joburg". "tourism ad" is flattened to "advertensie" and "the inside of" is dropped.

rows.en: That first breath of air will wake you better than coffee.
rows.text: Daai eerste asemteug gaan jou wakker maak. Belowe.
rows.back: That first breath is going to wake you up. Promise.
rows.reason: Punchline lost: "will wake you better than coffee" became "gaan jou wakker maak. Belowe." (will wake you up. Promise.), so the coffee comparison is gone.
reasons: DRIFT: Punchline lost: "will wake you better than coffee" became "gaan jou wakker maak. Belowe." (will wake you up. Promise.), so the coffee comparison is gone.

rows.en: Joburg winter dawn: the view is free; the air charges admission.
rows.text: Joburg winterdagbreek: die uitsig is verniet; die lug vra toegangsgeld.
rows.back: Joburg winter daybreak: the view is free; the air charges an entrance fee.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'vra' means 'ask; asks' — nothing in the English source; it is 1 letter from 'vry', the usual word for 'free'

rows.en: The city looks its best exactly when the air hurts most, which is unfair.
rows.text: Die stad lyk op sy beste presies wanneer die lug die seerste maak, en dis onregverdig.
rows.back: The city looks its best exactly when the air hurts the most, and that's unfair.

rows.en: Sun's out. Don't be fooled. Nature is lying.
rows.text: Son is uit. Moenie geflous word nie. Die natuur lieg.
rows.back: Sun is out. Don't be fooled. Nature lies.

rows.en: Sunshine: 10/10. Feels-like: don't ask.
rows.text: Sonskyn: 10/10. Gevoel: vra liewer nie.
rows.back: Sunshine: 10/10. Feel: rather don't ask.
rows.reason: The app pun in "Feels-like" is softened to "Gevoel"; the joke still reads.

rows.en: The sunny side of the wall is prime property, and it is taken.
rows.text: Die sonkant van die muur is premium eiendom, en dit is reeds gevat.
rows.back: The sunny side of the wall is premium property, and it's already taken.

rows.en: In the sun: bearable. Two steps left: Antarctica.
rows.text: In die son: draaglik. Twee treë links: Antarktika.
rows.back: In the sun: bearable. Two steps left: Antarctica.

rows.en: Karoo morning. The kind that makes you respect every farmer who chose this.
rows.text: Karoo-oggend. Die soort wat jou laat respek hê vir elke boer wat dit gekies het.
rows.back: Karoo morning. The kind that makes you respect every farmer who chose it.

rows.en: Full sun, visible breath: the Karoo running both seasons before lunch.
rows.text: Vol son, sigbare asem: die Karoo speel albei seisoene af voor middagete.
rows.back: Full sun, visible breath: the Karoo plays out both seasons before lunch.

rows.en: Breath like smoke, frost on the glass, sun already out: Highveld school run.
rows.text: Asem soos rook, ryp op die glas, son reeds op: Hoëveldse skoolrit.
rows.back: Breath like smoke, frost on the glass, sun already up: Highveld school run.

rows.en: The bakkie iced over under a completely clear sky, which is exactly how it works.
rows.text: Die bakkie het onder 'n heeltemal skoon lug toegevries — presies hoe dit werk.
rows.back: The bakkie froze over under a completely clear sky - that's exactly how it works.

rows.en: The sun is up and doing its best; the frost is unconvinced so far.
rows.text: Die son is op en doen sy bes; die ryp is tot dusver nie oortuig nie.
rows.back: The sun is up and doing his best; the frost isn't convinced so far.

rows.en: Window sun is the only sun doing its job today.
rows.text: Vensterson is die enigste son wat vandag werk.
rows.back: Window sun is the only sun that works today.

rows.en: It looks lovely out there. We've chosen to believe it from in here.
rows.text: Buite lyk dit heerlik. Ons het besluit om dit te glo van hier af.
rows.back: Outside looks lovely. We've decided to believe it from here.

rows.en: Full sunshine, full jacket. Both are non-negotiable.
rows.text: Volle sonskyn, volle baadjie. Altwee is nodig.
rows.back: Full sunshine, full jacket. Both are needed.

rows.en: The jacket is going on because the window already said so.
rows.text: Die baadjie gaan aan, want die venster het klaar so gesê.
rows.back: The jacket goes on, because the window already said so.

rows.en: Coats and coffees in full sun: winter in this city photographs like summer.
rows.text: Jasse en koffies in vol son: winter in hierdie stad lyk op foto's soos somer.
rows.back: Coats and coffees in full sun: winter in this city looks like summer in photos.

rows.en: Lekker koud, but the rugby fields are about to look perfect.
rows.text: Lekker koud, maar die rugbyvelde gaan nou-nou perfek lyk.
rows.back: Nicely cold, but the rugby fields are going to look perfect in a moment.

rows.en: Perfect rugby weather. For the spectators with blankets.
rows.text: Perfekte rugbyweer. Vir die toeskouers met komberse.
rows.back: Perfect rugby weather. For the spectators with blankets.

rows.en: Blue sky, gold grass, white edges: a Highveld rugby morning in full kit.
rows.text: Blou lug, goue gras, wit rande: 'n Hoëveldse rugbyoggend in volle drag.
rows.back: Blue sky, golden grass, white edges: a Highveld rugby morning in full kit.

rows.en: Sunny, with a 100% chance of shivering.
rows.text: Sonnig met 'n honderd persent kans van bibber.
rows.back: Sunny with a hundred percent chance of shivering.

rows.en: Frost on the grass, steam off the field: winter running weather at its most honest.
rows.text: Ryp op die gras, stoom van die veld af: wintersdrafweer op sy eerlikste.
rows.back: Frost on the grass, steam coming off the field: winter running weather at its most honest.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'wintersdrafweer' — not found in any external source

rows.en: Cold enough to see every breath, clear enough that nobody minds.
rows.text: Koud genoeg om elke asem te sien, helder genoeg dat niemand omgee nie.
rows.back: Cold enough to see every breath, clear enough that nobody minds.

rows.en: Perfect drying weather. The washing will dry and freeze, in that order.
rows.text: Perfekte wasgoedweer. Die wasgoed gaan droog word én bevries.
rows.back: Perfect washing weather. The washing is going to dry AND freeze.
rows.reason: "in that order" is dropped, but the emphatic "én" keeps the dry-and-freeze joke.

rows.en: The towels went out damp and are coming in as boards.
rows.text: Die handdoeke is klam uitgehang en kom as planke terug.
rows.back: The towels went out damp and are coming back as planks.

rows.en: That washing is not dry; it is preserved. Winter dusk works fast out here.
rows.text: Daardie wasgoed is nie droog nie; dit is ingelê. Winterskemer werk vinnig hier.
rows.back: That washing isn't dry; it's been preserved. Winter dusk works fast here.

rows.en: The dog is still keen. The dog is always keen. Respect.
rows.text: Die hond is nog steeds keen. Die hond is altyd keen. Respek.
rows.back: The dog is still keen. The dog is always keen. Respect.

rows.en: Even the dog's breath is showing. That's the reading.
rows.text: Die hond se asem wys ook. Dis hoe koud dit is.
rows.back: The dog's breath shows too. That's how cold it is.
rows.reason: Punchline flattened: "That is the reading" (the dog as thermometer) became the plain "Dis hoe koud dit is" (that is how cold it is).
reasons: DRIFT: Punchline flattened: "That is the reading" (the dog as thermometer) became the plain "Dis hoe koud dit is" (that is how cold it is).

rows.en: Frost already forming and the sun barely down: tonight means business.
rows.text: Die ryp trek al en die son is skaars weg: vanaand is dit ernstig.
rows.back: The frost is already setting in and the sun's barely gone: tonight it's serious.

rows.en: A clear dusk on the Highveld is just the frost clearing its throat.
rows.text: 'n Helder skemer op die Hoëveld is net die ryp wat sy keel skoonmaak.
rows.back: A clear dusk on the Highveld is just the frost clearing its throat.

rows.en: The sun is heading home now, taking the last three degrees with it.
rows.text: Die son gaan nou huis toe. Vat sy laaste drie grade saam.
rows.back: The sun is going home now. Taking his last three degrees with him.

rows.en: The horses are doing their own weather report, one breath at a time.
rows.text: Die perde doen hul eie weerberig, een asem op 'n slag.
rows.back: The horses are doing their own weather report, one breath at a time.

rows.en: Not a cloud in sight. Not a degree either.
rows.text: Nie 'n wolk in sig nie. Ook nie 'n graad nie.
rows.back: Not a cloud in sight. Not a degree either.

rows.en: The sunset is free of charge. So is the head cold.
rows.text: Die sonsondergang is verniet. Die verkoue ook.
rows.back: The sunset is free. So is the head cold.

rows.en: The braai is happening. The braai always happens. We just pull the chairs closer.
rows.text: Die braai gaan aan. Die braai gaan altyd aan. Ons trek net die stoele nader.
rows.back: The braai goes on. The braai always goes on. We just pull the chairs closer.

rows.en: The temperature dropped with the sun and the circle got tighter by exactly that much.
rows.text: Die temperatuur het saam met die son geval en die kring het presies soveel nader getrek.
rows.back: The temperature dropped with the sun, and the circle pulled in by exactly as much.

rows.en: The evening turned cold the minute it turned beautiful, which is the usual trade.
rows.text: Die aand het koud geword die oomblik toe dit mooi word — dis maar die gewone ruil.
rows.back: The evening turned cold the moment it turned pretty - that's just the usual trade.

rows.en: A sky that clean means the field freezes before the floodlights even warm up.
rows.text: So 'n skoon lug beteken die veld vries voor die ligte eers warm word.
rows.back: A sky this clear means the field freezes before the lights have even warmed up.

rows.en: Golden hour, ice-cold air. Cape Town loves a dramatic contrast.
rows.text: Golden hour, yskoue lug. Kaapstad hou van drama.
rows.back: Golden hour, ice-cold air. Cape Town loves drama.

rows.en: Tomorrow's first task: five minutes of windscreen scraping in your work clothes.
rows.text: Môreoggend se eerste taak: vyf minute ys krap in jou kerkklere.
rows.back: Tomorrow morning's first job: five minutes of scraping ice in your church clothes.
rows.note: church clothes implies tomorrow is Sunday
rows.reason: "in your work clothes" became "in jou kerkklere" (church clothes), which makes tomorrow a Sunday instead of a workday. That changes the day.
reasons: DRIFT: "in your work clothes" became "in jou kerkklere" (church clothes), which makes tomorrow a Sunday instead of a workday. That changes the day.

rows.en: The cars have surrendered. They're sleeping under ice tonight.
rows.text: Die karre het klaar opgegee. Hulle slaap onder ys.
rows.back: The cars have already given up. They're sleeping under ice.

rows.en: Frost on the lawn. Frost on the bakkie. Frost in the pet bowl.
rows.text: Ryp op die grasperk. Ryp op die bakkie. Ryp in die troeteldierbak.
rows.back: Frost on the lawn. Frost on the bakkie. Frost in the pet bowl.

rows.en: The frost is doing the rounds tonight and skipping nobody.
rows.text: Die ryp doen vanaand sy rondtes en slaan niemand oor nie.
rows.back: The frost is doing its rounds tonight and skipping nobody.

rows.en: Clear sky tonight. That means the cold has an all-access pass.
rows.text: Skoon lug vanaand. Dit beteken die koue het vrye toegang.
rows.back: Clear sky tonight. That means the cold has free access.

rows.en: The frost has already started its shift. By dawn the lawn will be glass.
rows.text: Die ryp is klaar besig. Teen dagbreek is die grasperk 'n spieël.
rows.back: The frost is already at work. By daybreak the lawn will be a mirror.

rows.en: The bin run is being done at speed tonight, and the sky knows why.
rows.text: Die vullisblik word vanaand teen spoed uitgevat, en die lug weet hoekom.
rows.back: The bin is being taken out at speed tonight, and the sky knows why.

rows.en: Tile floors are tonight's villain. Wear something on your feet.
rows.text: Teëlvloere is vanaand se skurk. Sit iets aan jou voete.
rows.back: Tile floors are tonight's villain. Put something on your feet.

rows.en: The Southern Cross is out and the lawn has gone silver under it.
rows.text: Die Suiderkruis is uit en die grasperk het silwer geword daaronder.
rows.back: The Southern Cross is out and the lawn has turned silver under it.

rows.en: A sky this clean at night is beautiful, and it charges in degrees.
rows.text: So 'n skoon naglug is pragtig, en jy betaal daarvoor in grade.
rows.back: A night sky this clear is beautiful, and you pay for it in degrees.

rows.en: Stars that sharp come standard with air this cold — it is a package deal.
rows.text: Sterre só skerp kom standaard met lug só koud — dis 'n pakketaanbod.
rows.back: Stars this sharp come standard with air this cold - it's a package deal.

rows.en: Every star is out tonight, and the frost is the entry fee.
rows.text: Elke ster is vanaand uit, en die ryp is die toegangsgeld.
rows.back: Every star is out tonight, and the frost is the entrance fee.

rows.en: The Southern Cross is out, and so is the frost. Package deal.
rows.text: Die Suiderkruis is uit, en die ryp ook. Pakketaanbod.
rows.back: The Southern Cross is out, and so is the frost. Package deal.

rows.en: Clear nights are winter's way of apologising.
rows.text: Helder nagte is die winter se jammer-sê.
rows.back: Clear nights are winter's way of saying sorry.

rows.en: Duvets in the bakkie, flask on the tailgate: the sky is worth the freeze tonight.
rows.text: Duvets in die bakkie, fles op die agterklap: die lug is vanaand die koue werd.
rows.back: Duvets in the bakkie, flask on the tailgate: tonight the sky is worth the cold.

rows.en: Braaiing in beanies under a hard clear sky: winter never cancelled anything here.
rows.text: Braai met musse op onder 'n kristalhelder lug: die winter kanselleer niks hier nie.
rows.back: Braaiing with beanies on under a crystal-clear sky: winter cancels nothing here.

rows.en: Free planetarium tonight. Admission: your toes.
rows.text: Gratis planetarium vanaand. Toegangsprys: jou tone.
rows.back: Free planetarium tonight. Entry price: your toes.

rows.en: First star is out. First ten degrees have also left.
rows.text: Eerste ster is uit. Eerste tien grade is ook uit.
rows.back: First star is out. First ten degrees are out too.

rows.en: The cold is charging admission tonight and the sky is worth every degree.
rows.text: Die koue vra vanaand toegangsgeld, en die lug is elke graad werd.
rows.back: The cold is charging an entrance fee tonight, and the sky is worth every degree.

rows.en: Somewhere out there people are going for a run right now. Strength to them.
rows.text: Iewers is daar mense wat nou gaan draf. Sterkte vir hulle.
rows.back: Somewhere there are people going for a run right now. Good luck to them.

rows.en: Ja, it's jersey weather. Double jersey.
rows.text: Ja, dis truiweer. Dubbel trui.
rows.back: Yes, it's jersey weather. Double jersey.

rows.en: The grass is wet, the air is cold, and the jersey was not optional.
rows.text: Die gras is nat, die lug is koud, en die trui was nie opsioneel nie.
rows.back: The grass is wet, the air is cold, and the jersey wasn't optional.

rows.en: Dew this heavy means the night got properly cold and stayed there.
rows.text: Dou só swaar beteken die nag het behoorlik koud geword en so gebly.
rows.back: Dew this heavy means the night got properly cold and stayed that way.

rows.en: Small dog, thick jersey, short patrol: winter mornings run on reduced hours.
rows.text: Klein hond, dik trui, kort patrollie: winteroggende werk verkorte ure.
rows.back: Small dog, thick jersey, short patrol: winter mornings work reduced hours.

rows.en: Frost on the grass, frost on the bakkie, frost on my will to live.
rows.text: Ryp op die gras, ryp op die bakkie, ryp op my moed.
rows.back: Frost on the grass, frost on the bakkie, frost on my courage.
rows.reason: "my will to live" is softened to "my moed" (my courage/spirit). The shape and the joke hold, and the tone is warmer.

rows.en: The sky is clear and the car is white, and those two facts are related.
rows.text: Die lug is skoon en die kar is wit, en daardie twee feite hou verband.
rows.back: The sky is clear and the car is white, and those two facts are connected.

rows.en: Layer up like you're climbing Sani Pass.
rows.text: Trek lae aan asof jy Sani Pass klim.
rows.back: Layer up like you're climbing Sani Pass.

rows.en: Your jacket has a jacket. It's that kind of day.
rows.text: Jou baadjie het 'n baadjie. Dis daai soort dag.
rows.back: Your jacket has a jacket. It's that kind of day.

rows.en: The zip goes all the way up today; the walk to the gate has teeth.
rows.text: Die rits gaan vandag heeltemal op; die stap hek toe het tande.
rows.back: The zip goes all the way up today; the walk to the gate has teeth.

rows.en: Beanie plus puffer plus school tie: the cold front has reached the uniform.
rows.text: Mus plus poffer plus skooldas: die kouefront het die skooldrag bereik.
rows.back: Beanie plus puffer plus school tie: the cold front has reached the school uniform.

rows.en: Your breath is doing special effects.
rows.text: Jou asem doen spesiale effekte.
rows.back: Your breath is doing special effects.

rows.en: Most beautiful time of day. Say the people who stay inside.
rows.text: Mooiste tyd van die dag. Sê die mense wat binne bly.
rows.back: Most beautiful time of day. Say the people who stay inside.

rows.en: Your hands are in your pockets and they're not coming out.
rows.text: Jou hande is in jou sakke en hulle kom nie uit nie.
rows.back: Your hands are in your pockets and they're not coming out.

rows.en: You can see his breath, and the sheep are wearing the only good answer.
rows.text: Jy kan sy asem sien, en die skape dra die enigste goeie antwoord.
rows.back: You can see his breath, and the sheep are wearing the only good answer.
rows.note: unsure: 'sy asem' - whose breath (a farmer?) is not established

rows.en: The Karoo does its coldest hour right before its prettiest one.
rows.text: Die Karoo se koudste uur kom net voor sy mooiste een.
rows.back: The Karoo's coldest hour comes just before its most beautiful one.

rows.en: The sheep bunched before he opened the gate; they read the cold first.
rows.text: Die skape het saamgebondel voor hy die hek oopgemaak het; hulle het die koue eerste gelees.
rows.back: The sheep huddled together before he opened the gate; they read the cold first.

rows.en: Getting out of bed was a mistake. A documented one.
rows.text: Om op te staan was 'n fout. 'n Gedokumenteerde een.
rows.back: Getting up was a mistake. A documented one.

rows.en: The warmest place in the province was abandoned here at about six-fifteen.
rows.text: Die warmste plek in die provinsie is hier omtrent kwart oor ses verlaat.
rows.back: The warmest place in the province gets abandoned here at about quarter past six.
rows.note: unsure: word order odd; presumably the warmest place = bed

rows.en: Smoke going straight up means cold, still and not one breath of wind.
rows.text: Rook wat reguit opstyg beteken koud, stil en geen luggie nie.
rows.back: Smoke rising straight up means cold, still and not a breath of wind.

rows.en: You're not cold, you're 'lekker koud'. Big difference.
rows.text: Jy is nie koud nie, jy is 'lekker koud'. Groot verskil.
rows.back: You're not cold, you're 'lekker cold'. Big difference.

rows.en: Minus something this morning: the windscreen has grown its own art collection.
rows.text: Minus iets vanoggend: die voorruit het sy eie kunsversameling gekweek.
rows.back: Minus something this morning: the windscreen has grown its own art collection.

rows.en: The cold front is here and it brought friends.
rows.text: Die kouefront is hier en hy het maats gebring.
rows.back: The cold front is here and he brought friends.

rows.en: Winter sun: all of the light, none of the heat. Nice try, sun.
rows.text: Winterson: al die lig, nul van die hitte. Mooi probeer, son.
rows.back: Winter sun: all the light, none of the heat. Nice try, sun.

rows.en: Outside is a test of character. You're failing.
rows.text: Buite is 'n karaktertoets. Jy druip.
rows.back: Outside is a character test. You're failing.

rows.en: The garden tap grew a white beard overnight; the night was that serious.
rows.text: Die tuinkraan het oornag 'n wit baard gekweek; so ernstig was die nag.
rows.back: The garden tap grew a white beard overnight; that's how serious the night was.

rows.en: That drop has been thinking about letting go since about four this morning.
rows.text: Daardie druppel dink al van omtrent vieruur vanoggend af daaraan om los te laat.
rows.back: That drop has been thinking about letting go since about four this morning.

rows.en: Time to dig out that ugly beanie.
rows.text: Tyd om daai lelike beanie te soek.
rows.back: Time to find that ugly beanie.

rows.en: The sign says the rain won; the faces say it didn't.
rows.text: Die bord sê die reën het gewen; die gesigte sê nee.
rows.back: The board says the rain won; the faces say no.
rows.note: unsure: 'bord' - scoreboard or a sign (e.g. match-cancelled notice)

rows.en: The car seats are freezing. Everything is freezing.
rows.text: Die karsitplekke vries. Alles vries.
rows.back: The car seats are freezing. Everything's freezing.

rows.en: The morning's second kettle has nothing to do with tea.
rows.text: Die oggend se tweede ketel het niks met tee te doen nie.
rows.back: The morning's second kettle has nothing to do with tea.

rows.en: The dog refused to go outside. Fair.
rows.text: Die hond het geweier om buite te gaan. Billik.
rows.back: The dog refused to go outside. Fair.

rows.en: The dog looked out the front door, turned around, and went back to bed. Says it all.
rows.text: Die hond het by die voordeur gekyk, omgedraai, en teruggegaan bed toe. Wys jou.
rows.back: The dog looked at the front door, turned around, and went back to bed. Goes to show you.

rows.en: One look at that white lawn and the blanket vote was unanimous.
rows.text: Een kyk na daardie wit grasperk en die kombersstemming was eenparig.
rows.back: One look at that white lawn and the blanket vote was unanimous.

rows.en: The duvet is calling and the duvet is winning.
rows.text: Die duvet roep en die duvet wen.
rows.back: The duvet calls and the duvet wins.

rows.en: Blanket burrito mode: activated.
rows.text: Kombers burrito modus: geaktiveer.
rows.back: Blanket burrito mode: activated.

rows.en: Construction finished at nine: one duvet cave, single occupant, no visitors till spring.
rows.text: Bouwerk klaar om nege: een duvetgrot, een bewoner, geen besoekers tot die lente nie.
rows.back: Construction done by nine: one duvet cave, one occupant, no visitors until spring.

rows.en: This is not what the tourism brochure promised.
rows.text: Dit is nie wat die toerisme brosjure beloof het nie.
rows.back: This is not what the tourism brochure promised.

rows.en: The sun is out. It means nothing. The sun is lying.
rows.text: Die son is uit. Dit beteken niks. Die son jok.
rows.back: The sun is out. It means nothing. The sun is lying.

rows.en: Somebody's optimism is still on the table, under a millimetre of frost.
rows.text: Iemand se optimisme lê nog op die tafel, onder 'n millimeter ryp.
rows.back: Someone's optimism is still lying on the table, under a millimetre of frost.

rows.en: Grey sky, white table: the patio has switched seasons without asking anyone.
rows.text: Grys lug, wit tafel: die stoep het seisoene geruil sonder om iemand te vra.
rows.back: Grey sky, white table: the stoep swapped seasons without asking anyone.

rows.en: The house is colder inside than outside. Architecture is a beautiful thing.
rows.text: Die huis is kouer binne as buite. Argitektuur is 'n mooi ding.
rows.back: The house is colder inside than outside. Architecture is a beautiful thing.

rows.en: One patch of sun came into this lounge and the dog got there first.
rows.text: Een kol son het in hierdie sitkamer ingekom en die hond was eerste daar.
rows.back: One patch of sun came into this lounge and the dog got there first.

rows.en: It is heater season, and the best seat in the house has fur on it.
rows.text: Dis verwarmerseisoen, en die beste sitplek in die huis het pels op.
rows.back: It's heater season, and the best seat in the house has fur on it.

rows.en: The heater is your best friend. Your only friend.
rows.text: Die heater is jou beste vriend. Jou enigste vriend.
rows.back: The heater is your best friend. Your only friend.

rows.en: The sun is leaving the mountains one shelf at a time.
rows.text: Die son verlaat die berge een rak op 'n slag.
rows.back: The sun leaves the mountains one ledge at a time.

rows.en: The mountain is in there somewhere, wrapped up for the winter.
rows.text: Die berg is daar êrens, toegedraai vir die winter.
rows.back: The mountain is there somewhere, wrapped up for winter.

rows.en: The beach has gone to one colour, and it is the cold one.
rows.text: Die strand het een kleur geword, en dis die koue een.
rows.back: The beach has turned one colour, and it's the cold one.

rows.en: Nobody's footprints on that sand today; the cold is keeping its beach to itself.
rows.text: Niemand se spore op daardie sand vandag nie; die koue hou sy strand vir homself.
rows.back: Nobody's footprints on that sand today; the cold is keeping its beach to itself.

rows.en: Outside is closed. Management is inside.
rows.text: Buite is gesluit. Bestuur is binne.
rows.back: Outside is closed. Management is inside.

rows.en: Pretty evening. Deeply uninhabitable.
rows.text: Mooi aand. Diep onbewoonbaar.
rows.back: Beautiful evening. Deeply uninhabitable.

rows.en: Beautiful view. Hostile air.
rows.text: Pragtige uitsig. Vyandige lug.
rows.back: Beautiful view. Hostile air.

rows.en: This is no longer a beverage. It's a strategy.
rows.text: Dit is nie meer 'n drankie nie. Dit is 'n strategie.
rows.back: It's not a drink any more. It's a strategy.

rows.en: Friday evening, snow on the Apostles, and the only queue is for the kettle.
rows.text: Vrydagaand, sneeu op die Apostels, en die enigste tou is vir die ketel.
rows.back: Friday night, snow on the Apostles, and the only queue is for the kettle.

rows.en: Hot chocolate weather is self-diagnosing. The marshmallows are the second opinion.
rows.text: Warmsjokolade-weer diagnoseer homself. Die malvalekkers is die tweede mening.
rows.back: Hot-chocolate weather diagnoses itself. The marshmallows are the second opinion.

rows.en: Snow on the mountain. The kind of cold Cape Town frames and hangs on the wall.
rows.text: Sneeu op die berg. Die soort koue wat Kaapstad raam en teen die muur hang.
rows.back: Snow on the mountain. The kind of cold Cape Town frames and hangs on the wall.

rows.en: Sunset showed up. The cold came with it.
rows.text: Die sonsondergang het opgedaag. Die koue het saamgekom.
rows.back: The sunset showed up. The cold came along.

rows.en: The sky apologised. The pavement didn't.
rows.text: Die lug het om verskoning gevra. Die sypaadjie nie.
rows.back: The sky apologised. The pavement didn't.

rows.en: The mist has moved into the valley for the night and locked the gate behind it.
rows.text: Die mis het vir die nag in die vallei ingetrek en die hek agter hom gesluit.
rows.back: The mist moved into the valley for the night and locked the gate behind him.

rows.en: That mist is tomorrow morning's frost out doing a site inspection.
rows.text: Daardie mis is môreoggend se ryp wat 'n terreininspeksie doen.
rows.back: That mist is tomorrow morning's frost doing a site inspection.

rows.en: The cold cleared the whole street an hour before closing time.
rows.text: Die koue het die hele straat 'n uur voor sluitingstyd skoongevee.
rows.back: The cold swept the whole street clean an hour before closing time.

rows.en: Every streetlamp down the road is lighting nobody; winter nights empty a dorp early.
rows.text: Elke straatlig langs die pad skyn vir niemand nie; winternagte maak 'n dorp vroeg leeg.
rows.back: Every streetlight along the road is shining for nobody; winter nights empty a town early.

rows.en: The chair is taken. The dog got there first. Rules are rules.
rows.text: Die stoel is gevat. Die hond het eerste gekom. Die reëls is die reëls.
rows.back: The chair is taken. The dog got there first. Rules are rules.

rows.en: Outside is for the stars tonight; everything with fur voted fireplace.
rows.text: Buite is vanaand vir die sterre; alles met pels het vir die kaggel gestem.
rows.back: Outside is for the stars tonight; everything with fur voted for the fireplace.

rows.en: Clear night, wet steps, visible breath: the frost is filling in its paperwork.
rows.text: Skoon nag, nat trappe, sigbare asem: die ryp voltooi sy papierwerk.
rows.back: Clear night, wet steps, visible breath: the frost is completing its paperwork.

rows.en: One last look at a sky that is about to get seriously cold.
rows.text: Een laaste kyk na 'n lug wat op die punt staan om ernstig koud te word.
rows.back: One last look at a sky that's about to get seriously cold.

rows.en: Hot water bottle is the real MVP today.
rows.text: Warmwaterbottel is die werklike held vandag.
rows.back: Hot water bottle is the real hero today.

rows.en: Fingerless gloves at a laptop: winter has entered the home office.
rows.text: Vingerlose handskoene by 'n laptop: winter het die tuiskantoor betree.
rows.back: Fingerless gloves at a laptop: winter has entered the home office.

rows.en: Prettiest blue sky in the country, and it feels like a fridge with a view.
rows.text: Mooiste blou lug in die land, en dit voel soos 'n yskas met uitsig.
rows.back: Prettiest blue sky in the country, and it feels like a fridge with a view.

rows.en: Cold enough to share one blanket, clear enough to make it worth it.
rows.text: Koud genoeg om een kombers te deel, helder genoeg om dit die moeite werd te maak.
rows.back: Cold enough to share one blanket, clear enough to make it worth it.

rows.en: Beanie, snood, torch, book: winter nights build the best reading rooms.
rows.text: Mus, nekwarmer, flits, boek: winternagte bou die beste leeskamers.
rows.back: Beanie, neck warmer, torch, book: winter nights build the best reading rooms.

rows.en: Wet road, grey sky, dog in a jersey: winter is fully operational.
rows.text: Nat pad, grys lug, hond in 'n trui: winter is ten volle in werking.
rows.back: Wet road, grey sky, dog in a jersey: winter is fully operational.

rows.en: The yard is wet, the air is cold, and security has suspended patrols.
rows.text: Die werf is nat, die lug is koud, en sekuriteit het patrollies opgeskort.
rows.back: The yard is wet, the air is cold, and security has suspended patrols.

rows.en: That is not a dog refusing a walk; that is a dog reading a forecast.
rows.text: Dit is nie 'n hond wat 'n stap weier nie; dit is 'n hond wat 'n voorspelling lees.
rows.back: That's not a dog refusing a walk; that's a dog reading a forecast.

rows.en: Your toes have filed a formal complaint.
rows.text: Jou tone het 'n formele klagte ingedien.
rows.back: Your toes have lodged a formal complaint.

rows.en: Socks go on the heater first; feet join later — the winter system works.
rows.text: Sokkies gaan eerste op die verwarmer; voete kom later — die winterstelsel werk.
rows.back: Socks go on the heater first; feet come later - the winter system works.

rows.en: Hot chocolate is not a want. It's a need.
rows.text: Warm sjokolade is nie 'n wens nie. Dis 'n behoefte.
rows.back: Hot chocolate isn't a wish. It's a need.

rows.en: Gloves-around-the-cup weather: the coffee is doing two jobs at once.
rows.text: Handskoene-om-die-beker-weer: die koffie doen twee werke tegelyk.
rows.back: Gloves-around-the-mug weather: the coffee is doing two jobs at once.

rows.en: Even the Capetonians are admitting it's cold.
rows.text: Selfs die Kapenaars erken dit is koud.
rows.back: Even the Capetonians admit it's cold.

rows.en: The jersey got promoted to balaclava somewhere between the door and the gate.
rows.text: Die trui is êrens tussen die deur en die hek tot balaclava bevorder.
rows.back: Somewhere between the door and the gate the jersey got promoted to balaclava.

rows.en: The air found the one gap in the outfit and he is closing it by hand.
rows.text: Die lug het die een gaping in die uitrusting gekry en hy maak dit met die hand toe.
rows.back: The air found the one gap in the outfit and he's closing it by hand.
rows.note: unsure: 'hy' - who closes the gap (the wearer?) is not established

rows.en: The washing is not going to dry. We hang it up for hope.
rows.text: Die wasgoed gaan nie droog word nie. Ons hang dit op vir die hoop.
rows.back: The washing isn't going to get dry. We're hanging it up for the sake of hope.
rows.note: 'vir die hoop' = out of hope / for hope's sake

rows.en: The sausage dog has a jersey. He didn't ask for it, but he wears it with dignity.
rows.text: Die worshond het 'n trui. Hy het dit nie gevra nie, maar hy dra dit met waardigheid.
rows.back: The dachshund has a jersey. He didn't ask for it, but he wears it with dignity.

rows.en: Cold plus beautiful is an honest trade. We'll take it.
rows.text: Koue plus mooi is 'n eerlike transaksie. Ons vat dit.
rows.back: Cold plus beautiful is an honest transaction. We'll take it.

rows.en: Snow on the berg, washing on the line: cold enough to freeze, dry enough to try.
rows.text: Sneeu op die berg, wasgoed op die draad: koud genoeg om te vries, droog genoeg om te probeer.
rows.back: Snow on the mountain, washing on the line: cold enough to freeze, dry enough to try.

rows.en: The great debate: do we switch the heater on too, or are we not made of money?
rows.text: Die groot debat: sit die verwarmer óók aan, of is ons nie gemaak van geld nie?
rows.back: The big debate: do we switch the heater on TOO, or are we not made of money?
rows.note: 'óók aan' = also on (in addition to something else); the second clause reads a bit tangled, roughly 'or aren't we made of money after all?'

rows.en: Chair turned to the heater, blanket up, tea close: winter Sunday, executed correctly.
rows.text: Stoel na die verwarmer gedraai, kombers op, tee naby: wintersondag, korrek uitgevoer.
rows.back: Chair turned to the heater, blanket on, tea close by: winter Sunday, correctly executed.

rows.en: The hi-vis is doing exactly what it was bought for this morning.
rows.text: Die reflekterende baadjie doen vanoggend presies waarvoor dit gekoop is.
rows.back: The reflective jacket is doing exactly what it was bought for this morning.

rows.en: The fog swallowed the whole street and gave up at the hi-vis.
rows.text: Die mis het die hele straat ingesluk en by die reflekterende baadjie opgegee.
rows.back: The mist swallowed the whole street and gave up at the reflective jacket.

rows.en: Those headlights have been ‘almost here’ for five minutes. Fog time runs slower.
rows.text: Daardie kopligte is al vyf minute 'amper hier'. Mistyd loop stadiger.
rows.back: Those headlights have been 'almost here' for five minutes. Mist-time runs slower.

rows.en: Everything past the streetlight is a rumour until about nine.
rows.text: Alles verby die straatlig is 'n gerug tot omtrent nege-uur.
rows.back: Everything past the streetlight is a rumour until about nine o'clock.

rows.en: The cows know exactly where they are. Which is more than the rest of us can say.
rows.text: Die koeie weet presies waar hulle is. Meer as wat ons kan sê.
rows.back: The cows know exactly where they are. More than we can say.

rows.en: Visibility is down to one cow.
rows.text: Sigbaarheid is af tot een koei.
rows.back: Visibility is down to one cow.

rows.en: Silent Hill vibes. Without the monsters. Hopefully.
rows.text: Silent Hill vibes. Sonder die monsters. Hopelik.
rows.back: Silent Hill vibes. Without the monsters. Hopefully.

rows.en: One lit window is taking on the whole fog, and losing beautifully.
rows.text: Een verligte venster vat die hele mis aan, en verloor pragtig.
rows.back: One lit window takes on the whole mist, and loses beautifully.

rows.en: The fog is thick enough to hold a beam of kitchen light like a solid object.
rows.text: Die mis is dik genoeg om 'n straal kombuislig soos 'n vaste ding vas te hou.
rows.back: The mist is thick enough to hold a beam of kitchen light like a solid object.

rows.en: The sun is coming through the fog at half strength and full gold.
rows.text: Die son kom deur die mis teen halwe krag en vol goud.
rows.back: The sun comes through the mist at half power and full gold.

rows.en: The streetlights are trying their best.
rows.text: Die straatligte probeer hul bes.
rows.back: The streetlights are trying their best.

rows.en: The world got a soft filter this morning.
rows.text: Die wêreld het 'n sagte filter gekry vanoggend.
rows.back: The world got a soft filter this morning.

rows.en: The fog rolled in at three and started deleting the neighbourhood from the far end.
rows.text: Die mis het drieuur ingerol en die buurt van die verste kant af begin uitvee.
rows.back: The mist rolled in at three and started erasing the neighbourhood from the far side.
rows.note: 'drieuur' = three o'clock, a.m. or p.m. not stated

rows.en: Visibility has clocked off. You're on your own.
rows.text: Sigbaarheid het uitgeklok. Jy is op jou eie.
rows.back: Visibility has clocked out. You're on your own.

rows.en: Forward is still an option. Sightseeing is not.
rows.text: Vorentoe is nog 'n opsie. Rondkyk nie.
rows.back: Forward is still an option. Looking around isn't.

rows.en: Fog settles in the low ground, which is why the herd sleeps on the hill.
rows.text: Mis sak in die laagtes, en dis hoekom die trop op die bult slaap.
rows.back: Mist settles in the hollows, and that's why the herd sleeps on the hill.

rows.en: The fog arrived unannounced. Classic fog.
rows.text: Die mis het onverwags opgedaag. Klassieke mis.
rows.back: The mist turned up unexpectedly. Classic mist.

rows.en: The world just... disappeared.
rows.text: Die wêreld het net... verdwyn.
rows.back: The world just... disappeared.

rows.en: The fog ate the neighbourhood.
rows.text: Die mis het die buurt opgeëet.
rows.back: The mist ate the neighbourhood.

rows.en: The cat can see exactly what is in that fog and is choosing not to say.
rows.text: Die kat kan presies sien wat in daardie mis is en kies om niks te sê nie.
rows.back: The cat can see exactly what's in that mist and chooses to say nothing.

rows.en: Walking the dog has become a trust exercise.
rows.text: Om die hond te stap het 'n vertroue-oefening geword.
rows.back: Walking the dog has become a trust exercise.

rows.en: The dog is definitely still on the end of that leash. Almost definitely.
rows.text: Die hond is definitief nog aan die punt van daardie leiband. Amper definitief.
rows.back: The dog is definitely still on the end of that lead. Almost definitely.

rows.en: Current visibility: one whole dog short of complete.
rows.text: Huidige sigbaarheid: een hele hond kort van volledig.
rows.back: Current visibility: one whole dog short of complete.

rows.en: The neighbours exist. Apparently. Can't confirm.
rows.text: Die bure bestaan. Glo so. Kan nie bevestig nie.
rows.back: The neighbours exist. Supposedly. Can't confirm.

rows.en: The fog is lying in the streets like it pays rates here.
rows.text: Die mis lê in die strate asof hy hier erfbelasting betaal.
rows.back: The mist lies in the streets as if it pays rates here.
rows.note: unsure: 'erfbelasting' = property rates on a stand (reading used) or inheritance tax; either way 'acts like it owns the place'

rows.en: The fog doesn't care about your schedule.
rows.text: Die mis gee nie om oor jou skedule nie.
rows.back: The mist doesn't care about your schedule.

rows.en: Even your GPS is confused.
rows.text: Selfs jou GPS is verward.
rows.back: Even your GPS is confused.

rows.en: Your GPS says you have arrived. Your GPS is lying.
rows.text: Die GPS sê jy het opgedaag. Die GPS jok.
rows.back: The GPS says you've arrived. The GPS is lying.

rows.en: The phone knows the route; the fog is testing how much he trusts it.
rows.text: Die foon ken die roete; die mis toets hoeveel hy dit vertrou.
rows.back: The phone knows the route; the mist is testing how much it trusts it.
rows.note: unsure: 'hoeveel hy dit vertrou' — 'hy' should be the phone (the phone trusting the route?) but the natural sense would be how much YOU trust the phone; reads muddled

rows.en: Walking to the bin is now an expedition.
rows.text: Stap na die asblik is nou 'n ekspedisie.
rows.back: Walking to the bin is now an expedition.

rows.en: The world ends two metres past the gate.
rows.text: Die wêreld eindig twee meter verby die hek.
rows.back: The world ends two metres past the gate.

rows.en: Gown, slippers, thirty metres of visibility: bin day waits for no weather.
rows.text: Kamerjas, pantoffels, dertig meter sig: vullisdag wag vir geen weer nie.
rows.back: Dressing gown, slippers, thirty metres of visibility: bin day waits for no weather.

rows.en: Kickoff is ten and the far posts have not arrived yet.
rows.text: Afskop is tien en die verste pale het nog nie opgedaag nie.
rows.back: Kick-off is at ten and the far posts haven't shown up yet.

rows.en: Visibility: basically zero.
rows.text: Sigbaarheid: basies nul.
rows.back: Visibility: basically zero.

rows.en: Found: one ball. The other three hundred metres of golf course are still missing.
rows.text: Gevind: een bal. Die ander driehonderd meter gholfbaan is steeds vermis.
rows.back: Found: one ball. The other three hundred metres of golf course are still missing.

rows.en: The fairway is out there somewhere, taking the morning off from being visible.
rows.text: Die baan is daar êrens, maar hy wys hom nie vanoggend nie.
rows.back: The course is out there somewhere, but it's not showing itself this morning.

rows.en: Somewhere out there is the road. We think.
rows.text: Iewers daarbuite is die pad. Ons dink.
rows.back: Somewhere out there is the road. We think.

rows.en: Your high beams are making it worse, boet.
rows.text: Jou brights maak dit erger, boet.
rows.back: Your brights are making it worse, boet.

rows.en: Headlights do about twenty metres out here; the rest is memory and respect.
rows.text: Ligte haal omtrent twintig meter hier; die res is geheue en respek.
rows.back: Lights reach about twenty metres here; the rest is memory and respect.

rows.en: The dog doesn't understand where the world went. Same, boy. Same.
rows.text: Die hond verstaan nie waar die wêreld heen is nie. Ons ook nie, boytjie. Ons ook nie.
rows.back: The dog doesn't understand where the world has gone. Neither do we, boytjie. Neither do we.

rows.en: Every streetlamp gets its own halo tonight; the fog is generous like that.
rows.text: Elke straatlig kry vanaand sy eie stralekrans; die mis is so vrygewig.
rows.back: Every streetlight gets its own halo tonight; the mist is that generous.

rows.en: Perfect weather to bump into someone you've 'been meaning to call'.
rows.text: Perfekte weer om iemand raak te loop wat jy 'nog wou bel'.
rows.back: Perfect weather to bump into someone you 'still meant to call'.

rows.en: Five metres of visibility. Same as your five-year plan.
rows.text: Vyf meter sig. Nes jou vyfjaarplan.
rows.back: Five metres of visibility. Just like your five-year plan.

rows.en: The fog swallowed the whole street and left the tail lights as a receipt.
rows.text: Die mis het die hele straat gesluk en die agterligte as kwitansie gelos.
rows.back: The mist swallowed the whole street and left the tail-lights as a receipt.

rows.en: The fog took the city but it is not getting the Bo-Kaap's colours.
rows.text: Die mis het die stad gevat, maar die Bo-Kaap se kleure kry hy nie.
rows.back: The mist took the city, but it's not getting the Bo-Kaap's colours.

rows.en: They turned the lights on. Fog turned everything else off.
rows.text: Hulle het die ligte aangesit. Die mis het al die res afgesit.
rows.back: They switched the lights on. The mist has switched everything else off.

rows.en: Pretty evening, if you like walls.
rows.text: Mooi aand, as jy van mure hou.
rows.back: Lovely evening, if you like walls.

rows.en: The street signs gave up.
rows.text: Die straatborde het tou opgegooi.
rows.back: The street signs have thrown in the towel.

rows.en: The fog got to the lookout first and took the whole view for itself.
rows.text: Die mis was eerste by die uitkykpunt en het die hele uitsig vir homself gevat.
rows.back: The mist got to the lookout point first and took the whole view for itself.

rows.en: Last taxis of the night, and the fog has the whole rank to itself soon.
rows.text: Laaste taxi's van die aand, en die mis het binnekort die hele staanplek vir homself.
rows.back: Last taxis of the evening, and soon the mist will have the whole rank to itself.

rows.en: Your car is out there. Somewhere. Probably.
rows.text: Jou kar is daarbuite. Iewers. Waarskynlik.
rows.back: Your car is out there. Somewhere. Probably.

rows.en: Ghost town. But it's just Tuesday.
rows.text: Spookdorp. Maar dis net Dinsdag.
rows.back: Ghost town. And it's only Tuesday.
rows.note: 'Maar dis net Dinsdag' = but it's only Tuesday

rows.en: Fog so thick it has opinions.
rows.text: Mis so dik dit het menings.
rows.back: Mist so thick it has opinions.

rows.en: The fog is so thick even the robot is hedging its bets.
rows.text: Die mis is so dik dat selfs die robot nie kleur wil beken nie.
rows.back: The mist is so thick even the robot won't admit to a colour.

rows.en: Cape Town just got a dimmer switch.
rows.text: Kaapstad het 'n dimmer skakelaar gekry.
rows.back: Cape Town got a dimmer switch.

rows.en: Cape Town is still on under there; the fog is just running interference.
rows.text: Kaapstad is nog aan daaronder; die mis staan net in die pad.
rows.back: Cape Town is still on under there; the mist is just in the way.

rows.en: Perfect weather for a horror movie.
rows.text: Perfekte weer vir n horror movie.
rows.back: Perfect weather for a horror movie.
rows.note: 'n' missing its apostrophe; 'horror movie' left in English
rows.reason: Meaning matches; orthography note only: 'n' lacks its apostrophe ('n).

rows.en: Everything looks like a film scene. A creepy one.
rows.text: Alles lyk soos 'n filmtoneel. 'n Grillerige een.
rows.back: Everything looks like a scene from a film. A creepy one.

rows.en: Visibility: vibes only.
rows.text: Sigbaarheid: net vibes.
rows.back: Visibility: just vibes.

rows.en: The fog moved in an hour ago and the streetlights have doubled in size since.
rows.text: Die mis het 'n uur gelede ingetrek en die straatligte het sedertdien verdubbel.
rows.back: The mist moved in an hour ago and the streetlights have doubled since.
rows.reason: 'het sedertdien verdubbel' drops 'in size', so it reads as the number of streetlights doubled rather than their fog-halo growing.
reasons: DRIFT: 'het sedertdien verdubbel' drops 'in size', so it reads as the number of streetlights doubled rather than their fog-halo growing.

rows.en: Let's call it atmosphere and go inside.
rows.text: Kom ons noem dit atmosfeer en gaan in.
rows.back: Let's call it atmosphere and go inside.

rows.en: That one window is doing lighthouse duty tonight, and it is enough.
rows.text: Daardie een venster staan vanaand vuurtoringdiens, en dit is genoeg.
rows.back: That one window is on lighthouse duty tonight, and that's enough.

rows.en: Joburg does fog so rarely it feels like a limited edition.
rows.text: Joburg doen mis so selde dat dit soos 'n spesiale uitgawe voel.
rows.back: Joburg does mist so rarely it feels like a special edition.

rows.en: The city noise is off tonight; fog is the best soundproofing there is.
rows.text: Die stadsgeraas is vanaand af; mis is die beste klankdemping wat daar is.
rows.back: The city noise is off tonight; mist is the best soundproofing there is.

rows.en: The sun has just come up, which is the part nobody is going to believe.
rows.text: Die son het nou eers opgekom. Dís die deel wat niemand gaan glo nie.
rows.back: The sun has only just come up. That's the part nobody's going to believe.

rows.en: That bonnet did not cool down overnight, which is the part that should worry you.
rows.text: Daardie enjinkap het nie oornag afgekoel nie, en dít is die deel wat jou moet bekommer.
rows.back: That bonnet didn't cool down overnight, and that's the part that should worry you.

rows.en: That egg has been on there about four minutes and it is nearly done.
rows.text: Daardie eier is omtrent vier minute daarop en dit is amper gaar.
rows.back: That egg's been on there about four minutes and it's almost cooked.
rows.note: on what — presumably a car bonnet

rows.en: Nobody in this dorp has needed a stove since about the second week of December.
rows.text: Niemand in hierdie dorp het sedert omtrent die tweede week van Desember 'n stoof nodig gehad nie.
rows.back: Nobody in this town has needed a stove since about the second week of December.

rows.en: Monday, and breakfast in this dorp has been sorted by a car bonnet.
rows.text: Maandag, en ontbyt in hierdie dorp is deur 'n enjinkap afgehandel.
rows.back: Monday, and breakfast in this town has been taken care of by a car bonnet.

rows.en: 6am and the sun is already done warming up. That wasn't a warm-up, that was a warning.
rows.text: 06:00 en die son is klaar klaar met opwarm. Dit was nie 'n opwarming nie, dit was 'n waarskuwing.
rows.back: 06:00 and the sun has already finished warming up. That wasn't a warm-up, it was a warning.
rows.note: 'klaar klaar' doubled — emphatic 'already done' or a typo

rows.en: The berg wind turned overnight. Cape Town, today you're basically Upington.
rows.text: Die bergwind het in die nag gedraai. Kaapstad, vandag is jy Upington.
rows.back: The berg wind turned in the night. Cape Town, today you're Upington.

rows.en: That water went in cold at five and it has not been cold since.
rows.text: Daardie water het vyfuur koud ingegaan en was sedertdien nie weer koud nie.
rows.back: That water went in cold at five o'clock and hasn't been cold since.
rows.note: unsure: 'het vyfuur koud ingegaan' — the water was cold when it went in (filled at five?) — literal and odd

rows.en: He got in before the sun cleared the fence and he has not come out.
rows.text: Hy het ingeklim voor die son die heining verby was en het nie weer uitgekom nie.
rows.back: He got in before the sun cleared the fence and hasn't come out since.

rows.en: He got in at six and he is not planning to get out.
rows.text: Hy het sesuur ingeklim en is nie van plan om uit te klim nie.
rows.back: He got in at six o'clock and has no intention of getting out.

rows.en: That water was cold about forty minutes ago and nobody has topped it up.
rows.text: Daardie water was omtrent veertig minute gelede koud en niemand het dit bygevul nie.
rows.back: That water was cold about forty minutes ago and nobody has topped it up.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'bygevul' — not found in any external source; closest attested: 'bygeval' (1× leipzig/hunspell, distance 1)

rows.en: The pool is not optional.
rows.text: Die swembad is nie opsioneel nie.
rows.back: The pool is not optional.

rows.en: Funny how everyone suddenly remembers they love you when you own a pool.
rows.text: Snaaks hoe almal skielik onthou hulle is lief vir jou wanneer jy 'n swembad het.
rows.back: Funny how everyone suddenly remembers they love you when you have a pool.

rows.en: They are out at half past five because there is no other window today.
rows.text: Hulle is halfses al uit, want vandag is daar geen ander kans nie.
rows.back: They were out by half past five, because today there's no other chance.

rows.en: That sun has been up eleven minutes and it is already doing that.
rows.text: Daardie son is elf minute op en doen dit reeds.
rows.back: That sun has been up eleven minutes and is already doing it.
rows.note: 'doen dit reeds' = already at it (already blazing) — vague

rows.en: Nobody is carrying water, which is a decision they are going to revisit.
rows.text: Niemand dra water nie, en dit is 'n besluit wat hulle weer gaan oorweeg.
rows.back: Nobody's carrying water, and that's a decision they're going to reconsider.

rows.en: The shade on this road runs out in about two hundred metres.
rows.text: Die skaduwee op hierdie pad raak oor omtrent tweehonderd meter op.
rows.back: The shade on this road runs out in about two hundred metres.

rows.en: Wednesday, and this is the coolest it is going to be all day.
rows.text: Woensdag, en koeler as nou word dit vandag nie.
rows.back: Wednesday, and it's not going to get any cooler than this today.

rows.en: 6:30 and the tar is already considering melting.
rows.text: 06:30 en die teer dink al aan smelt.
rows.back: 06:30 and the tar is already thinking about melting.

rows.en: He has picked the shade under a thorn tree, which is barely shade at all.
rows.text: Hy het die skaduwee onder 'n doringboom gekies, wat skaars skaduwee is.
rows.back: He picked the shade under a thorn tree, which is barely shade.

rows.en: The sun has been up eleven minutes and he has already stopped moving.
rows.text: Die son is elf minute op en hy het reeds opgehou beweeg.
rows.back: The sun has been up eleven minutes and he's already stopped moving.
rows.note: 'hy' = a person/animal in the photo, or the sun itself — ambiguous

rows.en: That stoep has chairs on it and none of them will be used before six.
rows.text: Daardie stoep het stoele op en nie een gaan voor sesuur gebruik word nie.
rows.back: That stoep has chairs out and not one will be used before six o'clock.

rows.en: Thursday, and by nine there will be nothing out here worth walking to.
rows.text: Donderdag, en teen nege gaan daar niks hier buite wees wat 'n stap werd is nie.
rows.back: Thursday, and by nine there'll be nothing out here worth walking.

rows.en: There is no shade on this whole werf that lasts past about ten.
rows.text: Daar is nie een stukkie skaduwee op hierdie werf wat ná tienuur nog oor is nie.
rows.back: There isn't one scrap of shade in this yard that's still left after ten o'clock.

rows.en: Move slowly. Speak slowly. Survive.
rows.text: Beweeg stadig. Praat stadig. Oorleef.
rows.back: Move slowly. Talk slowly. Survive.

rows.en: The shade is working harder than you today.
rows.text: Die skaduwee werk harder as jy vandag.
rows.back: The shade is working harder than you today.

rows.en: The sprinkler goes on at five and it is off again by seven.
rows.text: Die sproeier gaan vyfuur aan en is teen sewe weer af.
rows.back: The sprinkler comes on at five and is off again by seven.

rows.en: Everything green in this photograph is on a timer and everything else is not.
rows.text: Alles wat groen is in hierdie foto is op 'n timer en al die res nie.
rows.back: Everything green in this photo is on a timer, and everything else isn't.

rows.en: The aloes have not needed a drop of that and they never will.
rows.text: Die aalwyne het nie 'n druppel daarvan nodig gehad nie en sal ook nooit nie.
rows.back: The aloes didn't need a drop of it and never will.

rows.en: That lawn is the only thing for forty kilometres that gets a say.
rows.text: Daardie grasperk is die enigste ding vir veertig kilometer wat 'n sê het.
rows.back: That lawn is the only thing for forty kilometres that has a say.
rows.note: unsure: ''n sê het' = has a say / a voice — meaning unclear (the only green thing?)

rows.en: Friday, and by eleven this whole ridge will be one colour again.
rows.text: Vrydag, en teen elf gaan hierdie hele rant weer een kleur wees.
rows.back: Friday, and by eleven this whole ridge will be one colour again.

rows.en: There is steam coming off that pool, which is not a good sign at six.
rows.text: Daar kom stoom van daardie swembad af, wat nie 'n goeie teken is om sesuur nie.
rows.back: There's steam coming off that pool, which isn't a good sign at six o'clock.

rows.en: The water did not cool down last night and he has already checked.
rows.text: Die water het nie gisteraand afgekoel nie en hy het al gaan kyk.
rows.back: The water didn't cool down last night and he's already been to check.

rows.en: Saturday, and he is in before seven because by ten it is unusable.
rows.text: Saterdag, en hy is voor sewe in, want teen tien is dit onbruikbaar.
rows.back: Saturday, and he's in before seven, because by ten it's unusable.

rows.en: The paving round that pool is already too hot for bare feet at six.
rows.text: Die plaveisel om daardie swembad is sesuur al te warm vir kaal voete.
rows.back: The paving around that pool is already too hot for bare feet at six.

rows.en: That pool is warmer than he is and it is going to stay that way.
rows.text: Daardie swembad is warmer as hy en dit gaan so bly.
rows.back: That pool is warmer than he is and it's going to stay that way.

rows.en: She has found the one tile in this house that has not warmed up yet.
rows.text: Sy het die een teël in hierdie huis gekry wat nog nie warm geword het nie.
rows.back: She found the one tile in this house that hasn't warmed up yet.

rows.en: She is lying on tile rather than anything soft, and that was a decision.
rows.text: Sy lê op teël eerder as op iets sags, en dit was 'n besluit.
rows.back: She's lying on tile instead of something soft, and that was a decision.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'sags' is an English word with no af attestation and is not in the English source line

rows.en: By nine that windowsill is going to be the worst place in the house.
rows.text: Teen nege gaan daardie vensterbank die ergste plek in die huis wees.
rows.back: By nine that windowsill will be the worst spot in the house.

rows.en: The sun is only just up and she has already picked her spot.
rows.text: Die son is skaars op en sy het haar plek reeds gekies.
rows.back: The sun is barely up and she's already chosen her spot.

rows.en: Sunday, and she has about ninety minutes before she has to move again.
rows.text: Sondag, en sy het omtrent negentig minute voor sy weer moet skuif.
rows.back: Sunday, and she has about ninety minutes before she has to move again.

rows.en: Your makeup has an expiry date of 9am.
rows.text: Jou grimering se vervaldatum is 9vm.
rows.back: Your make-up's expiry date is 9am.

rows.en: That bonnet is hotter than most pans ever get on most stoves.
rows.text: Daardie enjinkap is warmer as wat die meeste panne ooit op die meeste stowe word.
rows.back: That bonnet is hotter than most pans ever get on most stoves.

rows.en: He tried the roof first and the roof was somehow hotter.
rows.text: Hy het eers die dak probeer en die dak was op een of ander manier warmer.
rows.back: He tried the roof first and the roof was somehow hotter.

rows.en: Nobody has touched that car door and every one of them knows why.
rows.text: Niemand het nog aan daardie kardeur geraak nie en elkeen van hulle weet hoekom.
rows.back: Nobody has touched that car door yet and every one of them knows why.

findings: MEDIUM morphology: negation 'Niemand' without the closing 'nie' at the end of the clause

rows.en: Nobody here is wondering whether it works. They are watching it work.
rows.text: Niemand hier wonder of dit werk nie. Hulle kyk hoe dit werk.
rows.back: Nobody here is wondering whether it works. They're watching it work.

rows.en: Monday, and it is not even eleven o'clock yet, which is the frightening part.
rows.text: Maandag, en dis nie eers elfuur nie, en dít is die skrikwekkende deel.
rows.back: Monday, and it's not even eleven o'clock yet, and that's the frightening part.

rows.en: The ice cream van is playing everyone's anthem.
rows.text: Die roomyswa speel almal se volkslied.
rows.back: The ice-cream van is playing everyone's national anthem.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'roomyswa' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source; closest attested: 'roomys' (59× kaikki/leipzig/hunspell, distance 2)

rows.en: 35 in the shade. In the sun, nobody's counting anymore.
rows.text: 35 in die skadu. In die son tel niemand meer nie.
rows.back: 35 in the shade. In the sun nobody's counting any more.

rows.en: Two fans moving hot air around a room that has been shut since eight.
rows.text: Twee waaiers wat warm lug rondskuif in 'n kamer wat sedert agt toe is.
rows.back: Two fans pushing hot air around a room that's been shut since eight.

rows.en: The file she is fanning with is the one she is meant to be reading.
rows.text: Die lêer waarmee sy koelte waai is die een wat sy veronderstel is om te lees.
rows.back: The file she's fanning herself with is the one she's supposed to be reading.

rows.en: Two fans, four papers flying, and not one document has been read today.
rows.text: Twee waaiers, vier papiere wat vlieg, en nie een dokument is vandag gelees nie.
rows.back: Two fans, four papers flying, and not one document has been read today.

rows.en: Nobody in that building can open a window and every one of them has tried.
rows.text: Niemand in daardie gebou kan 'n venster oopmaak nie en elkeen van hulle het probeer.
rows.back: Nobody in that building can open a window and every one of them has tried.

findings: MEDIUM morphology: negation 'Niemand' without the closing 'nie' at the end of the clause

rows.en: Tuesday, and somebody in this building is going to be sent home early.
rows.text: Dinsdag, en iemand in hierdie gebou gaan vroeg huis toe gestuur word.
rows.back: Tuesday, and someone in this building is going to be sent home early.

rows.en: The office aircon war has begun.
rows.text: Die kantoor-aircon oorlog het begin.
rows.back: The office aircon war has begun.

rows.en: The aircon remote is now public property. Negotiate.
rows.text: Die aircon-afstandsbeheer is nou openbare eiendom. Onderhandel.
rows.back: The aircon remote is now public property. Negotiate.

rows.en: That is the only cool water in this garden and it has been claimed.
rows.text: Dit is die enigste koel water in hierdie tuin en dit is opgeëis.
rows.back: This is the only cool water in this garden and it's been claimed.

rows.en: He has not moved out of it since eleven and he is not going to.
rows.text: Hy het sedert elfuur nie daaruit beweeg nie en gaan ook nie.
rows.back: He hasn't moved out of it since eleven and isn't going to.

rows.en: There is a whole garden out there and about a metre of it is bearable.
rows.text: Daar is 'n hele tuin daar buite en omtrent 'n meter daarvan is draaglik.
rows.back: There's a whole garden out there and about a metre of it is bearable.

rows.en: The pool is already fully booked. By everyone. For the whole day.
rows.text: Die swembad is reeds bespreek. Deur almal. Vir die hele dag.
rows.back: The pool is already booked. By everyone. For the whole day.

rows.en: Too hot to argue. Too hot to function.
rows.text: Te warm om te stry. Te warm om te funksioneer.
rows.back: Too hot to argue. Too hot to function.

rows.en: Everyone with a pool just became very popular.
rows.text: Almal met 'n swembad het skielik baie populêr geword.
rows.back: Everyone with a pool has suddenly become very popular.

rows.en: The A/C button is right there and it has clearly not been pressed.
rows.text: Die aircon-knoppie is reg daar en dit is duidelik nog nie gedruk nie.
rows.back: The aircon button is right there and it clearly hasn't been pressed yet.

rows.en: Whoever left that there thought they would only be twenty minutes.
rows.text: Wie ook al dit daar gelos het, het gedink hulle sal net twintig minute wees.
rows.back: Whoever left it there thought they'd only be twenty minutes.

rows.en: That dashboard is hot enough that the wrapper gave up before the chocolate did.
rows.text: Daardie dashboard is so warm dat die papiertjie voor die sjokolade moed opgegee het.
rows.back: That dashboard is so hot the wrapper on the chocolate has given up.
rows.note: unsure: 'die papiertjie voor die sjokolade' = the little paper in front of/around the chocolate — phrasing odd
rows.reason: 'die papiertjie voor die sjokolade moed opgegee het' reads as 'the wrapper in front of the chocolate gave up', so the 'gave up before the chocolate did' punchline is blurred.
reasons: DRIFT: 'die papiertjie voor die sjokolade moed opgegee het' reads as 'the wrapper in front of the chocolate gave up', so the 'gave up before the chocolate did' punchline is blurred.

rows.en: The steering wheel in there is currently not something you can hold.
rows.text: Die stuurwiel daarin is op die oomblik nie iets wat jy kan vashou nie.
rows.back: The steering wheel in there is currently not something you can hold.

rows.en: Thursday, and that car is going to be worse at four than it is now.
rows.text: Donderdag, en daardie kar gaan vieruur erger wees as nou.
rows.back: Thursday, and that car will be worse at four o'clock than it is now.

rows.en: Somewhere a chocolate bar just died.
rows.text: Iewers het 'n sjokolade net gesterf.
rows.back: Somewhere a chocolate just died.

rows.en: Hotter than a bakkie dashboard at noon.
rows.text: Warmer as 'n bakkie se dashboard teen middag.
rows.back: Hotter than a bakkie's dashboard at midday.

rows.en: He came out of the cage, and he did not come out for the view.
rows.text: Hy het uit die hok gekom, en hy het nie vir die uitsig uitgekom nie.
rows.back: He came out of the kennel, and he didn't come out for the view.

rows.en: Nobody on this stoep is going anywhere until about four o'clock.
rows.text: Niemand op hierdie stoep gaan enige plek heen voor omtrent vieruur nie.
rows.back: Nobody on this stoep is going anywhere before about four o'clock.

rows.en: Friday, and that is the only moving air for about sixty kilometres.
rows.text: Vrydag, en dit is die enigste bewegende lug vir omtrent sestig kilometer.
rows.back: Friday, and this is the only moving air for about sixty kilometres.

rows.en: You're not sweating. You're 'glowing'. Sure.
rows.text: Jy sweet nie. Jy 'glow'. Ja, reg.
rows.back: You're not sweating. You're 'glowing'. Yeah, right.

rows.en: Jislaaik, it's properly hot!
rows.text: Jinne, dis ordentlik warm!
rows.back: Jinne, it's properly hot!

rows.en: That number has not moved in eighty kilometres and neither has the scenery.
rows.text: Daardie syfer het in tagtig kilometer nie geroer nie, en die uitsig ook nie.
rows.back: That number hasn't budged in eighty kilometres, and neither has the view.

rows.en: The aircon is losing and everyone in this car has stopped talking about it.
rows.text: Die aircon verloor, en almal in hierdie kar het opgehou om daaroor te praat.
rows.back: The aircon is losing, and everyone in this car has stopped talking about it.

rows.en: Saturday, and the only shade for the next hour is inside this car.
rows.text: Saterdag, en die enigste skaduwee vir die volgende uur is binne hierdie kar.
rows.back: Saturday, and the only shade for the next hour is inside this car.

rows.en: Somebody said the padkos would be fine in the boot. Somebody was wrong.
rows.text: Iemand het gesê die padkos sal oukei wees in die kattebak. Iemand was mis.
rows.back: Someone said the padkos would be fine in the boot. Someone was wrong.

rows.en: The road ahead has been the same road for a very long time.
rows.text: Die pad vorentoe is al 'n baie lang tyd dieselfde pad.
rows.back: The road ahead has been the same road for a very long time.

rows.en: Your car seat is a weapon right now.
rows.text: Jou karsitplek is 'n wapen nou.
rows.back: Your car seat is a weapon now.

rows.en: Your steering wheel is a hot plate.
rows.text: Jou stuurwiel is 'n warmplaat.
rows.back: Your steering wheel is a hotplate.

rows.en: That sprinkler has been the best-value thing in this garden all summer.
rows.text: Daardie sproeier is die hele somer die beste waarde in hierdie tuin.
rows.back: That sprinkler is the best value in this garden all summer.

rows.en: Those two on the stoep have made their choice and they are sticking with it.
rows.text: Daardie twee op die stoep het hul keuse gemaak en hulle bly daarby.
rows.back: Those two on the stoep have made their choice and they're sticking to it.

rows.en: Nobody is going to remember the temperature, only the sprinkler.
rows.text: Niemand gaan die temperatuur onthou nie, net die sproeier.
rows.back: Nobody's going to remember the temperature, only the sprinkler.

rows.en: Sunday, and the water bill has already quietly accepted its fate.
rows.text: Sondag, en die waterrekening het sy lot reeds stilweg aanvaar.
rows.back: Sunday, and the water bill has quietly accepted its fate.

rows.en: The lawn is taking a beating that has nothing to do with the sun.
rows.text: Die grasperk kry pak wat niks met die son te doen het nie.
rows.back: The lawn is taking a hiding that has nothing to do with the sun.

rows.en: Every leaf on that sunflower has given up and the head is still facing it.
rows.text: Elke blaar aan daardie sonneblom het moed opgegee en die kop kyk dit steeds in die oë.
rows.back: Every leaf on that sunflower has given up and the head is still looking it in the eye.
