rows.text: Die maan is uit en die palms het sedert sonsak nie opgehou beweeg nie.
rows.back: The moon is out and the palms haven't stopped moving since sunset.

rows.en: The moon is holding still and everything else up there is not.
rows.text: Die maan hou stil en al die res daarbo nie.
rows.back: The moon is holding still and everything else up there isn't.
rows.note: elliptical grammar: 'al die res daarbo nie' — understood as 'the rest up there isn't'

rows.en: Whatever is landing on that road is not rain, it is the sea arriving sideways.
rows.text: Wat ook al op daardie pad land is nie reën nie, dit is die see wat sywaarts aankom.
rows.back: Whatever is landing on that road isn't rain, it's the sea coming in sideways.

rows.en: The palms have been making that noise for hours and nobody is awake to mind.
rows.text: Die palms maak al ure daardie geraas en niemand is wakker om om te gee nie.
rows.back: The palms have been making that racket for hours and nobody's awake to care.

rows.en: The road is empty, every light is on, and the wind has the place to itself.
rows.text: Die pad is leeg, elke lig is aan, en die wind het die plek vir homself.
rows.back: The road is empty, every light is on, and the wind has the place to itself.

rows.en: The leaves came in. The cat did not go out.
rows.text: Die blare het ingekom. Die kat het nie uitgegaan nie.
rows.back: The leaves came in. The cat didn't go out.

rows.en: The wind has been delivering leaves to that doormat all evening.
rows.text: Die wind lewer die hele aand blare by daardie deurmat af.
rows.back: The wind has been delivering leaves to that doormat all evening.

rows.en: Every leaf on that mat arrived without being invited.
rows.text: Elke blaar op daardie mat het opgedaag sonder 'n uitnodiging.
rows.back: Every leaf on that mat showed up without an invitation.

rows.en: The garden is moving and he has decided the doorway is far enough.
rows.text: Die tuin beweeg en hy het besluit die deur is ver genoeg.
rows.back: The garden is moving and he's decided the door is far enough.

rows.en: The wind is bringing the outside in and he is letting it come to him.
rows.text: Die wind bring die buitekant in en hy laat dit na hom toe kom.
rows.back: The wind is bringing the outside in and he's letting it come to him.

rows.en: Tonight's wind has opinions.
rows.text: Vanaand se wind het opinies.
rows.back: Tonight's wind has opinions.

rows.en: The mountain has its cloth on and the palm is holding the pose.
rows.text: Die berg het sy tafeldoek op en die palm hou die houding.
rows.back: The mountain has its tablecloth on and the palm is holding the pose.

rows.en: Wednesday, and the Cape Doctor is doing its rounds a little early.
rows.text: Woensdag, en die Kaapse Dokter doen sy rondtes 'n bietjie vroeg.
rows.back: Wednesday, and the Cape Doctor is doing his rounds a bit early.

rows.en: Nobody walks this road at this hour, and tonight nobody wants to.
rows.text: Niemand loop hierdie pad op hierdie uur nie, en vanaand wil niemand ook nie.
rows.back: Nobody walks this road at this hour, and tonight nobody wants to either.

rows.en: That palm has been bent that way so long it thinks it is upright.
rows.text: Daardie palm is al so lank so gebuig dat hy dink hy staan regop.
rows.back: That palm has been bent like that for so long it thinks it's standing up straight.

rows.en: The whole street is inside pretending the roof noise is normal.
rows.text: Die hele straat is binne en maak asof die dakgeraas normaal is.
rows.back: The whole street is indoors, pretending the noise on the roof is normal.

rows.en: The Cape Doctor is on night shift. The whole street has an appointment.
rows.text: Die Kaapse Dokter werk nagskof. Die hele straat het 'n afspraak.
rows.back: The Cape Doctor is on night shift. The whole street has an appointment.

rows.en: The palm is the only one still outside, and it regrets everything.
rows.text: Die palm is die enigste een wat nog buite is, en hy is spyt oor alles.
rows.back: The palm is the only one still outside, and it regrets everything.

rows.en: The southeaster doesn’t knock. You’ll hear it under the door all night.
rows.text: Die suidooster klop nie. Jy gaan hom die hele nag onder die deur hoor.
rows.back: The south-easter doesn't knock. You'll hear it under the door all night.

rows.en: The aloe is not moving and has no intention of starting now.
rows.text: Die aalwyn beweeg nie en is glad nie van plan om nou te begin nie.
rows.back: The aloe isn't moving and has no intention of starting now.

rows.en: That thorn tree has been leaning since before anyone on this street arrived.
rows.text: Daardie doringboom leun al van voor enigiemand in hierdie straat aangekom het.
rows.back: That thorn tree has been leaning since before anyone in this street arrived.

rows.en: The dust is going somewhere and it is not asking permission.
rows.text: Die stof gaan êrens heen en dit vra nie verlof nie.
rows.back: The dust is going somewhere and it isn't asking permission.

rows.en: Northern Cape wind does not howl. It leans on things until they give.
rows.text: Noord-Kaapse wind huil nie. Hy leun op goed tot hulle meegee.
rows.back: Northern Cape wind doesn't howl. It leans on things until they give in.

rows.en: Everything out here is either properly rooted or already gone.
rows.text: Alles hier buite is óf behoorlik gewortel óf reeds weg.
rows.back: Everything out here is either properly rooted or already gone.

rows.en: Sleep tight. The wind will watch the house. Loudly.
rows.text: Slaap lekker. Die wind sal die huis oppas. Hard.
rows.back: Sleep tight. The wind will look after the house. Loudly.

rows.en: The banner is holding on better than the palms and it knows it.
rows.text: Die banier hou beter vas as die palms en dit weet dit.
rows.back: The banner is holding on better than the palms and it knows it.

rows.en: Friday night on the promenade and the sea has cleared everyone's diary.
rows.text: Vrydagaand op die promenade en die see het almal se dagboek skoongemaak.
rows.back: Friday evening on the promenade and the sea has cleared everyone's diary.

rows.en: Every palm on this strip is pointing at the same thing tonight.
rows.text: Elke palm op hierdie strook wys vanaand na dieselfde ding.
rows.back: Every palm on this strip is pointing at the same thing tonight.

rows.en: The city across the water is having a completely different evening.
rows.text: Die stad oorkant die water het 'n heeltemal ander aand.
rows.back: The city across the water is having a completely different evening.

rows.en: Nobody is walking that promenade tonight and the lights know it.
rows.text: Niemand stap vanaand op daardie promenade nie, en die ligte weet dit.
rows.back: Nobody's walking on that promenade tonight, and the lights know it.

rows.en: The sparks are going sideways and the tongs are still going in.
rows.text: Die vonke gaan sywaarts en die tang gaan steeds in.
rows.back: The sparks are going sideways and the tongs are still going in.

rows.en: Table Mountain, a braai, and a wind with its own strong opinion.
rows.text: Tafelberg, 'n braai, en 'n wind met sy eie sterk mening.
rows.back: Table Mountain, a braai, and a wind with a strong opinion of its own.

rows.en: Saturday, and neither of them will admit the wind is winning.
rows.text: Saterdag, en nie een van hulle wil erken die wind wen nie.
rows.back: Saturday, and not one of them wants to admit the wind is winning.

rows.en: The tongs are out, so the argument about who cooks is over.
rows.text: Die tang is uit, so die argument oor wie braai is verby.
rows.back: The tongs are out, so the argument about who's braaiing is over.

rows.en: Those coals are doing more for the fence than they are for the meat.
rows.text: Daardie kole doen meer vir die heining as vir die vleis.
rows.back: Those coals are doing more for the fence than for the meat.

rows.en: Somebody is going to remember that washing at about two in the morning.
rows.text: Iemand gaan omtrent tweeuur die oggend aan daardie wasgoed dink.
rows.back: Someone is going to think about that washing at about two in the morning.

rows.en: That hedge has been leaning like that since Thursday and it is not straightening.
rows.text: Daardie heining leun al van Donderdag af so, en dit gaan nie regop kom nie.
rows.back: That fence has been leaning like that since Thursday, and it's not coming back upright.

rows.en: The security light is picking up things you would rather not watch moving.
rows.text: Die sekuriteitslig vang goed op wat jy liewer nie wil sien beweeg nie.
rows.back: The security light is picking up things you'd rather not see moving.

rows.en: Sunday night, and even the washing is refusing to accept it.
rows.text: Sondagaand, en selfs die wasgoed weier om dit te aanvaar.
rows.back: Sunday evening, and even the washing refuses to accept it.
rows.note: unclear what 'dit' refers to (the weekend ending? the wind?)

rows.en: Whatever is not pegged down out there is already somebody else's problem.
rows.text: Wat ook al nie daar buite vasgemaak is nie, is reeds iemand anders se probleem.
rows.back: Whatever isn't tied down out there is already someone else's problem.

rows.en: The trampoline has relocated and taken the neighbour's wall as a partner.
rows.text: Die trampolien het verhuis en die buurman se muur as maat gevat.
rows.back: The trampoline has moved house and taken the neighbour's wall as a partner.

rows.en: Somebody is going to be explaining that to somebody else this evening.
rows.text: Iemand gaan dit vanaand aan iemand anders moet verduidelik.
rows.back: Someone is going to have to explain this to someone else tonight.

rows.en: Monday, and the garden has rearranged itself without asking anyone.
rows.text: Maandag, en die tuin het homself herrangskik sonder om iemand te vra.
rows.back: Monday, and the garden rearranged itself without asking anyone.

rows.en: The palms are fine. The trampoline had opinions about staying put.
rows.text: Die palms staan nog. Die trampolien het ander idees gehad.
rows.back: The palms are still standing. The trampoline had other ideas.

rows.en: It took the wind four seconds to move what took two hours to build.
rows.text: Die wind het in vier sekondes weggewaai wat twee uur geneem het om te bou.
rows.back: In four seconds the wind blew away what took two hours to build.

rows.en: Someone's trampoline is now two streets away.
rows.text: Iemand se trampoline is nou twee strate weg.
rows.back: Someone's trampoline is now two streets away.
rows.note: 'trampoline' in English spelling; neighbouring rows use Afrikaans 'trampolien'
rows.reason: spelling only: 'trampoline' (English form) vs 'trampolien' in 1482/1485

rows.en: The bin made it to the pavement and then made its own decisions.
rows.text: Die vullisblik het tot by die sypaadjie gekom en toe self besluit.
rows.back: The wheelie bin made it as far as the pavement and then made its own decision.

rows.en: Tuesday is bin day, and the wind has clearly read the schedule too.
rows.text: Dinsdag is vullisdag, en die wind het duidelik ook die rooster gelees.
rows.back: Tuesday is bin day, and the wind clearly read the schedule too.

rows.en: Half of this street's recycling is now the hedge's problem.
rows.text: Die helfte van hierdie straat se herwinning is nou die heining se probleem.
rows.back: Half this street's recycling is now the fence's problem.

rows.en: The oaks are fine. The wheelie bins never stood a chance.
rows.text: Die eike is oukei. Die vullisdromme het nooit 'n kans gestaan nie.
rows.back: The oaks are okay. The wheelie bins never stood a chance.

rows.en: Three houses are out there picking up what the wind redistributed.
rows.text: Drie huishoudings is buite besig om op te tel wat die wind herverdeel het.
rows.back: Three households are outside picking up what the wind redistributed.

rows.en: Every jacaranda on this street is emptying itself onto one man.
rows.text: Elke jakaranda in hierdie straat maak homself op een man leeg.
rows.back: Every jacaranda in this street is emptying itself onto one man.

rows.en: That tie has been horizontal since he left the car.
rows.text: Daardie das waai al horisontaal vandat hy uit die kar geklim het.
rows.back: That tie has been blowing horizontal since he got out of the car.

rows.en: He will be finding purple in that jacket pocket until Friday.
rows.text: Hy gaan tot Vrydag pers in daardie baadjiesak kry.
rows.back: He'll be finding purple in that jacket pocket until Friday.

rows.en: Wednesday morning, and the walk from the parking is now the hard part.
rows.text: Woensdagoggend, en die stap van die parkering af is nou die moeilike deel.
rows.back: Wednesday morning, and the walk from the parking lot is now the hard part.

rows.en: He is bent that far over because standing upright stopped working.
rows.text: Hy leun so ver vooroor omdat regop staan nie meer werk nie.
rows.back: He's leaning that far forward because standing upright doesn't work anymore.

rows.en: The flag is doing its patriotic duty at about sixty kilometres an hour.
rows.text: Die vlag doen sy vaderlandse plig teen omtrent sestig kilometer per uur.
rows.back: The flag is doing its patriotic duty at about sixty kilometres an hour.

rows.en: That shade sail is one good gust away from becoming a spinnaker.
rows.text: Nog een goeie windvlaag, en daardie skaduseil is 'n spinnaker.
rows.back: One more good gust, and that shade sail is a spinnaker.

rows.en: The palm has given up on symmetry and committed to one direction.
rows.text: Die palm het simmetrie opgegee en kies nou net een kant.
rows.back: The palm has given up on symmetry and now just picks one side.

rows.en: Nobody on this side of Gqeberha is hanging washing out today.
rows.text: Niemand aan hierdie kant van Gqeberha hang vandag wasgoed op nie.
rows.back: Nobody on this side of Gqeberha is hanging out washing today.

rows.en: The aloe is unbothered, which is the entire point of an aloe.
rows.text: Die aalwyn steur hom aan niks, en dis die hele punt van 'n aalwyn.
rows.back: The aloe isn't bothered by anything, and that's the whole point of an aloe.

rows.en: The banana leaves are being redesigned in real time and taking it well.
rows.text: Die piesangblare word voor jou oë herontwerp en vat dit goed.
rows.back: The banana leaves are being redesigned before your eyes and taking it well.

rows.en: That shade cloth has been drumming since breakfast and nobody can hear the television.
rows.text: Daardie skadunet slaan al van ontbyt af soos 'n trom, en niemand kan die TV hoor nie.
rows.back: That shade net has been banging like a drum since breakfast, and nobody can hear the TV.

rows.en: The sea looks calm from up here, which is a complete lie.
rows.text: Die see lyk kalm van hier bo af, wat 'n volslae leuen is.
rows.back: The sea looks calm from up here, which is a complete lie.

rows.en: Friday, and the humidity has teamed up with the wind against everybody.
rows.text: Vrydag, en die klammigheid en die wind het teen almal saamgespan.
rows.back: Friday, and the humidity and the wind have ganged up on everyone.

rows.en: Every leaf on that palm is now a slightly different length.
rows.text: Elke blaar aan daardie palm het nou sy eie lengte.
rows.back: Every frond on that palm now has its own length.
rows.note: unclear: presumably fronds shredded/torn to uneven lengths

rows.en: The jacaranda is redecorating the whole road whether you like it or not.
rows.text: Die jakaranda herversier die hele pad of jy daarvan hou of nie.
rows.back: The jacaranda is redecorating the whole road whether you like it or not.

rows.en: Saturday, and the wind has strong opinions about your plans for the garden.
rows.text: Saterdag, en die wind het sterk menings oor jou planne vir die tuin.
rows.back: Saturday, and the wind has strong opinions about your plans for the garden.

rows.en: That grass on the verge has been lying flat since Thursday.
rows.text: Daardie gras langs die pad lê al sedert Donderdag plat.
rows.back: That grass by the road has been lying flat since Thursday.

rows.en: Somebody is going to sweep all that purple up and somebody is not.
rows.text: Een persoon gaan al daardie pers opvee, en iemand anders gaan nie.
rows.back: One person is going to sweep up all that purple, and someone else isn't.

rows.en: The sky has gone the colour that makes Joburg check the group chat.
rows.text: Die lug het die kleur geword wat Joburg na die group chat laat kyk.
rows.back: The sky has turned the colour that makes Joburg check the group chat.

rows.en: Every tree on the street is bowing the same way. Peer pressure.
rows.text: Elke boom in die straat buig dieselfde kant toe. Groepsdruk.
rows.back: Every tree in the street bends the same way. Peer pressure.

rows.en: The sheets are dry already and the wind is not finished with them.
rows.text: Die lakens is klaar droog en die wind is nog nie klaar met hulle nie.
rows.back: The sheets are already dry and the wind isn't done with them yet.

rows.en: The Helderberg is clear, the washing is horizontal, and that is Sunday sorted.
rows.text: Die Helderberg is helder, die wasgoed hang horisontaal, en Sondag is gereël.
rows.back: The Helderberg is clear, the washing is hanging horizontal, and Sunday is sorted.

rows.en: That little olive tree is going to grow up with a permanent lean.
rows.text: Daardie klein olyfboompie gaan met 'n permanente skuinste grootword.
rows.back: That little olive tree is going to grow up with a permanent lean.

rows.en: Nobody in this house is paying to dry anything today.
rows.text: Niemand in hierdie huis betaal vandag om iets droog te maak nie.
rows.back: Nobody in this house is paying to dry anything today.

rows.en: Those pegs are all that stands between you and a fence full of sheets.
rows.text: Daardie wasgoedpennetjies is al wat tussen jou en 'n heining vol lakens staan.
rows.back: Those clothes pegs are all that stands between you and a fence full of sheets.

rows.en: Thunder's grumbling, hey.
rows.text: Die donder dreun.
rows.back: The thunder rumbles.
rows.reason: chatty EN 'Thunder's grumbling, hey.' became the flat, formal 'Die donder dreun.' — spoken 'hey' dropped, reads like a textbook sentence
reasons: DRIFT: chatty EN 'Thunder's grumbling, hey.' became the flat, formal 'Die donder dreun.' — spoken 'hey' dropped, reads like a textbook sentence

rows.en: Weather so dramatic it needs a Carte Blanche segment.
rows.text: Weer so dramaties dit het 'n Carte Blanche insetsel nodig.
rows.back: Weather so dramatic it needs a Carte Blanche segment.
rows.note: grammar: 'so dramaties dit het' lacks 'dat' — reads a little broken
rows.reason: same joke; small grammar wobble ('so dramaties dit het' wants a comma or 'dat')

rows.en: Even the bakkies on the N2 pulled over.
rows.text: Selfs die bakkies op die N2 het stilgehou.
rows.back: Even the bakkies on the N2 have pulled over.

rows.en: The sky just went full Carte Blanche.
rows.text: Die lug het voluit bedonerd gegaan.
rows.back: The sky has gone full-on grumpy.
rows.reason: EN 'went full Carte Blanche' (TV-exposé drama) became 'voluit bedonerd gegaan' (gone full-on grumpy) — a different joke with the Carte Blanche reference gone; 'bedonerd' is also misspelt (bedonnerd)

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'bedonerd' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source; closest attested: 'bedonnerd' (4× kaikki/leipzig, distance 1)

rows.en: Windows closed, kettle on, and wait.

rows.note: literally the shoes chose today; presumably meant 'you chose your suede shoes today?'

rows.en: The queue at the petrol station just tripled.
rows.text: Die ry by die petrolstasie het net verdriedubbel.
rows.back: The queue at the petrol station just tripled.

rows.en: The puddle was deeper than it looked. It's always deeper.
rows.text: Die poel was dieper as wat dit gelyk het. Dis altyd dieper.
rows.back: The puddle was deeper than it looked. It's always deeper.

rows.en: Nobody told the forecast. It just arrived.
rows.text: Niemand het die voorspelling gesê nie. Dit het net opgedaag.
rows.back: Nobody said the forecast. It just showed up.
rows.note: garbled: 'het die voorspelling gesê' doesn't make sense — maybe 'nobody told the forecast' or 'nobody predicted it'
rows.reason: EN 'Nobody told the forecast' needs 'vir die voorspelling gesê'; 'Niemand het die voorspelling gesê nie' reads as the garbled 'nobody said the forecast', so the forecast-wasn't-informed joke is gone
reasons: MISMATCH: EN 'Nobody told the forecast' needs 'vir die voorspelling gesê'; 'Niemand het die voorspelling gesê nie' reads as the garbled 'nobody said the forecast', so the forecast-wasn't-informed joke is gone

rows.en: Every taxi on the road has decided to freestyle.
rows.text: Elke taxi op die pad het besluit om te freestyle.
rows.back: Every taxi on the road has decided to freestyle.

rows.en: The umbrella tax is now in effect.
rows.text: Die sambreelbelasting is nou van krag.
rows.back: The umbrella tax is now in effect.

rows.en: The dog is staring at the rain like it's a personal insult.
rows.text: Die hond staar na die reën asof dit n persoonlike belediging is.
rows.back: The dog is staring at the rain like it's a personal insult.
rows.reason: 'n written without apostrophe — typo only

rows.en: Cape winter: the mountain is getting its water back, with interest.
rows.text: Kaapse winter: die berg kry sy water terug, met rente.
rows.back: Cape winter: the mountain gets its water back, with interest.

rows.en: Every farmer in the Boland is smiling in their sleep right now.
rows.text: Elke boer in die Boland glimlag nou in sy slaap.
rows.back: Every farmer in the Boland is smiling in his sleep right now.

rows.en: In the Karoo this isn't rain. It's a celebrity appearance.
rows.text: In die Karoo is dit nie reën nie. Dis 'n verskyning.
rows.back: In the Karoo it isn't rain. It's an apparition.
rows.reason: EN 'a celebrity appearance' shrank to 'n verskyning' (an appearance/apparition) — the celebrity punchline is lost
reasons: DRIFT: EN 'a celebrity appearance' shrank to 'n verskyning' (an appearance/apparition) — the celebrity punchline is lost

rows.en: Even the sheep are standing still for this one.
rows.text: Selfs die skape staan stil vir hierdie een.
rows.back: Even the sheep stand still for this one.

rows.en: Somebody's birthday-candle wish just paid out.
rows.text: Iemand het reggewens by die verjaarsdagkoek.
rows.back: Someone wished right at the birthday cake.

rows.en: That sound on the roof just hit snooze for the entire country.
rows.text: Die reën op die dak het net amptelik snooze gedruk vir die hele land.
rows.back: The rain on the roof just officially hit snooze for the whole country.

rows.en: Five more minutes. The weather itself signed off on it.
rows.text: Vyf minute nog. Die weer het self so gesê.
rows.back: Five more minutes. The weather said so itself.

rows.en: One breath of rain air and suddenly the whole country is a poet.
rows.text: Een teug reënlug en skielik is almal in hierdie land 'n digter.
rows.back: One breath of rain-air and suddenly everyone in this country is a poet.

rows.en: Petrichor is the Greek word for it. Our word is 'sjoe'.
rows.text: Petrichor is die Griekse woord. Ons woord is 'sjoe'.
rows.back: Petrichor is the Greek word. Our word is 'sjoe'.

rows.en: Dam levels are the Cape's real Currie Cup.
rows.text: Damvlakke is die Kaap se eintlike Currie Cup.
rows.back: Dam levels are the Cape's real Currie Cup.

rows.en: Every percentage point gets its own family WhatsApp announcement.
rows.text: Elke persentasiepunt kry sy eie familie-WhatsApp.
rows.back: Every percentage point gets its own family WhatsApp.

rows.en: Theewaterskloof is about to trend in the group chat.
rows.text: Theewaterskloof gaan vanoggend viraal in die groepsgesprek.
rows.back: Theewaterskloof is going viral in the group chat this morning.
rows.reason: adds a time of day: 'vanoggend' (this morning) is not in EN 'is about to trend in the group chat'
reasons: DRIFT: adds a time of day: 'vanoggend' (this morning) is not in EN 'is about to trend in the group chat'

rows.en: Wet tar at sunrise. That's not a smell, that's heritage.
rows.text: Nat teer by sonsopkoms. Dis nie 'n reuk nie, dis 'n erfenis.
rows.back: Wet tar at sunrise. It's not a smell, it's a heritage.

rows.en: Post-storm Highveld air should be bottled and sold overseas.
rows.text: Die Hooglandlug ná reën behoort in 'n botteltjie verkoop te word.
rows.back: The highland air after rain should be sold in a little bottle.
rows.note: unsure: 'Hooglandlug' — highlands generally, or the Highveld (normally 'Hoëveld')
rows.reason: EN 'Highveld' became 'Hoogland' (reads as generic highlands, not Hoëveld), and 'sold overseas' lost 'overseas', flattening the export boast
reasons: DRIFT: EN 'Highveld' became 'Hoogland' (reads as generic highlands, not Hoëveld), and 'sold overseas' lost 'overseas', flattening the export boast

rows.en: Twenty minutes of opera, then the sun acts like nothing happened.
rows.text: Twintig minute se opera, dan maak die son of niks gebeur het nie.
rows.back: Twenty minutes of opera, then the sun acts like nothing happened.

rows.en: Other cities get weather. Joburg gets a production.
rows.text: Ander stede kry weer. Joburg kry 'n vertoning.
rows.back: Other cities get weather. Joburg gets a show.

rows.en: Two drops on a windscreen and the whole N1 forgets everything it ever learned.
rows.text: Twee druppels op die voorruit en die hele N1 se geheue is skoon gewas.
rows.back: Two drops on the windscreen and the whole N1's memory is washed clean.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'geheue' means 'memory; store' — nothing in the English source; it is 2 letters from 'geheel', the usual word for 'whole'

rows.en: Capetonians don't run from rain. They run towards it, cheering.
rows.text: Kapenaars hardloop nie weg van die reën nie. Hulle hardloop soontoe.
rows.back: Capetonians don't run away from the rain. They run towards it.

rows.en: One drought in living memory and now every downpour is a lottery win.
rows.text: Drie jaar se droogte-geheue en skielik is elke bui 'n lotto-wen.
rows.back: Three years of drought memory and suddenly every shower is a lotto win.
rows.reason: adds a number: EN 'One drought in living memory' became 'Drie jaar se droogte-geheue' (three years of drought memory)
reasons: DRIFT: adds a number: EN 'One drought in living memory' became 'Drie jaar se droogte-geheue' (three years of drought memory)

rows.en: Rain is just weather's way of saying stay where the coffee is.
rows.text: Reën is net die weer se manier om te sê: bly waar die koffie is.
rows.back: Rain is just the weather's way of saying: stay where the coffee is.

rows.en: All plans are officially moved to 'when it clears up'. Which is never. Shame.
rows.text: Alle afsprake is amptelik verskuif na 'wanneer dit opklaar'.
rows.back: All appointments are officially moved to 'when it clears up'.
rows.reason: the kicker 'Which is never. Shame.' is dropped, so the line ends on the setup; 'plans' also became 'afsprake' (appointments)
reasons: DRIFT: the kicker 'Which is never. Shame.' is dropped, so the line ends on the setup; 'plans' also became 'afsprake' (appointments)

rows.en: You smell Highveld rain before you see it. That's the trailer.
rows.text: Jy ruik Hoëveldse reën voor jy hom sien. Dis die lokprent.
rows.back: You smell Highveld rain before you see it. That's the trailer.

rows.en: The veld already knows. The veld always knows first.
rows.text: Die veld weet reeds. Die veld weet altyd eerste.
rows.back: The veld already knows. The veld always knows first.

rows.en: In the Cape, wine genuinely tastes better when the dam levels are rising.
rows.text: In die Kaap proe die wyn beter as die damme styg.
rows.back: In the Cape the wine tastes better when the dams rise.

rows.en: To the dam levels! Every downpour is a round on the house.
rows.text: Op die damvlakke! Elke bui is 'n rondte op die huis.
rows.back: To the dam levels! Every shower is a round on the house.

rows.en: School shoes' greatest enemy has just landed.
rows.text: Skoolskoene se grootste vyand het pas geland.
rows.back: School shoes' worst enemy has just landed.

rows.en: Somebody's mom is going to have words. Worth it.
rows.text: Iemand se ma gaan iets sê. Dit was die moeite werd.
rows.back: Someone's mom is going to say something. It was worth it.

rows.en: The storm was the performance. This is the bow.
rows.text: Die storm was die opvoering. Dít is die buiging.
rows.back: The storm was the performance. This is the bow.

rows.en: Dusk rain turns the whole city's volume down a notch.
rows.text: Skemer-reën draai die hele stad se volume saggies af.
rows.back: Dusk rain gently turns down the whole city's volume.

rows.en: The mountain is having a quiet drink. So is half the city, probably.
rows.text: Die berg drink rustig. Die stad ook, waarskynlik.
rows.back: The mountain is drinking quietly. The city too, probably.

rows.en: Distant lightning and a warm mug: best channel on television.
rows.text: Weerlig in die verte, koffie in die hand — beste kanaal op televisie.
rows.back: Lightning in the distance, coffee in hand — best channel on TV.

rows.en: In the Karoo you watch rain the way other people watch rugby.
rows.text: In die Karoo kyk jy reën soos ander mense rugby kyk.
rows.back: In the Karoo you watch rain the way other people watch rugby.

rows.en: It's still fifty kilometres away and the stoep is already sold out.
rows.text: Dis nog vyftig kilometer weg en die stoep is klaar vol.
rows.back: It's still fifty kilometres away and the stoep is already full.

rows.en: Rain on a tin roof: the official national lullaby.
rows.text: Reën op 'n sinkdak: die land se amptelike slaapliedjie.
rows.back: Rain on a tin roof: the country's official lullaby.

rows.en: No sleep app on earth can compete with a tin roof.
rows.text: Geen slaap-app op aarde kan met 'n sinkdak meeding nie.
rows.back: No sleep app on earth can compete with a tin roof.

rows.en: Put the phone down. The roof is talking.
rows.text: Sit die foon neer. Die dak is besig om te praat.
rows.back: Put the phone down. The roof is talking.

rows.en: Free fireworks, no tickets, best seats in the house.
rows.text: Gratis vuurwerke. Geen kaartjies. Beste sitplekke in die huis.
rows.back: Free fireworks. No tickets. Best seats in the house.
rows.note: 'Geen kaartjies' fragment without closing 'nie' — acceptable in a list

rows.en: The Highveld doesn't do subtle, and honestly we're grateful.
rows.text: Die Hoëveld hou nie van subtiel nie en ons is dankbaar.
rows.back: The Highveld doesn't do subtle and we're grateful.

rows.en: The Boland is getting watered in its sleep and will absolutely brag about it tomorrow.
rows.text: Die Boland word in sy slaap natgelê en môre spog hy daaroor.
rows.back: The Boland is getting soaked in its sleep and tomorrow it'll brag about it.
rows.note: 'natgelê' — 'natlê' means bed-wetting, so it reads as 'the Boland wets the bed in its sleep' (possibly an intended pun)
rows.reason: EN 'getting watered in its sleep' became 'word in sy slaap natgelê' — 'natlê' means bed-wetting, so the Boland now wets the bed and brags about it, a cruder image than being watered
reasons: DRIFT: EN 'getting watered in its sleep' became 'word in sy slaap natgelê' — 'natlê' means bed-wetting, so the Boland now wets the bed and brags about it, a cruder image than being watered

rows.en: The clouds are having a moment.
rows.text: Amafu anesikhathi sawo.
rows.back: The clouds are having their moment.

rows.en: Grab your brolly, boet.
rows.text: Thatha isambulela sakho, boet.
rows.back: Take your umbrella, boet.

rows.en: The garden's saying dankie at last.
rows.text: Ingadi ithi ekugcineni ngiyabonga.
rows.back: The garden finally says thank you.

rows.en: The potholes are becoming swimming pools.
rows.text: Imigodi iba amapulazi okubhukuda.
rows.back: Potholes become swimming farms.
rows.reason: 'amapulazi okubhukuda' means swimming FARMS, not swimming pools (known amapulazi error), so the line is garbled.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'amapulazi' was misused before in this app (means 'farms', misused for 'pools') — verify it is the intended sense here

reasons: MISMATCH: 'amapulazi okubhukuda' means swimming FARMS, not swimming pools (known amapulazi error), so the line is garbled.

rows.en: Your car wash was a waste of money.
rows.text: Ukuwasha imoto kwakho bekuyize yemali.
rows.back: Your car wash was a waste of money.

rows.en: Joburg drivers are panicking already.
rows.text: Abashayeli baseJoburg sebeyesaba.
rows.back: Joburg drivers are already scared.

rows.en: Perfect excuse to cancel plans.
rows.text: Isizathu esihle sokukhansela izinhlelo.
rows.back: A good excuse to cancel plans.

rows.en: The dams are doing a happy dance.
rows.text: Amadamu enza umdanso ojabulayo.
rows.back: The dams are doing a happy dance.

rows.en: The N1 is now a waterpark.
rows.text: I-N1 manje yi-waterpark.
rows.back: The N1 is now a waterpark.

rows.en: Good soup weather, not gonna lie.
rows.text: Isimo sezulu esihle sesobho.
rows.back: Good soup weather.
rows.reason: Filler 'not gonna lie' dropped.

rows.en: Someone's braai just got ruined.
rows.text: Ukosa komuntu kusanda konakala.
rows.back: Someone's braai just got ruined.

rows.en: Rain so heavy it should pay rent.
rows.text: Imvula enzima kakhulu kufanele ikhokhe irenti.
rows.back: Rain this heavy should be paying rent.

rows.en: Your shoes are about to have a bad day.
rows.text: Izicathulo zakho zizoba nosuku olubi.
rows.back: Your shoes are going to have a bad day.

rows.en: The commute just became a team sport.
rows.text: Uhambo seluphenduke umdlalo weqembu.
rows.back: The commute has turned into a team sport.

rows.en: Everyone's forgotten how to drive. Again.
rows.text: Bonke sebakhohlwe ukushayela. Futhi.
rows.back: Everyone has forgotten how to drive. Again.

rows.en: The umbrella broke on the first gust. Classic.
rows.text: Isambulela sephuke ngomoya wokuqala. Okujwayelekile.
rows.back: The umbrella broke in the first gust. Typical.

rows.en: Wet socks. The ultimate betrayal.
rows.text: Amasokisi amanzi. Ukukhaphela okukhulu.
rows.back: Wet socks. The great betrayal.

rows.en: You'll dry. Eventually. Probably.
rows.text: Uzokoma. Ekugcineni. Cishe.
rows.back: You'll dry. Eventually. Probably.
rows.note: 'uzokoma' can also read 'you'll be thirsty' (ukoma); 'dry' is the natural reading here

rows.en: At least the garden's happy. Someone has to be.
rows.text: Okungenani ingadi iyajabula. Othile kumele ajabule.
rows.back: At least the garden is happy. Someone has to be.

rows.en: The wipers are on max and it's still not enough.
rows.text: Ama-wipers aku-max kodwa akwanele.
rows.back: The wipers are on max but it's not enough.

rows.en: Your suede shoes chose today? Bold.
rows.text: Izicathulo zakho zesuede zikhethe namuhla? Isibindi.
rows.back: Your suede shoes, today of all days? Brave.

rows.en: The queue at the petrol station just tripled.
rows.text: Umugqa esiteshini sikaphethiloli usanda kuphindeka kathathu.
rows.back: The queue at the petrol station just tripled.

rows.en: Somewhere an umbrella just turned inside out. Moment of silence.
rows.text: Endaweni ethile isambulela sisanda kuphenduka ngaphakathi. Umzuzu wokuthula.
rows.back: Somewhere an umbrella just turned inside out. A moment of silence.

rows.en: The puddle was deeper than it looked. It's always deeper.
rows.text: Isiziba sasijule kunalokho ebesibukeka ngakho. Sihlala sijule.
rows.back: The puddle was deeper than it looked. It always is.

rows.en: Hair plans: cancelled.
rows.text: Izinhlelo zezinwele: zikhanselelwe.
rows.back: Hair plans: cancelled.

findings: HIGH lexical: 'zikhanselelwe' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source

rows.en: The traffic is emotional.
rows.text: Ithrafikhi inomzwelo.
rows.back: The traffic has feelings / is emotional.
rows.note: unsure: 'inomzwelo' — 'umzwelo' not a form I recognise; 'uzwelo' = sympathy, 'imizwa' = feelings
rows.reason: 'inomzwelo' reads as 'has feelings', but 'umzwelo' is a doubtful form.

rows.en: Nobody told the forecast. It just arrived.
rows.text: Akekho otshele isibikezelo. Sivele safika.
rows.back: Nobody told the forecast. It just showed up.
rows.note: subject of 'Sivele safika' is ambiguous (the forecast itself arrived?)

rows.en: Every taxi on the road has decided to freestyle.
rows.text: Yonke itekisi emgwaqweni ikhethe ukudlala ngokukhululeka.
rows.back: Every taxi on the road has decided to freestyle.

rows.en: Yes, it's raining sideways. South Africa speciality.
rows.text: Yebo, kuyana ngenhlangothi. Okukhethekile kweNingizimu Afrika.
rows.back: Yes, it's raining sideways. A South African speciality.
rows.reason: The meaning carries; 'ngenhlangothi' should be 'ngohlangothi'.

rows.en: The umbrella tax is now in effect.
rows.text: Intela yesambulela isiyasebenza.
rows.back: The umbrella tax is now in effect.

rows.en: Wet jeans for the rest of the day. The classic punishment.
rows.text: Ijiyini emanzi kuyo yonke insuku. Isijeziso esijwayelekile.
rows.back: Wet jeans all day. The usual punishment.
rows.note: garbled: 'kuyo yonke insuku' — 'insuku' is not a standard form ('usuku lonke' = all day; 'zonke izinsuku' = every day)
rows.reason: 'for the rest of the day' becomes the ungrammatical 'kuyo yonke insuku', which can read as 'every day'.
reasons: DRIFT: 'for the rest of the day' becomes the ungrammatical 'kuyo yonke insuku', which can read as 'every day'.

rows.en: Solidarity to everyone with one wet shoe right now.
rows.text: Ukuhlangana nabo bonke abanesicathulo esisodwa esimanzi manje.
rows.back: Solidarity with everyone who has one wet shoe right now.

rows.en: The pavement is a river and the river has plans.
rows.text: Ipavimende ingumfula futhi umfula uneziluleko.
rows.back: The pavement is a river and the river has advice.
rows.reason: 'the river has plans' (menace) becomes 'umfula uneziluleko' (the river has advice), which changes the punchline.
reasons: DRIFT: 'the river has plans' (menace) becomes 'umfula uneziluleko' (the river has advice), which changes the punchline.

rows.en: Forgot your jacket? The universe noticed.
rows.text: Ukhohlwe ijazi lakho? Indawo yonke iqaphele.
rows.back: Forgot your jacket? The whole place noticed.
rows.reason: 'Indawo yonke' (everywhere / the whole world) stands in for 'the universe'.

rows.en: The dog is staring at the rain like it's a personal insult.
rows.text: Inja ibheka imvula sengathi inhlamba yomuntu siqu.
rows.back: The dog looks at the rain as if it's a personal insult.

rows.en: The traffic just remembered rain exists. Again.
rows.text: Ithrafikhi isanda kukhumbula ukuthi imvula ikhona. Futhi.
rows.back: The traffic just remembered that rain exists. Again.

rows.en: The dams get their drink before you get your coffee. Know your place.
rows.text: Amadamu athola ukuphuza kwawo ngaphambi kokuba uthole ikhofi lakho. Yazi indawo yakho.
rows.back: The dams get their drink before you get your coffee. Know your place.

rows.en: Cape winter: the mountain is getting its water back, with interest.
rows.text: Ubusika baseKapa: intaba ithola amanzi ayo emuva, nenzalo.
rows.back: Cape winter: the mountain gets its water back, with interest.

rows.en: Every farmer in the Boland is smiling in their sleep right now.
rows.text: Wonke umlimi eBoland umamatheka ebuthongweni njengamanje.
rows.back: Every farmer in the Boland is smiling in their sleep right now.

rows.en: In the Karoo this isn't rain. It's a celebrity appearance.
rows.text: EKaroo lokhu akuyona imvula. Kuwukuvela kwe-celebrity.
rows.back: In the Karoo this isn't rain. It's a celebrity appearance.

rows.en: Even the sheep are standing still for this one.
rows.text: Ngisho nezimvu zimile zithe du ngenxa yalokhu.
rows.back: Even the sheep are standing dead still because of this.

rows.en: Somebody's birthday-candle wish just paid out.
rows.text: Isifiso sikamuntu se-candle yosuku lokuzalwa sisanda kugcwaliseka.
rows.back: Someone's birthday-candle wish just came true.

rows.en: That sound on the roof just hit snooze for the entire country.
rows.text: Lowo msindo ophahleni usanda kucindezela i-snooze yezwe lonke.
rows.back: That sound on the roof just hit snooze for the whole country.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'usanda' means 'to increase, multiply; to spread (of rumours, a disease); to become larger' — nothing in the English source; it is 3 letters from 'shaya', the usual word for 'hit'

rows.en: Five more minutes. The weather itself signed off on it.
rows.text: Imizuzu emihlanu nje. Izulu ngokwalo livumile.
rows.back: Just five minutes. The sky itself agreed.
rows.reason: 'Imizuzu emihlanu nje' (just five minutes) is close to 'five more minutes'.

rows.en: One breath of rain air and suddenly the whole country is a poet.
rows.text: Umphefumulo owodwa womoya wemvula bese lonke izwe liba yimbongi.
rows.back: One breath of rain air and the whole country becomes a poet.

rows.en: Petrichor is the Greek word for it. Our word is 'sjoe'.
rows.text: I-Petrichor yigama lesiGreki. Elethu igama lithi 'yoh'.
rows.back: Petrichor is a Greek word. Our word is 'yoh'.
rows.reason: 'sjoe' localised as 'yoh', an equivalent SA exclamation.

rows.en: Dam levels are the Cape's real Currie Cup.
rows.text: Amazinga amadamu yiCurrie Cup yangempela yaseKapa.
rows.back: Dam levels are the Cape's real Currie Cup.

rows.en: Every percentage point gets its own family WhatsApp announcement.
rows.text: Wonke i-percentage point ithola isimemezelo sayo se-WhatsApp yomndeni.
rows.back: Every percentage point gets its own family WhatsApp announcement.

rows.en: Theewaterskloof is about to trend in the group chat.
rows.text: I-Theewaterskloof isizoba yi-trend ku-group chat.
rows.back: Theewaterskloof is about to trend in the group chat.

rows.en: Rain on a farm isn't weather. It's a salary falling from the sky.
rows.text: Imvula epulazini akusona isimo sezulu. Ngumholo owela uvela ezulwini.
rows.back: Rain on a farm isn't weather. It's a salary falling from heaven.

rows.en: Somewhere a farmer is doing a small private dance nobody's allowed to see.
rows.text: Ndawana thile umlimi wenza umdanso omncane wangasese okungavumelekile ukuba ubonwe.
rows.back: Somewhere a farmer is doing a small private dance that nobody is allowed to see.

rows.en: Wet tar at sunrise. That's not a smell, that's heritage.
rows.text: I-tar emanzi ekuphumeni kwelanga. Akulona iphunga, yifa.
rows.back: Wet tar at sunrise. It's not a smell, it's a heritage.

rows.en: Joburg rain keeps a diary: 2pm sharp, maximum drama, no apologies.
rows.text: Imvula yaseJoburg igcina idayari: ngo-2 emini ncamashi, umdlalo omkhulu, azixolisi.
rows.back: Joburg rain keeps a diary: 2pm sharp, big drama, no apologies.

rows.en: Twenty minutes of opera, then the sun acts like nothing happened.
rows.text: Imizuzu engamashumi amabili ye-opera, bese ilanga lenza sengathi akukho okwenzekile.
rows.back: Twenty minutes of opera, then the sun pretends nothing happened.

rows.en: Other cities get weather. Joburg gets a production.
rows.text: Amanye amadolobha athola isimo sezulu. IJoburg ithola umbukiso.
rows.back: Other cities get weather. Joburg gets a show.

rows.en: Two drops on a windscreen and the whole N1 forgets everything it ever learned.
rows.text: Amaconsi amabili ku-windscreen bese yonke i-N1 ikhohlwa yikho konke eyake yakufunda.
rows.back: Two drops on the windscreen and the whole N1 forgets everything it ever learned.
rows.note: 'ikhohlwa yikho konke' — 'yikho' reads as passive agent ('is forgotten by everything'); minor slip

rows.en: Rain turns every South African driver back into a learner. Hazards on, dignity off.
rows.text: Imvula iphendula wonke umshayeli waseNingizimu Afrika abe umfundi futhi. Ama-hazards avuliwe, isithunzi sicishiwe.

rows.en: Free fireworks, no tickets, best seats in the house.
rows.text: Ii-fireworks zasimahla, akukho matikiti, ezona zihlalo zibhetele endlwini.
rows.back: Free fireworks, no tickets, the best seats are indoors.

rows.en: The Highveld doesn't do subtle, and honestly we're grateful.
rows.text: IHighveld ayenzi nto ithe cwaka, kwaye ngokunyanisekileyo siyabulela.
rows.back: The Highveld doesn't do anything quietly, and honestly we're grateful.

rows.en: Sleep tight, dams. You worked hard today.
rows.text: Lala kamnandi, madama. Nisebenze nzima namhlanje.
rows.back: Sleep well, dams. You worked hard today.

rows.en: The Boland is getting watered in its sleep and will absolutely brag about it tomorrow.
rows.text: IBoland inkcenkceshelwa ebuthongweni yaye ngomso iza kuqhayisa ngako.
rows.back: The Boland is being watered in its sleep and tomorrow it's going to brag about it.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'inkcenkceshelwa' — not found in any external source

rows.en: The clouds are having a moment.
rows.text: Maru a na le nako ea 'ona.
rows.back: The clouds are having their moment.

rows.en: Grab your brolly, boet.
rows.text: Nka sekhele sa hao, boet.
rows.back: Take your umbrella, boet.

rows.en: The garden's saying dankie at last.
rows.text: Jarata e re kea leboha qetellong.
rows.back: The garden finally says thank you.

rows.en: The potholes are becoming swimming pools.
rows.text: Mesima e fetoha matamo a ho sesa.
rows.back: Potholes are turning into swimming pools.

rows.en: Your car wash was a waste of money.
rows.text: Ho hlatswa koloi ea hao e ne e le tjhelete e lahliloeng.
rows.back: Washing your car was money thrown away.

rows.en: Joburg drivers are panicking already.
rows.text: Bakganni ba joburg ba se ba tsohile
rows.back: Joburg drivers are already up.
rows.note: 'ba se ba tsohile' = are already awake - no clear joke; lowercase 'joburg'.
rows.reason: 'ba se ba tsohile' means 'are already awake/up', not 'panicking already', so the punchline is gone.
reasons: DRIFT: 'ba se ba tsohile' means 'are already awake/up', not 'panicking already', so the punchline is gone.

rows.en: Perfect excuse to cancel plans.
rows.text: Lebaka le letle la ho hlakola merero.
rows.back: A good excuse to cancel plans.

rows.en: The dams are doing a happy dance.
rows.text: Matamo a etsa motjeko o thabileng.
rows.back: The dams/puddles are doing a happy dance.

rows.en: The N1 is now a waterpark.
rows.text: N1 jwale ke waterpark.
rows.back: The N1 is now a waterpark.

rows.en: Good soup weather, not gonna lie.
rows.text: Lehodimo le letle la  sopho
rows.back: Lovely soup weather.
rows.note: double space; fragment 'a lovely sky for soup'.

rows.en: Someone's braai just got ruined.
rows.text: Braai ea motho e senyehile.
rows.back: Someone's braai is ruined.

rows.en: Rain so heavy it should pay rent.
rows.text: Pula e boima haholo e lokela ho lefa rente.
rows.back: Rain this heavy should pay rent.

rows.en: Your shoes are about to have a bad day.
rows.text: Dieta tsa hao li tla ba le letsatsi le lebe.
rows.back: Your shoes are going to have a bad day.

rows.en: The commute just became a team sport.
rows.text: Leeto le fetohile papadi ea sehlopha.
rows.back: The commute has turned into a team sport.

rows.en: Everyone's forgotten how to drive. Again.
rows.text: Bohle ba lebetse ho otlela. Hape.
rows.back: Everyone forgot how to drive. Again.

rows.en: The umbrella broke on the first gust. Classic.
rows.text: Sekhele se robehile ka moya oa pele. Setso.
rows.back: The umbrella broke in the first gust. Tradition.
rows.reason: 'Setso' (tradition) stands in for 'Classic'.

rows.en: Wet socks. The ultimate betrayal.
rows.text: Dikausu tse metsi. Boko bo boholo.
rows.back: Wet socks. Big brain.
rows.note: 'Boko bo boholo' = big brain; joke unclear (no sense of betrayal/regret).
rows.reason: 'Boko bo boholo' means 'big brain', not 'the ultimate betrayal', so the punchline says something else entirely.
reasons: MISMATCH: 'Boko bo boholo' means 'big brain', not 'the ultimate betrayal', so the punchline says something else entirely.

rows.en: You'll dry. Eventually. Probably.
rows.text: O tla oma. Qetellong. Mohlomong.
rows.back: You'll dry. Eventually. Maybe.
rows.note: 'O tla oma' = you'll dry (or 'it will dry').

rows.en: At least the garden's happy. Someone has to be.
rows.text: Bonyane jarata e thabile. Motho e mong o tlameha ho thaba.
rows.back: At least the garden is happy. Someone has to be.

rows.en: The wipers are on max and it's still not enough.
rows.text: Di-wiper di ho max empa ha di ea lekana.
rows.back: The wipers are on max but they're not enough.
rows.note: 'ha di ea lekana' nonstandard (expected 'ha di a lekana').

rows.en: Your suede shoes chose today? Bold.
rows.text: Dieta tsa hao tsa suede li kgethile kajeno? Sebete.
rows.back: Your suede shoes chose today? Brave.

rows.en: The queue at the petrol station just tripled.
rows.text: Mola seteisheneng sa petlolo o sa tswa phethahala hararo.
rows.back: The queue at the petrol station just tripled.
rows.note: 'o sa tswa phethahala hararo' odd - literally 'has just been completed thrice'; read as 'tripled'.
rows.reason: 'o sa tswa phethahala hararo' (has just been completed three times) is an unnatural way to say 'tripled'; the number only survives if the reader decodes it.
reasons: DRIFT: 'o sa tswa phethahala hararo' (has just been completed three times) is an unnatural way to say 'tripled'; the number only survives if the reader decodes it.

rows.en: Somewhere an umbrella just turned inside out. Moment of silence.
rows.text: Kae-kae sekhele se sa tswa reteleha ka hare. Motsotso oa kgutso.
rows.back: Somewhere an umbrella just turned inside out. A moment of silence.

rows.en: The puddle was deeper than it looked. It's always deeper.
rows.text: Letamo le ne le tebile ho feta kamoo le neng le shebahala kateng. Le dula le tebile.
rows.back: The puddle was deeper than it looked. It always is.

rows.en: Hair plans: cancelled.
rows.text: Merero ea moriri: e hlakotswe.
rows.back: Hair plans: cancelled.

rows.en: The traffic is emotional.
rows.text: Sephethephethe se na le maikutlo.
rows.back: The traffic has feelings.

rows.en: Nobody told the forecast. It just arrived.
rows.text: Ha ho motho ea bolelletseng ponelopele. E fihletse feela.
rows.back: Nobody told the forecast. It just showed up.
rows.note: unsure: 'ha ho motho ea bolelletseng ponelopele' - 'nobody told the forecast' vs 'nobody forecast it'.

rows.en: Every taxi on the road has decided to freestyle.
rows.text: Tekisi e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe tseleng e kgethile ho bapala ka bo eona.
rows.back: Every taxi on the road has decided to play by its own rules.
rows.reason: 'ho bapala ka bo eona' (play its own way) stands in for 'freestyle'.

rows.en: Yes, it's raining sideways. South Africa speciality.
rows.text: E, pula e na ka mahlakoreng. Phaello ea Afrika Borwa.
rows.back: Yes, the rain is falling sideways. A South African bonus.

rows.en: The umbrella tax is now in effect.
rows.text: Lekgetho la sekhele le se le sebetsa.
rows.back: The umbrella tax is now in effect.

rows.en: Wet jeans for the rest of the day. The classic punishment.
rows.text: Lijinse tse metsi letsatsi lohle. Kotlo ea setso.
rows.back: Wet jeans all day. The traditional punishment.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'Lijinse' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source

rows.en: Solidarity to everyone with one wet shoe right now.
rows.text: Kopano le bohle ba nang le seeta se le seng se metsi jwale.
rows.back: Solidarity with everyone who now has one wet shoe.

rows.en: The pavement is a river and the river has plans.
rows.text: Pavimente ke noka mme noka e na le merero.
rows.back: The pavement is a river and the river has plans.

rows.en: Forgot your jacket? The universe noticed.
rows.text: U lebetse jase ea hao? Bokahohle bo bone.
rows.back: Forgot your jacket? The universe saw.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'bone' is a tn function-word marker (tn 3286× vs st 207×)

rows.en: The dog is staring at the rain like it's a personal insult.
rows.text: Ntja e shebile pula jwalo ka thohako ea botho.
rows.back: The dog is staring at the rain like it's a personal curse.
rows.note: unsure: 'thohako ea botho' - a curse on humanity / a personal curse.
rows.reason: 'thohako ea botho' reads as 'a curse (on humanity)' rather than 'a personal insult', which blurs the joke that the dog takes it personally.
reasons: DRIFT: 'thohako ea botho' reads as 'a curse (on humanity)' rather than 'a personal insult', which blurs the joke that the dog takes it personally.

rows.en: The traffic just remembered rain exists. Again.
rows.text: Sephethephethe se sa tswa hopola hore pula e teng. Hape.
rows.back: The traffic just remembered that rain exists. Again.

rows.en: The dams get their drink before you get your coffee. Know your place.
rows.text: Matamo a nwa pele o fumana kofi ya hao. Tseba sebaka sa hao.
rows.back: The dams drink before you get your coffee. Know your place.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'sebaka' means 'area; distance; scene' — nothing in the English source; it is 2 letters from 'seka', the usual word for 'place'

rows.en: Cape winter: the mountain is getting its water back, with interest.
rows.text: Mariha a Cape: thaba e fumana metsi a eona morao, ka phaello.
rows.back: Cape winter: the mountain gets its water back, with interest.

rows.en: Every farmer in the Boland is smiling in their sleep right now.
rows.text: Molemi e mong le e mong Boland o bososela borokong hona jwale.
rows.back: Every farmer in the Boland is smiling in their sleep right now.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'hona' means 'this; demonstrative pronoun this; it (absolute pronoun)' — nothing in the English source; it is 1 letter from 'tona', the usual word for 'right'

rows.en: In the Karoo this isn't rain. It's a celebrity appearance.
rows.text: Karoo sena ha se pula. Ke ho iponahatsa ha motho ea tummeng.
rows.back: Karoo, this isn't rain. It's a celebrity appearance.

rows.en: Even the sheep are standing still for this one.
rows.text: Esita le dinku di eme li tsitsitse bakeng sa ena.
rows.back: Even the sheep are standing still for this.

rows.en: That sound on the roof just hit snooze for the entire country.
rows.text: Modumo oo marulelong o sa tswa tobetsa snooze bakeng sa naha eohle.
rows.back: That sound on the roof just hit snooze for the whole country(side).
rows.note: 'naha' = country or the countryside/farmland; 'modumo' here = the sound on the roof.

rows.en: Five more minutes. The weather itself signed off on it.
rows.text: Metsotso e mehlano hape. Boemo ba lehodimo bo itse ho lokile.
rows.back: Five more minutes. The weather said it's fine.

rows.en: One breath of rain air and suddenly the whole country is a poet.
rows.text: Ho hema moya oa pula hang 'me naha eohle e fetoha seroki.
rows.back: One breath of rain air and the whole country turns poet.

rows.en: Petrichor is the Greek word for it. Our word is 'sjoe'.
rows.text: Petrichor ke lentswe la Segerike. Lentswe la rona ke 'sjoe'.
rows.back: Petrichor is a Greek word. Our word is 'sjoe'.

rows.en: Dam levels are the Cape's real Currie Cup.
rows.text: Boemo ba matamo ke Currie Cup ea 'nete ea Cape.
rows.back: Dam levels are the Cape's real Currie Cup.

rows.en: Every percentage point gets its own family WhatsApp announcement.
rows.text: Phesente e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe e fumana tsebiso ea eona ea lelapa ka WhatsApp.
rows.back: Every percent gets its own family WhatsApp announcement.

rows.en: Theewaterskloof is about to trend in the group chat.
rows.text: Theewaterskloof e se e tlo trenda ka group chat.
rows.back: Theewaterskloof is about to trend in the group chat.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'trenda' — not found in any external source; closest attested: 'trends' (4× wiki, distance 1)

rows.en: Rain on a farm isn't weather. It's a salary falling from the sky.
rows.text: Pula polasing ha se boemo ba lehodimo. Ke moputso o wang lehodimong.
rows.back: Rain on the farm isn't weather. It's wages falling from the sky.
rows.note: 'o wang lehodimong' = falling in the sky (expected 'ho tswa lehodimong').

rows.en: Somewhere a farmer is doing a small private dance nobody's allowed to see.
rows.text: Kae-kae molemi o tantša motjeko o monyane oo ho seng motho ea dumellwang ho o bona.
rows.back: Somewhere a farmer is doing a little dance nobody is allowed to see.

rows.en: Wet tar at sunrise. That's not a smell, that's heritage.
rows.text: Tar e metsi ha letsatsi le tjhaba. Hoo ha se monko, ke lefa.
rows.back: Wet tar when the sun comes out. That's not a smell, it's heritage.

rows.en: Post-storm Highveld air should be bottled and sold overseas.
rows.text: Moya wa Highveld kamora sefefo o lokela ho kenngwa botlolong o rekiswe ditjhabeng.
rows.back: Highveld air after a storm should be bottled and sold overseas.

rows.en: Joburg rain keeps a diary: 2pm sharp, maximum drama, no apologies.
rows.text: Pula ea Joburg e na le bukana: 2pm hantle, drama e ngata, ha ho boitšoarelo.
rows.back: Joburg rain has a rulebook: 2pm sharp, lots of drama, no apologies.
rows.reason: 'bukana' (notebook) stands in for 'diary'.

rows.en: Twenty minutes of opera, then the sun acts like nothing happened.
rows.text: Metsotso e mashome a mabedi ea opera, ebe letsatsi le iketsa eka ha ho letho le etsahetseng.
rows.back: Twenty minutes of opera, then the sun acts like nothing happened.

rows.en: Other cities get weather. Joburg gets a production.
rows.text: Metse e meng e fumana boemo ba lehodimo. Joburg e fumana production.
rows.back: Other towns get weather. Joburg gets a production.

rows.en: Two drops on a windscreen and the whole N1 forgets everything it ever learned.
rows.text: Marothodi a mabedi windscreen-eng 'me N1 eohle e lebala tsohle tseo e kileng ea ithuta tsona.
rows.back: Two drops on the windscreen and the whole N1 forgets everything it ever learned.

rows.en: Capetonians don't run from rain. They run towards it, cheering.
rows.text: Batho ba Cape Town ha ba balehe pula. Ba mathela ho eona, ba hoeletsa.
rows.back: Cape Town people don't run from the rain. They run into it, shouting.
rows.reason: 'ba hoeletsa' (shouting) stands in for 'cheering'.

rows.en: Rain is just weather's way of saying stay where the coffee is.
rows.text: Pula ke tsela ya boemo ba lehodimo ya ho re dula moo kofi e leng teng.
rows.back: Rain is the weather's way of telling us to stay where the coffee is.

rows.en: All plans are officially moved to 'when it clears up'. Which is never. Shame.
rows.text: Merero eohle e fallisetswe ho 'ha ho se ho hlaka'. E leng le kgale. Shame.
rows.back: All plans have been moved to 'when it clears up'. Which is never. Shame.
rows.note: 'E leng le kgale' = which is never.

rows.en: You smell Highveld rain before you see it. That's the trailer.
rows.text: O utlwa monko oa pula ea Highveld pele o e bona. Ke trailer eo.
rows.back: You smell Highveld rain before you see it. That's the trailer.

rows.en: The veld already knows. The veld always knows first.
rows.text: Naha e se e tseba. Naha e dula e tseba pele.
rows.back: The land already knows. The land always knows first.

rows.en: In the Cape, wine genuinely tastes better when the dam levels are rising.
rows.text: Cape, wine e latsweha hamonate ha boemo ba matamo bo phahama.
rows.back: Cape, wine tastes better when the dam levels rise.

rows.en: Breaking news: the puddles are open for business.
rows.text: Ditaba tse ntjha: matamo a manyane a butse kgwebo.
rows.back: Breaking news: the little puddles have opened for business.
rows.note: 'matamo a manyane' = small dams, i.e. puddles.

rows.en: School shoes' greatest enemy has just landed.
rows.text: Sera se seholo sa dieta tsa sekolo se sa tswa fihla.
rows.back: School shoes' greatest enemy has just arrived.

rows.en: Somebody's mom is going to have words. Worth it.
rows.text: Mme oa motho o tla bua. E ne e le molemo.
rows.back: Someone's mom is going to have words. It was worth it.
rows.note: 'o tla bua' = will have words (scold); Lesotho 'oa'.

rows.en: Joburg rains for twenty minutes, then paints the sky like nothing happened.
rows.text: Joburg e na metsotso e mashome a mabedi, ebe e penta lehodimo eka ha ho letho le etsahetseng.
rows.back: Joburg rains for twenty minutes, then paints the sky like nothing happened.

rows.en: The storm was the performance. This is the bow.
rows.text: Sefefo e ne e le pontšo. Ena ke ho inama.
rows.back: The storm was the show. This is the bow.

rows.en: Dusk rain turns the whole city's volume down a notch.
rows.text: Pula ea mantsiboya e theola volume ea toropo eohle.
rows.back: Evening rain turns down the whole town's volume.

rows.en: The mountain is having a quiet drink. So is half the city, probably.
rows.text: Thaba e nwa ka kgutso. Le halofo ea toropo, mohlomong.
rows.back: The mountain drinks quietly. So does half the town, probably.

rows.en: Distant lightning and a warm mug: best channel on television.
rows.text: Lehadima le hole le komiki e futhumetseng: chanele e ntle ka ho fetisisa ea thelevishene.
rows.back: Distant lightning and a warm mug: the best channel on TV.

rows.en: In the Karoo you watch rain the way other people watch rugby.
rows.text: Karoo o shebella pula jwalo ka ha batho ba bang ba shebella rugby.
rows.back: The Karoo watches rain the way other people watch rugby.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'bang' means 'certain; gender; sex' — nothing in the English source; it is 2 letters from 'bona', the usual word for 'watch'

rows.en: It's still fifty kilometres away and the stoep is already sold out.
rows.text: E sa le likhilomithara tse mashome a mahlano thoko 'me stoep e se e tletse.
rows.back: It's still fifty kilometres away and the stoep is already full.

rows.en: Rain on a tin roof: the official national lullaby.
rows.text: Pula marulelong a tšepe: pina ea boroko ea naha.
rows.back: Rain on a tin roof: the countryside's lullaby.

rows.en: No sleep app on earth can compete with a tin roof.
rows.text: Ha ho sleep app lefatšeng le ka qothisanang lehlokwa le marulelo a tšepe.
rows.back: No sleep app in the world can compete with a tin roof.

rows.en: Put the phone down. The roof is talking.
rows.text: Beha mohala fatše. Marulelo a bua.
rows.back: Put the phone down. The roof is talking.

rows.en: Free fireworks, no tickets, best seats in the house.
rows.text: Fireworks ea mahala, ha ho ditekete, ditulo tse ntle ka ho fetisisa ka tlung.
rows.back: Free fireworks, no tickets, best seats in the house.

rows.en: The Highveld doesn't do subtle, and honestly we're grateful.
rows.text: Highveld ha e etse dintho ka bonolo, 'me ka nnete rea leboha.
rows.back: The Highveld doesn't do things gently, and honestly, we're grateful.

rows.en: The Boland is getting watered in its sleep and will absolutely brag about it tomorrow.
rows.text: Boland e nosetsoa borokong 'me ka nnete e tla ithorisa ka hona hosane.
rows.back: The Boland is being watered in its sleep and honestly it'll brag about it tomorrow.

rows.en: The clouds are threatening but probably bluffing.
rows.text: Die wolke dreig maar bluf waarskynlik.
rows.back: The clouds are threatening but probably bluffing.

rows.en: Bring a jacket. Or sunscreen. Or both.
rows.text: Bring 'n baadjie. Of sonbrandroom. Of albei.
rows.back: Bring a jacket. Or sunscreen. Or both.

rows.en: Somewhere between fine and soaked. Good luck.
rows.text: Iewers tussen oukei en pap nat. Sterkte.
rows.back: Somewhere between okay and sopping wet. Good luck.

rows.en: The clouds are just vibing. No promises.
rows.text: Die wolke vibe net. Geen beloftes nie.
rows.back: The clouds are just vibing. No promises.

rows.en: Trust issues with the sky today.
rows.text: Vertroueprobleme met die lug vandag.
rows.back: Trust issues with the sky today.

rows.en: Maybe rain, maybe not. Classic.
rows.text: Mhlawumbe imvula, mhlawumbe cha. Okujwayelekile.
rows.back: Maybe rain, maybe not. Typical.

rows.en: Clouds looking proper suspicious.
rows.text: Amafu abukeka esolisa ngempela.
rows.back: The clouds look really suspicious.

rows.en: Take a brolly just in case, hey.
rows.text: Thatha isambulela uma kungenzeka, hey.
rows.back: Take an umbrella just in case, hey.

rows.en: 50/50 on getting wet. Like a coin toss.
rows.text: 50/50 ukuba manzi. Njengenhlahla.
rows.back: 50/50 on getting wet. Like luck.
rows.note: unsure: 'njengenhlahla' — likely a typo for 'njengenhlanhla' (like luck); 'ihlahla' would be 'bush'
rows.reason: 'Like a coin toss' becomes 'Njengenhlahla', apparently a misspelling of 'njengenhlanhla' (like luck), so the image is softened and the word misreads.
reasons: DRIFT: 'Like a coin toss' becomes 'Njengenhlahla', apparently a misspelling of 'njengenhlanhla' (like luck), so the image is softened and the word misreads.

rows.en: Don't trust those clouds. They're plotting.
rows.text: Ungawathembi lawo mafu. Ayaceba.
rows.back: Don't trust those clouds. They're scheming.
rows.note: unsure: 'Ayaceba' — isiZulu 'ceba' = tell tales / snitch; 'scheme/plot' is the isiXhosa sense
rows.reason: 'They're plotting' becomes 'Ayaceba'. In isiZulu 'ceba' means tell tales/snitch; 'plot' is the isiXhosa sense.
reasons: DRIFT: 'They're plotting' becomes 'Ayaceba'. In isiZulu 'ceba' means tell tales/snitch; 'plot' is the isiXhosa sense.

rows.en: Weather's being more indecisive than you at Spur.
rows.text: Isimo sezulu asikwazi ukuzinquma njengawe eSpur.
rows.back: The weather can't make up its mind, like you at the Spur.

rows.en: Pack an umbrella. Or don't. We don't know either.
rows.text: Phaka isambulela. Noma ungaphaki. Asazi nathi.
rows.back: Pack an umbrella. Or don't. We don't know either.
rows.note: 'Phaka' = dish up/serve food in isiZulu; read as 'pack' only from context
rows.reason: 'Pack an umbrella' becomes 'Phaka isambulela', and 'phaka' means dish up/serve food in isiZulu, a wrong-sense verb.
reasons: DRIFT: 'Pack an umbrella' becomes 'Phaka isambulela', and 'phaka' means dish up/serve food in isiZulu, a wrong-sense verb.

rows.en: The sky can't make up its mind. Join the club.
rows.text: Isibhakabhaka asikwazi ukuzinquma. Joyina iklabhu.
rows.back: The sky can't make up its mind. Join the club.

rows.en: The clouds are threatening but probably bluffing.
rows.text: Amafu ayesabisa kodwa cishe ayakhohlisa.
rows.back: The clouds look threatening but they're probably bluffing.

rows.en: Forecast says maybe. We say probably.
rows.text: Isibikezelo sithi mhlawumbe. Sithi cishe.
rows.back: The forecast says maybe. We say probably.

rows.en: Bring a jacket. Or sunscreen. Or both.
rows.text: Letha ijazi. Noma isivikelo selanga. Noma kokubili.
rows.back: Bring a jacket. Or sunscreen. Or both.

rows.en: The sky's giving mixed signals again.
rows.text: Isibhakabhaka siphinda sinikeze izimpawu ezixubile.
rows.back: The sky is giving mixed signals again.

rows.en: Rain? Possibly. Commitment? Never.
rows.text: Imvula? Kungenzeka. Ukuzibophezela? Soze.
rows.back: Rain? Maybe. Commitment? Never.

rows.en: This weather needs a life coach.
rows.text: Lesi simo sezulu sidinga umqeqeshi wempilo.
rows.back: This weather needs a life coach.

rows.en: Schrodinger's rain. It both is and isn't.
rows.text: Imvula ka-Schrödinger. Iyakhona futhi ayikho.
rows.back: Schrödinger's rain. It's there and it isn't.

findings: HIGH morphology: diacritic in a Nguni line

rows.en: The washing's on the line and you're feeling brave.
rows.text: Izingubo zisemsebenzini futhi uzizwa unesibindi.
rows.back: The clothes are 'at work' and you're feeling brave.
rows.note: unsure: 'zisemsebenzini' = are at work — presumably 'washing is out on the line'
rows.reason: 'The washing's on the line' becomes 'Izingubo zisemsebenzini' (the clothes are at work), which loses the key detail.
