reasons: WRONG SOURCE? The back-translation is closer to another line of the same bin: "The sky is buffering."

rows.en: The clouds are committed to being average.
rows.text: Maru a itlamile ho ba karolelano.
rows.back: The clouds have committed to being average.

findings: HIGH contamination: 'itlamile' is attested in tn (29× leipzig/nchlt/dictionary) but in no external st source (only in this app's own copy)

rows.en: Nothing to see here. Literally.
rows.text: Ha ho letho leo ho le bonwang mona. Ka nnete.
rows.back: Nothing to see here. Really.

rows.en: The sky picked a vibe and the vibe is shrug.
rows.text: Lehodimo le kgethile vibe mme vibe ke ho phahamisa mahetla.
rows.back: The sky picked a vibe and the vibe is a shrug.

rows.en: Cloud cover with a side of who-cares.
rows.text: Maru le lehlakore la mang ea tsotellang.
rows.back: Clouds with a side of who cares.
rows.note: calque of 'with a side of'; 'lehlakore' = side of a thing/place, not a food side-order.

rows.en: The sun's on airplane mode.
rows.text: Letsatsi le ho airplane mode.
rows.back: The sun is on airplane mode.

rows.en: A perfectly average sky doing perfectly average things.
rows.text: Lehodimo le karolelano le etsang dintho tsa karolelano.
rows.back: An average sky doing average things.

rows.en: The clouds RSVP'd 'maybe' and showed up anyway.
rows.text: Maru a arabile 'mohlomong' empa a fihlile.
rows.back: The clouds replied 'maybe' but they showed up.

rows.en: Today's weather: still loading.
rows.text: Lehodimo la kajeno: le sa loadhella.
rows.back: Today's sky: still loading.

rows.en: The sky is the colour of an old Tupperware lid.
rows.text: Lehodimo le na le 'mala oa sekwahelo sa Tupperware sa kgale.
rows.back: The sky is the colour of an old Tupperware lid.
rows.note: ''mala' = Lesotho spelling of colour (SA: mmala); house list flags it (mala = entrails); Lesotho 'oa'.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'mala' means 'entrails' — nothing in the English source; it is 2 letters from 'mebala', the usual word for 'colour'

rows.en: Forecast: vibes neutral, expectations lower.
rows.text: Ponelopele: vibes li bohareng, ditebello li tlase.
rows.back: Forecast: vibes medium, expectations low.

rows.en: The sun is technically present. Spiritually elsewhere.
rows.text: Letsatsi ka tsela ea ts'ebetso le teng. Ka moya le sebakeng se seng.
rows.back: Technically the sun is here. In spirit, it's somewhere else.

rows.en: The sun hit snooze again. Honestly? Same.
rows.text: Letsatsi le tobetse snooze hape. Ka nnete? Le nna.
rows.back: The sun hit snooze again. Honestly? Me too.

rows.en: Early grey. Like the tea, just let it steep.
rows.text: Lehodimo le lerootho hoseng. Jwalo ka tee, le tlohele le eme feela.
rows.back: A grey sky in the morning. Like tea, just let it stand.
rows.reason: The 'Early grey' / Earl Grey pun is lost; ST just says 'a grey sky in the morning... like tea' (hard to carry over).
reasons: DRIFT: The 'Early grey' / Earl Grey pun is lost; ST just says 'a grey sky in the morning... like tea' (hard to carry over).

rows.en: The day is starting on eco-mode. Hop in anyway.
rows.text: Letsatsi le qala ka eco-mode. Kena feela.
rows.back: The sun is starting in eco-mode. Just get in (go with it).
rows.note: 'Kena feela' = just get in/enter - odd; maybe 'just go with it'.
rows.reason: 'Kena feela' = 'hop in'.

rows.en: Morning is coming in soft, almost like an apology.
rows.text: Hoseng ho kena ka bonolo, hoo e batlang e le boitšoarelo.
rows.back: The morning comes in gently, almost like an apology.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'batlang' means 'seeking' — nothing in the English source; it is 3 letters from 'batlile', the usual word for 'almost'

rows.en: Under this sky a second coffee isn't a luxury, it's procedure.
rows.text: Tlas'a lehodimo lena kofi ea bobedi ha se manyofonyofo, ke tsela ea ho etsa dintho.
rows.back: Under this sky a second coffee isn't an indulgence, it's how things are done.

rows.en: Washing-line roulette: do you hang, or do you fold?
rows.text: Roulette ya ho aneka: o a aneka, kapa wa mena?
rows.back: Washing roulette: do you hang it out, or do you fold it?
rows.note: 'wa mena' = do you fold (i.e. keep it in).

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'aneka' is attested in xh (kaikki) but in no external st source
MEDIUM contamination: 'aneka' is attested in xh (kaikki) but in no external st source

rows.en: The app says cloudy. Aunty's knee says rain. We trust the knee.
rows.text: App e re ho na le maru. Lengole la 'mangoane le re pula. Re tšepa lengole.
rows.back: The app says cloudy. Auntie's knee says rain. We trust the knee.

rows.en: Chance of rain: maybe. Chance of everyone discussing it: 100%.
rows.text: Monyetla oa pula: mohlomong. Monyetla oa hore bohle ba bue ka eona: 100%.
rows.back: Chance of rain: maybe. Chance everyone talks about it: 100%.

rows.en: The sun is buffering. Do not refresh the page.
rows.text: Letsatsi le a buffera. Se ke wa refresha leqephe.
rows.back: The sun is buffering. Don't refresh the page.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'buffera' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source
MEDIUM lexical: 'refresha' — not found in any external source; closest attested: 'refresh' (1× leipzig, distance 1)

rows.en: 'We'll see how it looks' — South Africa's official RSVP.
rows.text: 'Re tla bona hore le shebahala jwang' — RSVP ea semmuso ea Afrika Borwa.
rows.back: 'We'll see how it looks' - South Africa's official RSVP.

rows.en: The weather is 50/50. We are 100% going anyway.
rows.text: Boemo ba lehodimo bo 50/50. Rona re ea 100% leha ho le jwalo.
rows.back: The weather is 50/50. We're going 100% anyway.

rows.en: Overcast isn't a cancellation, it's ambience.
rows.text: Ho aparetse ka maru ha se ho hlakolwa, ke moya o monate.
rows.back: Overcast isn't cancelled, it's a nice vibe (or: a nice breeze).
rows.note: 'moya o monate' = pleasant breeze or pleasant mood.

rows.en: Duvet weather on a workday. Strength, Mzansi.
rows.text: Boemo ba duvet ka letsatsi la mosebetsi. Matla, Mzansi.
rows.back: Duvet weather on a work day. Strength, Mzansi.

rows.en: The family group says rain. The sky has declined to comment.
rows.text: Group ea lelapa e re pula. Lehodimo le hanne ho fana ka maikutlo.
rows.back: The family group says rain. The sky has declined to comment.

rows.en: Clouds like these mean swing bowling. Ask any oom at the gate.
rows.text: Maru a jwalo a bolela swing bowling. Botsa oom ofe kapa ofe heke.
rows.back: Clouds like these mean swing bowling. Ask any oom at the gate.

rows.en: The chops don't know it's cloudy. The braai proceeds.
rows.text: Lichopo ha di tsebe hore ho na le maru. Braai e tswela pele.
rows.back: The chops don't know it's cloudy. The braai goes on.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'Lichopo' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source; closest attested: 'likhopo' (2× wiki, distance 1)
MEDIUM semantic: 'tsebe' means 'ear' — nothing in the English source; it is 1 letter from 'tseba', the usual word for 'know'

rows.en: The sky is in its interview suit: grey, neat, giving nothing away.
rows.text: Lehodimo le apere suit ya interview: le lerootho, le hlwekile, ha le fane ka letho.
rows.back: The sky is wearing its interview suit: grey, neat, giving nothing away.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'fane' means 'gave; provided; rendered' — nothing in the English source; it is 1 letter from 'fang', the usual word for 'giving'

rows.en: Weekend grey: official permission to do absolutely nothing.
rows.text: Lerootho la mafelo-beke: tumello ea semmuso ea ho se etse letho.
rows.back: Weekend grey: official permission to do nothing.

rows.en: It's rusk-dunking weather, and that is not up for debate.
rows.text: Ke boemo ba ho ina di-rusk, 'me hoo ha ho buisanwe ka hona.
rows.back: It's rusk-dunking weather, and that's non-negotiable.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'di-rusk' is an English word with no st attestation and is not in the English source line

rows.en: Clouds rolling in like family — no phone call first.
rows.text: Maru a kena jwalo ka lelapa — ntle le ho letsetsa pele.
rows.back: The clouds come in like family - without calling first.

rows.en: Free studio lighting today. Take the selfie.
rows.text: Studio lighting ea mahala kajeno. Nka selfie.
rows.back: Free studio lighting today. Take a selfie.

rows.en: These clouds have rehearsed a storm all day. It never shows up for the audition.
rows.text: Maru ana a itokiseditse sefefo letsatsi lohle. Ha se ka sa fihla audition-eng.
rows.back: These clouds have been preparing to be a storm all day. It never made it to the audition.

rows.en: Grey day equals baking day. Somebody's kitchen already smells amazing.
rows.text: Letsatsi le lerootho ke letsatsi la ho baka. Kitchen ea motho e se e nkga hamonate.
rows.back: A grey day is a baking day. Someone's kitchen already smells lovely.

rows.en: Tonight's sunset is behind a paywall.
rows.text: Ho dikela ha letsatsi bosiung bona ho ka morao ho paywall.
rows.back: Tonight's sunset is behind a paywall.

rows.en: No sunset pics tonight. The sky's privacy settings are on.
rows.text: Ha ho difoto tsa ho dikela ha letsatsi bosiu bona. Li-privacy settings tsa lehodimo li bulehile.
rows.back: No sunset photos tonight. The sky's privacy settings are open.
rows.note: 'li bulehile' = are open - contradicts the privacy joke; Lesotho 'Li-'.
rows.reason: 'li bulehile' (are open) can be read as 'public', which undercuts 'privacy settings are on' (it only works if read as 'switched on').
reasons: DRIFT: 'li bulehile' (are open) can be read as 'public', which undercuts 'privacy settings are on' (it only works if read as 'switched on').

rows.en: The sun clocked out without saying bye. Rude, but relatable.
rows.text: Letsatsi le clock-ile ntle le ho re tsamaya hantle. Ha se botho, empa rea utloisisa.
rows.back: The sun clocked off without saying goodbye. Not polite, but we understand.

rows.en: The day is going out like a candle, not a firework. Respect.
rows.text: Letsatsi le tima jwalo ka kerese, eseng firework. Hlompho.
rows.back: The sun goes out like a candle, not a firework. Respect.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'kerese' — not found in any external source; closest attested: 'kereke' (216× kaikki/leipzig/wiki/dictionary, distance 1)

rows.en: Looks like the clouds are staying for supper.
rows.text: Ho bonahala maru a sala bakeng sa dijo tsa mantsiboya.
rows.back: Looks like the clouds are staying for dinner.

rows.en: The day is ending like a voicenote that just cuts off mid-
rows.text: Letsatsi le fela jwalo ka voicenote e kgaolwang har'a—
rows.back: The day ends like a voice note cut off in the middle of-

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'fela' is a tn function-word marker (tn 2556× vs st 232×)

rows.en: Dusk is on mute tonight. The evening showed up anyway.
rows.text: Ho dikela ho ho mute bosiu bona. Mantsiboya a fihlile leha ho le jwalo.
rows.back: The sunset is on mute tonight. Evening arrived anyway.

rows.en: The day is logging off without drama. We'll take that.
rows.text: Letsatsi le loga off ntle le drama. Re tla amohela hoo.
rows.back: The sun logs off without drama. We'll take that.

findings: HIGH contamination: 'loga' is attested in tn (33× leipzig/nchlt/dictionary) but in no external st source

rows.en: Tonight's sunset is an indoors-only event.
rows.text: Ho dikela ha letsatsi bosiu bona ke ketsahalo ea ka hare feela.
rows.back: Tonight's sunset is an internal event only.
rows.reason: 'ketsahalo ea ka hare' = indoors event.

rows.en: No colours in the sky tonight, just shades of calm.
rows.text: Ha ho mebala lehodimong bosiu bona, ke mefuta ea kgutso feela.
rows.back: No colours in the sky tonight, just shades of quiet.

rows.en: The sky is under the covers. Yours are waiting. Coincidence? Never.
rows.text: Lehodimo le ka tlas'a dikobo. Tsa hao di o emetse. Ho sa rerwa? Le kgale.
rows.back: The sky is under the blankets. Yours are waiting for you. Plans? Never.
rows.note: unsure: 'Ho sa rerwa? Le kgale.' - 'still being planned? never' - meaning unclear.
rows.reason: 'Ho sa rerwa? Le kgale.' reads 'Unplanned? Never.', which is equivalent to 'Coincidence? Never.' (my blind reading of 'sa' was off).

rows.en: The clouds switched off the big light. Go to bed, Mzansi.
rows.text: Maru a timile lebone le leholo. Eya robala, Mzansi.
rows.back: The clouds switched off the big light. Go to sleep, Mzansi.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'timile' is attested in tn (1× leipzig) but in no external st source

rows.en: No stars tonight, but the neighbourhood dogs still have opinions.
rows.text: Ha ho dinaledi bosiu bona, empa dintja tsa tikoloho di sa na le maikutlo.
rows.back: No stars tonight, but the neighbourhood dogs still have opinions.

rows.en: The sky is on aeroplane mode. No notifications till morning.
rows.text: Lehodimo le ho airplane mode. Ha ho di-notification ho fihlela hoseng.
rows.back: The sky is on airplane mode. No notifications until morning.

rows.en: The moon has hung out a do-not-disturb sign.
rows.text: Kgwedi e leketlisitse letswao la 'se ke wa nkgathatsa'.
rows.back: The moon has hung up a 'do not disturb' sign.

findings: MEDIUM morphology: 'leketlisitse' is unattested but splits into attested 'leke' + 'tlisitse' — fused word boundary?

rows.en: The sky's curtains are drawn. Privacy, please.
rows.text: Dikgaratene tsa lehodimo di kwetswe. Privacy, ka kopo.
rows.back: The sky's curtains are closed. Privacy, please.

rows.en: The moon has signal tonight, just no bars.
rows.text: Kgwedi e na le signal bosiu bona, empa ha ho bars.
rows.back: The moon has signal tonight, but no bars.

rows.en: Tomorrow is a fresh negotiation with the weather. Tonight we rest.
rows.text: Hosane ke puisano e ntjha le boemo ba lehodimo. Bosiu bona rea phomola.
rows.back: Tomorrow is a new conversation with the weather. Tonight we rest.

rows.en: The night has thrown a weighted blanket over everything.
rows.text: Bosiu bo lahletse kobo e boima holim'a tsohle.
rows.back: The night has thrown a heavy blanket over everything.

rows.en: Night clouds are the sky's way of saying: let's talk tomorrow.
rows.text: Maru a bosiu ke tsela ya lehodimo ya ho re: a re bue hosane.
rows.back: Night clouds are the sky's way of saying: let's talk tomorrow.

rows.en: Somewhere a braai is down to its last coals, no stars — the conversation carries the night.

rows.back: Somewhere a braai is down to its last coals, no stars - the conversation is carrying the night.

rows.en: Night-shift clouds: just keeping the place warm till the sun gets back.
rows.text: Maru a night-shift: a boloka sebaka se futhumetse ho fihlela letsatsi le kgutla.
rows.back: Night-shift clouds: keeping the place warm until the sun comes back.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'sebaka' means 'area; distance; scene' — nothing in the English source; it is 2 letters from 'seka', the usual word for 'place'

rows.en: The sky put the stars on silent. They're still up there, promise.
rows.text: Lehodimo le behile dinaledi ho silent. Di sa ntsane di le teng hodimo, ke a tshepisa.
rows.back: The sky has put the stars on silent. They're still up there, I promise.

rows.text: Boemo ba ho robala ba maemo a hodimo. Maru a netefaditse hoo.
rows.back: Top-level sleeping conditions. The clouds have confirmed it.

rows.back: Half-heartedly cloudy.

rows.en: Cloud cover, low effort.

rows.back: Cloudy, but it's not really putting in any effort.

rows.back: Show-off clouds today.

rows.back: Halfway to a Highveld storm. Or not.

reasons: DRIFT: The joke is rebuilt as a recipe ('halwe koppie wolke ... resep') in place of 'but make it casual'. The claim of light cloud survives. 'n' is missing its apostrophe.

rows.en: Almost a braai day.

rows.back: Almost a braai day.

rows.en: Sunscreen, but keep a hoodie close.
rows.text: Sonskerm en 'n trui — vat altwee.
rows.back: Sunscreen and a jersey — take both.

rows.en: Indecisive sky energy.

rows.back: Sky on a maybe-vibe.

rows.text: Moya oa bosiu bona o na le maikutlo.
rows.back: Tonight's wind is in a mood.

rows.en: The wind swept the clouds away so you could see the stars. Apologies about everything else.
rows.text: Moya o feetse maru hore o tle o bone dinaledi. Boitšoarelo ka tse ding tsohle.
rows.back: The wind swept the clouds away so you can see the stars. Sorry about everything else.

rows.en: Karoo white noise: one windpump, no off switch.
rows.text: White noise ea Karoo: windpomp e le 'ngoe, ha ho konopo ea ho tima.
rows.back: Karoo white noise: one windpump, no off switch.

rows.en: Tonight you're not counting sheep, you're counting gusts.
rows.text: Bosiu bona ha o bale dinku, o bala meya e fokang ka sefutho.
rows.back: Tonight you're not counting sheep, you're counting gusts.

rows.en: Somebody forgot to bring in the washing. The washing has not forgotten.
rows.text: Motho o lebetse ho kenya diaparo. Diaparo ha di eso lebale.
rows.back: Someone forgot to bring in the washing. The washing hasn't forgotten.

rows.en: Tomorrow morning's first job: a search party.
rows.text: Mosebetsi oa pele oa hosane hoseng: sehlopha sa ho batla.
rows.back: First job tomorrow morning: a search party.

rows.en: Every peg in the village is holding thumbs tonight.
rows.text: Peg e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe motseng e tšoere menwana bosiu bona.
rows.back: Every peg in the village/town is holding its fingers tonight.

rows.reason: SA idiom 'holding thumbs' (hoping) calqued as 'e tšoere menwana' (gripping fingers), which reads literally as pegs pinching; the hoping sense is lost.

rows.en: Cold enough for soup. And a second soup.
rows.text: Koud genoeg vir sop. En 'n tweede sop.
rows.back: Cold enough for soup. And a second soup.

rows.en: Two-fleece minimum today.
rows.text: Twee-fleece minimum vandag.
rows.back: Two-fleece minimum today.

rows.en: The duvet had the right idea this morning.
rows.text: Die duvet het die regte idee gehad vanoggend.
rows.back: The duvet had the right idea this morning.

rows.en: Why did you leave the house? Honestly.
rows.text: Hoekom het jy die huis verlaat? Eerlik.
rows.back: Why did you leave the house? Honestly.

rows.en: Three pairs of socks and still not enough.
rows.text: Drie pare sokkies en steeds nie genoeg nie.
rows.back: Three pairs of socks and still not enough.

rows.en: Rooibos consumption just doubled.
rows.text: Rooibos-verbruik het net verdubbel.
rows.back: Rooibos consumption just doubled.

rows.en: The duvet understood the assignment.
rows.text: Die duvet het die opdrag verstaan.
rows.back: The duvet understood the assignment.

rows.en: The kettle is working harder than anyone today.
rows.text: Die ketel werk harder as enigiemand vandag.
rows.back: The kettle is working harder than anyone today.

rows.en: Nobody signed up for this temperature.
rows.text: Niemand het hiervoor ingeteken nie.
rows.back: Nobody signed up for this.

rows.en: Your motivation froze on the way to the door.
rows.text: Jou motivering het gevries op pad deur toe.
rows.back: Your motivation froze on the way to the door.

rows.en: The couch has made a compelling case for staying.
rows.text: Die bank het 'n oortuigende saak gemaak vir bly.
rows.back: The couch made a convincing case for staying.

rows.en: Why did past-you make plans? Past-you is the worst.
rows.text: Hoekom het verlede-jy planne gemaak? Verlede-jy is die ergste.
rows.back: Why did past-you make plans? Past-you is the worst.

rows.en: Even the geyser is putting in extra hours.
rows.text: Selfs die geyser sit ekstra ure in.
rows.back: Even the geyser is putting in extra hours.

rows.en: You miss your bed and you've been gone twelve minutes.
rows.text: Jy mis jou bed en jy is twaalf minute weg.
rows.back: You miss your bed and you've been gone twelve minutes.

rows.en: The shower was the highlight. It is downhill from here.
rows.text: Die stort was die hoogtepunt. Dit gaan nou afdraand.
rows.back: The shower was the highlight. It's all downhill from here.

rows.en: Coffee count: rising. Motivation count: still zero.
rows.text: Koffie-telling: styg. Motiverings-telling: steeds nul.
rows.back: Coffee count: rising. Motivation count: still zero.

rows.en: Outside has betrayed you and you went anyway.
rows.text: Buite het jou verraai en jy het in elk geval gegaan.
rows.back: Outside betrayed you and you went anyway.

rows.en: The fridge feels warmer than the lounge today.
rows.text: Die yskas voel warmer as die sitkamer vandag.
rows.back: The fridge feels warmer than the lounge today.

rows.en: First one up puts the kettle on. That's the law.
rows.text: Eerste een op moet die ketel aansit. Dis die wet.
rows.back: First one up has to put the kettle on. It's the law.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'wet' is core English weather vocabulary left untranslated

rows.en: Five more minutes. Okay ten. Okay until the sun reaches the bed.
rows.text: Vyf minute nog. Oukei tien. Oukei tot die son op die bed val.
rows.back: Five more minutes. Okay, ten. Okay, until the sun lands on the bed.

rows.en: Cape cold is wet cold. It moves into your bones and unpacks.
rows.text: Kaapse koue is nat koue. Dit klim in jou bene en pak uit.
rows.back: Cape cold is wet cold. It climbs into your bones and unpacks.

rows.en: The gown is daywear now. We're calling it winter couture.
rows.text: Die kamerjas is nou dagdrag. Ons noem dit winter couture.
rows.back: The dressing gown is daywear now. We call it winter couture.

rows.en: Snow on the mountains means one thing: everyone is going to tell you about it today.
rows.text: Sneeu op die berge beteken een ding: almal gaan dit vandag vir jou sê.
rows.back: Snow on the mountains means one thing: everyone is going to tell you about it today.

rows.en: Getting out of bed was the hardest summit of the day.
rows.text: Uit die bed uit was die moeilikste bergklim van die dag.
rows.back: Getting out of bed was the hardest mountain climb of the day.

rows.en: Two duvets and a prayer. That's the system.
rows.text: Twee duvets en 'n gebed. So oorleef ons.
rows.back: Two duvets and a prayer. That's how we survive.

rows.en: Highveld winter: sunburn and frostbite achievable on the same day.
rows.text: Highveld winter: sonbrand en verkluiming op dieselfde dag moontlik.
rows.back: Highveld winter: sunburn and hypothermia possible on the same day.

rows.en: Joburg winter: jacket in the morning, T-shirt by two, jacket again by four.
rows.text: Joburg-winter: jas in die oggend, T-hemp teen twee, jas weer teen vier.
rows.back: Joburg winter: coat in the morning, T-shirt by two, coat again by four.

rows.en: The flask of tea is the original social network.
rows.text: Die fles tee is die ware sosiale netwerk.
rows.back: The flask of tea is the real social network.

rows.en: Sitting in the sun, complaining about the cold. National sport.
rows.text: Sit in die son, klae oor die koue. Nasionale sport.
rows.back: Sitting in the sun, complaining about the cold. National sport.
rows.note: 'klae' used as verb; standard verb is 'kla'
rows.reason: Grammar: 'klae' is used as the verb; the standard form is 'kla'.

rows.en: The mountains got rain and now think they're in Scotland.
rows.text: Die berge het reën gekry en dink hulle is nou in Skotland.
rows.back: The mountains got rain and now think they're in Scotland.

rows.en: Rooibos was born for exactly this weather. Drink it where it grows.
rows.text: Rooibos is gebore vir presies hierdie weer. Drink dit waar dit groei.
rows.back: Rooibos was born for exactly this weather. Drink it where it grows.

rows.en: The aloes are blooming. They're the only ones enjoying winter.
rows.text: Die aalwyne blom. Hulle is die enigstes wat die winter geniet.
rows.back: The aloes are flowering. They're the only ones enjoying winter.

rows.en: Even the plants have decided orange is the answer to cold.
rows.text: Selfs die plante het besluit oranje is die antwoord op koue.
rows.back: Even the plants have decided orange is the answer to cold.

rows.en: Dress like an aloe: layers on layers, and refuse to fall over.
rows.text: Trek aan soos 'n aalwyn: lae op lae, en bly staan.
rows.back: Dress like an aloe: layer on layer, and stay standing.

rows.en: Snow on the mountains. Every family WhatsApp group now has the same photo.
rows.text: Sneeu op die berge. Elke familiegroep het nou dieselfde foto.
rows.back: Snow on the mountains. Every family group now has the same photo.

rows.en: Close enough to admire, far enough that you don't have to shovel it. Perfect.
rows.text: Naby genoeg om te bewonder, ver genoeg om nie te skep nie. Perfek.
rows.back: Close enough to admire, far enough not to have to shovel it. Perfect.

rows.en: Someone is driving up there 'just to look'. They are going to sit in traffic.
rows.text: Iemand ry nou soontoe 'om te gaan kyk'. Hulle gaan in die verkeer sit.
rows.back: Someone is driving there right now 'to go have a look'. They're going to sit in traffic.

rows.en: The dog took the best spot. Nobody is brave enough to move him.
rows.text: Die hond het die beste plek gevat. Niemand is dapper genoeg om te skuif nie.
rows.back: The dog took the best spot. Nobody is brave enough to move him.
rows.note: 'om te skuif' — move oneself or shift the dog; read as shift the dog

rows.en: Fire lit before noon. We are no longer playing games.
rows.text: Vuur aan voor twaalf. Ons speel nie meer nie.
rows.back: Fire on before twelve. We're not playing anymore.

rows.en: So cold the frost stayed for lunch.
rows.text: So koud dat die ryp middagete gebly het.
rows.back: So cold the frost stayed for lunch.

rows.en: Trout weather. Lovely for the fish. Character-building for the fisherman.
rows.text: Forelweer. Vir die vis is dit lekker. Vir die visserman is dit karakterbou.
rows.back: Trout weather. For the fish it's lovely. For the fisherman it's character-building.

rows.en: The water looks like glass. It feels like ice. Do not run the experiment.
rows.text: Die water lyk soos glas. Dit voel soos ys. Moenie eksperimenteer nie.
rows.back: The water looks like glass. It feels like ice. Don't experiment.

rows.en: Wet sea cold: the kind that gets through four layers and a good mood.
rows.text: Nat koue by die see: die soort wat deur vier lae en 'n goeie humeur trek.
rows.back: Wet cold by the sea: the kind that goes through four layers and a good mood.

rows.en: Today is a fish-and-chips-out-the-paper day. Doctor's orders.
rows.text: Vandag is 'n vis-en-tjips-uit-die-papier dag. Dokter se orders.
rows.back: Today is a fish-and-chips-out-of-the-paper day. Doctor's orders.

rows.en: The seagulls sound furious about it. Same, seagulls. Same.
rows.text: Die meeue klink kwaad. Dieselfde, meeue. Dieselfde.
rows.back: The gulls sound angry. Same, gulls. Same.

rows.en: The sun is leaving and taking all the degrees with it.
rows.text: Die son gaan weg en vat al die grade saam.
rows.back: The sun leaves and takes all the degrees with it.

rows.en: You can watch the cold arriving. It's not even being subtle about it.
rows.text: Jy kan die koue sien inkom. Dit maak nie eers geheim daarvan nie.
rows.back: You can see the cold coming in. It doesn't even make a secret of it.

rows.en: Woodsmoke at dusk: the Highveld's winter perfume.
rows.text: Houtrook teen skemer: die Highveld se winterparfuum.
rows.back: Woodsmoke at dusk: the Highveld's winter perfume.

rows.en: Somebody's driving home right now with the heater on full and the seat warmer as a bonus.
rows.text: Iemand ry nou huis toe met die verwarmer op vol en die sitplekverwarmer as bonus.
rows.back: Someone is driving home now with the heater on full and the seat heater as a bonus.

rows.en: The pass is beautiful. The pass is also the opening act for -2°C.
rows.text: Die pas is mooi. Die pas is ook -2°C se voorprogram.
rows.back: The pass is beautiful. The pass is also the opening act for -2°C.

rows.en: Last one home lights the fire. Drive, friend, drive.
rows.text: Laaste een by die huis maak die kaggel aan. Ry, vriend, ry.
rows.back: Last one home lights the fireplace. Drive, friend, drive.

rows.en: Blanket around the shoulders on the stoep: national dress of winter.
rows.text: Kombers om die skouers op die stoep: nasionale drag van die winter.
rows.back: Blanket round the shoulders on the stoep: the national dress of winter.

rows.en: We're visiting outside in the cold because inside is, honestly, colder.
rows.text: Ons kuier buite in die koue want binne is dit, eerlikwaar, kouer.
rows.back: We're visiting outside in the cold because inside it's, honestly, colder.

rows.en: One brazier, three neighbours, zero hurry.
rows.text: Een konka, drie bure, geen haas nie.
rows.back: One konka, three neighbours, no rush.

rows.en: Snow on the Twelve Apostles. Cape Town will talk about this for a week.
rows.text: Sneeu op die Twaalf Apostels. Kaapstad gaan vir 'n week hieroor praat.
rows.back: Snow on the Twelve Apostles. Cape Town will talk about this for a week.

rows.en: At least the cold front left a beautiful receipt.
rows.text: Die koue front het darem 'n mooi kwitansie gelos.
rows.back: The cold front at least left a pretty receipt.

rows.en: Look quickly. By tomorrow it's gone and nobody will believe you.
rows.text: Kyk vinnig. Teen môre is dit weg en niemand gaan jou glo nie.
rows.back: Look quickly. By tomorrow it'll be gone and nobody will believe you.

rows.en: The mountain glows like a fireplace. Unfortunately it only warms the eyes.
rows.text: Die berg gloei soos 'n kaggel. Ongelukkig werk dit net vir die oë.
rows.back: The mountain glows like a fireplace. Unfortunately it only works for the eyes.

rows.en: The blesbok wear no scarves and file no complaints. We could learn something. We won't, but we could.
rows.text: Die blesbokke dra nie serpe nie en kla ook nie. Ons kan iets leer. Ons gaan nie, maar ons kan.
rows.back: The blesbok don't wear scarves and don't complain either. We could learn something. We won't, but we could.

rows.en: Free State dusk: the most beautiful ten minutes of the coldest night.
rows.text: Vrystaat-skemer: die mooiste tien minute van die koudste aand.
rows.back: Free State dusk: the prettiest ten minutes of the coldest evening.

rows.en: The stars shine brighter when it's cold. The universe's way of apologising.
rows.text: Die sterre is helderder as dit koud is. Die heelal se manier van jammer sê.
rows.back: The stars are brighter when it's cold. The universe's way of saying sorry.

rows.en: Five minutes of stargazing. Then you run back inside. That's the deal.
rows.text: Vyf minute sterre kyk. Dan hardloop jy terug binnetoe. Dis die deal.
rows.back: Five minutes of stargazing. Then you run back inside. That's the deal.

rows.en: Somewhere under those stars, someone is tiptoeing barefoot to the bathroom. Strength.
rows.text: Iewers onder daardie sterre trippel iemand kaalvoet badkamer toe. Sterkte.
rows.back: Somewhere under those stars someone is tiptoeing barefoot to the bathroom. Good luck.

rows.back: Outside: 2 degrees. Inside: 9 degrees and a very good fire. SA houses, hey.

rows.en: The last log is a decision, not an inventory item.

rows.back: The last log is a decision, not an inventory item.

rows.en: Rain sounds lovely on the roof. Provided you are not in it.

rows.back: The rain sounds lovely on the roof. As long as you're NOT out in it.

rows.en: Cape winter night: the mountain's still there, you'll see it again tomorrow.
rows.text: Kaapse winternag: die berg is daar, jy sal hom môre weer sien.
rows.back: Cape winter night: the mountain is there, you'll see him again tomorrow.

rows.text: Elektriese kombers weer vergeet om vooraf aan te sit. Elke. Enkele. Aand.
rows.back: Forgot to switch the electric blanket on in advance again. Every. Single. Night.

rows.back: The Berg is wearing snow tonight. Somewhere a farmer's dog is already inside the house.

rows.back: That one little light is someone doing winter right: hut, fire, done.

rows.en: Beautiful enough to climb out of the blanket for a photo. Almost.
rows.text: Mooi genoeg om vir 'n foto uit die kombers uit te klim. Amper.
rows.back: Pretty enough to climb out of the blanket for a photo. Almost.

rows.en: The town decided at seven that it's blanket time. The town is correct.
rows.text: Die dorp het sewe-uur al besluit dis kombers-tyd. Die dorp is reg.
rows.back: The town decided at seven already that it's blanket time. The town is right.

rows.text: Nat en koud is die Kaap se winterresep. Twee bestanddele, elke keer.
rows.back: Wet and cold is the Cape's winter recipe. Two ingredients, every time.

rows.text: Laaste een wat toemaak, los asseblief die liggie aan. Dit lyk mooi.
rows.back: Last one to close up, please leave the light on. It looks pretty.

rows.en: Ja, it's jersey weather. Double jersey.

rows.back: Yes, it's jersey time. A double jersey.

rows.back: Time to dig out the ugly beanie.

rows.en: Cold enough for soup. And a second soup.
rows.text: Kubanda ngokwanele kwesobho. Nesobho lesibili.
rows.back: Cold enough for soup. And a second soup.

rows.en: Hot chocolate is not a want. It's a need.

rows.back: Hot chocolate isn't a wish. It's a need.

rows.en: Layer up like you're climbing Sani Pass.

rows.en: Why did past-you make plans? Past-you is the worst.
rows.text: Kungani wena-wesikhathi-esidlule wenze izinhlelo? Wena-wesikhathi-esidlule mubi.
rows.back: Why did past-you make plans? Past-you is awful.

rows.en: The duvet is calling and the duvet is winning.
rows.text: I-duvet iyabiza futhi i-duvet iyaphumelela.
rows.back: The duvet is calling and the duvet is winning.
rows.note: 'iyabiza' = calls / is expensive; context gives calls

rows.en: Even the geyser is putting in extra hours.
rows.text: Ngisho ne-geyser isebenza amahora engeziwe.
rows.back: Even the geyser is working overtime.

rows.en: You miss your bed and you've been gone twelve minutes.
rows.text: Ukhumbula umbhede wakho futhi sekuyimizuzu eyishumi nambili uhambile.
rows.back: You miss your bed and it's been twelve minutes since you left.

rows.en: The shower was the highlight. It is downhill from here.
rows.text: Ishawa kwakuyinto enhle. Konke kuya phansi manje.
rows.back: The shower was nice. It's all downhill from here.

rows.en: Your toes have filed a formal complaint.
rows.text: Izinzwane zakho zifake isikhalazo esisemthethweni.
rows.back: Your toes have lodged an official complaint.

rows.en: Coffee count: rising. Motivation count: still zero.
rows.text: Ukubalwa kwekhofi: kuyenyuka. Ukubalwa kogqozi: kusewuziro.
rows.back: Coffee count: rising. Motivation count: still zero.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'kusewuziro' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source

rows.en: Outside has betrayed you and you went anyway.
rows.text: Ngaphandle kukukhaphele futhi noma kunjalo uhambile.
rows.back: Outside saw you off, and you went anyway.
rows.note: unsure: 'kukukhaphele' — 'khaphela' = escort / see off; does not fit well; maybe 'warned you' was meant
rows.reason: 'kukukhaphele' = betrayed you (khaphela = betray, Leipzig Bible text); blind read was unsure.

rows.en: The fridge feels warmer than the lounge today.
rows.text: Ifriji ibonakala ifudumele kunelawunji namuhla.
rows.back: The fridge seems warmer than the lounge today.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'kunelawunji' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source

rows.en: The house is colder inside than outside. Architecture is a beautiful thing.
rows.text: Indlu ibanda ngaphakathi kunangaphandle. I-architecture yinto enhle.
rows.back: The house is colder inside than outside. Architecture is a lovely thing.

rows.en: First one up puts the kettle on. That's the law.
rows.text: Owokuqala ukuvuka ubeka iketela. Wumthetho lowo.
rows.back: The first one up puts the kettle on. That's the rule.

rows.en: Five more minutes. Okay ten. Okay until the sun reaches the bed.
rows.text: Eminye imizuzu emihlanu. Kulungile eyishumi. Kulungile kuze ilanga lifike embhedeni.
rows.back: Five more minutes. OK, ten. OK, until the sun reaches the bed.

rows.en: The dog looked out the front door, turned around, and went back to bed. Says it all.
rows.text: Inja ibuke ngomnyango wangaphambili, yaphenduka, yabuyela embhedeni. Kusho konke.
rows.back: The dog looked at the front door, turned around, went back to bed. Says it all.

rows.en: Frost on the grass, frost on the bakkie, frost on my will to live.
rows.text: Isithwathwa otshanini, isithwathwa ku-bakkie, isithwathwa entandweni yami yokuphila.
rows.back: Frost on the grass, frost on the bakkie, frost on my will to live.

rows.en: Most beautiful time of day. Say the people who stay inside.
rows.text: Isikhathi esihle kunazo zonke zosuku. Kusho abantu abahlala ngaphakathi.
rows.back: The best time of day. Say the people who stay indoors.

rows.en: Cape cold is wet cold. It moves into your bones and unpacks.
rows.text: Amakhaza aseKapa amanzi. Angena emathanjeni akho akhiphe impahla.
rows.back: Cape cold is wet. It gets into your bones and unpacks its bags.
rows.note: 'akhiphe impahla' = takes out the goods/luggage, read as 'unpacks'

rows.en: The gown is daywear now. We're calling it winter couture.
rows.text: Igawuni manje isivunyelwe emini. Sesiyibiza nge-winter couture.
rows.back: The dressing gown is now allowed in the daytime. We call it winter couture.

rows.en: Somewhere out there people are going for a run right now. Strength to them.
rows.text: Ndawana laphaya abantu bayagijima njengamanje. Amandla kubo.
rows.back: Somewhere out there people are running right now. Power to them.
rows.note: unsure: 'Ndawana' — 'a little place' / somewhere; not the standard adverb (kwenye indawo)

rows.en: Snow on the mountains means one thing: everyone is going to tell you about it today.
rows.text: Iqhwa ezintabeni lisho into eyodwa: wonke umuntu uzokutshela ngalo namuhla.
rows.back: Snow on the mountains means one thing: everyone will tell you about it today.

rows.en: Getting out of bed was the hardest summit of the day.
rows.text: Ukuphuma embhedeni bekuyisiqongo esinzima kunazo zonke zosuku.
rows.back: Getting out of bed was the hardest summit of the day.

rows.en: Two duvets and a prayer. That's the system.
rows.text: Ama-duvet amabili nomthandazo. Yiwo umgomo lowo.
rows.back: Two duvets and a prayer. That's the plan.

rows.en: The sun is out. It means nothing. The sun is lying.
rows.text: Ilanga liphumile. Alisho lutho. Ilanga liqamba amanga.
rows.back: The sun is out. It means nothing. The sun is lying.

rows.en: Highveld winter: sunburn and frostbite achievable on the same day.
rows.text: Ubusika be-Highveld: ukusha kwelanga nokuluma kwamakhaza kungenzeka ngosuku olulodwa.
rows.back: Highveld winter: sunburn and the bite of the cold can happen on the same day.

rows.en: Joburg winter: jacket in the morning, T-shirt by two, jacket again by four.
rows.text: Ubusika baseJoburg: ijazi ekuseni, i-T-shirt ngo-2, ijazi futhi ngo-4.
rows.back: Joburg winter: coat in the morning, T-shirt at 2, coat again at 4.

rows.en: The flask of tea is the original social network.
rows.text: Iflaski yetiye iyi-social network yangempela yokuqala.
rows.back: The flask of tea is the original social network.

rows.en: Sitting in the sun, complaining about the cold. National sport.
rows.text: Ukuhlala elangeni, ukhononda ngamakhaza. Umdlalo wesizwe.
rows.back: Sitting in the sun, complaining about the cold. The national sport.

rows.en: The mountains got rain and now think they're in Scotland.
rows.text: Izintaba zithole imvula manje zicabanga ukuthi ziseScotland.
rows.back: The mountains got rain and now think they're in Scotland.

rows.en: Rooibos was born for exactly this weather. Drink it where it grows.
rows.text: I-rooibos yazalelwa khona kanye lesi simo sezulu. Liphuze lapho likhula khona.
rows.back: Rooibos was born for exactly this weather. Drink it where it grows.
rows.reason: Minor concord slip: 'I-rooibos yazalelwa' (cl.9) then 'Liphuze … likhula' (cl.5).

rows.en: Cold plus beautiful is an honest trade. We'll take it.
rows.text: Amakhaza kanye nobuhle kuwukushintshisana okuqotho. Sizokuthatha.
rows.back: Cold and beauty are a fair trade. We'll take it.

rows.en: The washing is not going to dry. We hang it up for hope.
rows.text: Iwashing ngeke yome. Siyilengisa ngethemba.
rows.back: The washing won't dry. We hang it out in hope.

rows.en: The sausage dog has a jersey. He didn't ask for it, but he wears it with dignity.
rows.text: Inja i-sausage inejezi. Ayilicelanga, kodwa iligqoka ngesithunzi.
rows.back: The sausage dog has a jersey on. It didn't ask for it, but it wears it with dignity.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'inejezi' — not found in any external source

rows.en: The aloes are blooming. They're the only ones enjoying winter.
rows.text: Ama-aloe ayakhahlela. Yiwo wodwa athokozela ubusika.
rows.back: The aloes are kicking. They're the only ones enjoying winter.
rows.note: unsure: 'ayakhahlela' = literally 'they kick'; odd if 'flowering/blazing' was meant
rows.reason: 'Ama-aloe ayakhahlela' = the aloes are kicking, not 'blooming'; wrong-sense verb, though the 'only ones enjoying winter' punchline survives.
reasons: DRIFT: 'Ama-aloe ayakhahlela' = the aloes are kicking, not 'blooming'; wrong-sense verb, though the 'only ones enjoying winter' punchline survives.

rows.en: Even the plants have decided orange is the answer to cold.
rows.text: Ngisho nezitshalo sezinqume ukuthi i-orange yimpendulo yamakhaza.
rows.back: Even the plants have decided orange is the answer to the cold.

rows.en: Dress like an aloe: layers on layers, and refuse to fall over.
rows.text: Gqoka njenge-aloe: izingubo phezu kwezingubo, futhi wenqabe ukuwa.
rows.back: Dress like an aloe: layers on layers, and refuse to fall over.

rows.en: Snow on the mountains. Every family WhatsApp group now has the same photo.
rows.text: Iqhwa ezintabeni. Wonke amaqembu omndeni e-WhatsApp manje anesithombe esifanayo.
rows.back: Snow on the mountains. Every family WhatsApp group now has the same photo.

rows.en: Close enough to admire, far enough that you don't have to shovel it. Perfect.
rows.text: Kuseduze ngokwanele ukukubuka, kukude ngokwanele ukuthi awudingi ukukumba. Kuphelele.
rows.back: Close enough to look at, far enough that you don't have to dig it. Perfect.
rows.note: 'ukukubuka' can also read 'to look at you'

rows.en: Someone is driving up there 'just to look'. They are going to sit in traffic.
rows.text: Umuntu ushayela aye phezulu laphaya 'ukuze abuke nje'. Uzohlala ku-traffic.
rows.back: Someone is driving up there 'just to look'. They'll sit in traffic.

rows.en: The dog took the best spot. Nobody is brave enough to move him.
rows.text: Inja ithathe indawo enhle kunazo zonke. Akekho onesibindi esanele sokuyisusa.
rows.back: The dog took the best spot. Nobody has the guts to move it.

rows.en: Fire lit before noon. We are no longer playing games.
rows.text: Umlilo uphenjwe ngaphambi kwemini. Asisadlali.
rows.back: The fire was lit before noon. We're not playing anymore.

rows.en: The great debate: do we switch the heater on too, or are we not made of money?
rows.text: Inkulumo-mpikiswano enkulu: sivula ne-heater, noma asenziwanga ngemali?
rows.back: The great debate: do we put the heater on too, or are we not made of money?

rows.en: So cold the frost stayed for lunch.
rows.text: Kubanda kangangokuthi isithwathwa sasala nesidlo sasemini.
rows.back: So cold that the frost stayed for lunch.

rows.en: The water looks like glass. It feels like ice. Do not run the experiment.
rows.text: Amanzi abukeka njengengilazi. Azwakala njengeqhwa. Ungawenzi lo mzamo.
rows.back: The water looks like glass. Feels like ice. Don't try it.

rows.en: Wet sea cold: the kind that gets through four layers and a good mood.
rows.text: Amakhaza amanzi aselwandle: uhlobo olungena ezingutsheni ezine kanye nomoya omuhle.
rows.back: Wet seaside cold: the kind that gets through four layers and a good attitude.
rows.note: 'Amakhaza amanzi aselwandle' can also parse as 'the cold of the sea water'; 'umoya omuhle' = good spirit or nice wind

rows.en: Today is a fish-and-chips-out-the-paper day. Doctor's orders.
rows.text: Namuhla usuku lwe-fish-and-chips ephepheni. Imiyalo kadokotela.
rows.back: Today is a fish-and-chips-in-paper day. Doctor's orders.

rows.en: The seagulls sound furious about it. Same, seagulls. Same.
rows.text: Izinyoni zolwandle zizwakala zithukuthele ngakho. Nathi, zinyoni. Nathi.
rows.back: The seabirds sound angry about it. Same, birds. Same.
rows.reason: 'seagulls' rendered 'izinyoni zolwandle' (seabirds), which is fine and avoids the izinkonjane error.

rows.en: The sun is leaving and taking all the degrees with it.
rows.text: Ilanga liyahamba lithathe wonke ama-degrees kanye nalo.
rows.back: The sun is leaving and taking all the degrees with it.

rows.en: You can watch the cold arriving. It's not even being subtle about it.
rows.text: Ungawabuka amakhaza efika. Awazifihli nakancane.
rows.back: You can watch the cold coming. It doesn't hide at all.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'Awazifihli' — not found in any external source; closest attested: 'abazifihli' (1× leipzig, distance 1)

rows.en: Woodsmoke at dusk: the Highveld's winter perfume.
rows.text: Intuthu yezinkuni ntambama: iphunga lasebusika le-Highveld.
rows.back: Woodsmoke in the late afternoon: the winter smell of the Highveld.
rows.reason: Time of day shifts: 'ntambama' = afternoon where the English says 'at dusk'; 'perfume' is flattened to 'iphunga' (smell).
reasons: DRIFT: Time of day shifts: 'ntambama' = afternoon where the English says 'at dusk'; 'perfume' is flattened to 'iphunga' (smell).

rows.en: Somebody's driving home right now with the heater on full and the seat warmer as a bonus.
rows.text: Umuntu ushayela eya ekhaya njengamanje ne-heater ivuliwe ngokugcwele ne-seat warmer njenge-bonus.
rows.back: Someone is driving home right now with the heater on full and the seat warmer as a bonus.

rows.en: The pass is beautiful. The pass is also the opening act for -2°C.
rows.text: I-pass inhle. I-pass iphinde ibe umdlalo wokuvula we--2°C.
rows.back: The pass is beautiful. The pass is also the opening match of -2°C.
rows.note: unclear: 'umdlalo wokuvula' = opening match/game; meaning of the second sentence is muddy
rows.reason: 'umdlalo wokuvula' (opening match) renders 'opening act'.

rows.en: Last one home lights the fire. Drive, friend, drive.
rows.text: Owokugcina ekhaya uphemba umlilo. Shayela, mngane, shayela.
rows.back: The last one home lights the fire. Drive, friend, drive.

rows.en: Blanket around the shoulders on the stoep: national dress of winter.
rows.text: Ingubo emahlombe e-stoep: isembatho sesizwe sasebusika.
rows.back: A blanket round the shoulders on the stoep: the national winter garment.

rows.en: We're visiting outside in the cold because inside is, honestly, colder.
rows.text: Sixoxa ngaphandle emakhazeni ngoba ngaphakathi, eqinisweni, kubanda kakhulu.
rows.back: We're chatting outside in the cold because inside, honestly, it's really cold.

rows.en: One brazier, three neighbours, zero hurry.
rows.text: Imbawula eyodwa, omakhelwane abathathu, akukho ukujaha.
rows.back: One brazier (imbawula), three neighbours, no rush.

rows.en: Snow on the Twelve Apostles. Cape Town will talk about this for a week.
rows.text: Iqhwa kwi-Twelve Apostles. IKapa izokhuluma ngalokhu isonto lonke.
rows.back: Snow on the Twelve Apostles. Cape Town will talk about it all week.
rows.reason: Meaning intact, but 'kwi-Twelve Apostles' uses the isiXhosa locative 'kwi-' (isiZulu 'ku-').
reasons: DRIFT: Meaning intact, but 'kwi-Twelve Apostles' uses the isiXhosa locative 'kwi-' (isiZulu 'ku-').

rows.en: At least the cold front left a beautiful receipt.
rows.text: Okungenani amakhaza ashiye irisidi elihle.
rows.back: At least the cold left a nice receipt.

rows.en: Look quickly. By tomorrow it's gone and nobody will believe you.
rows.text: Bheka ngokushesha. Ngakusasa kusuke sekuhambile futhi akekho ozokukholwa.
rows.back: Look quickly. By tomorrow it'll be gone and nobody will believe you.

rows.en: The mountain glows like a fireplace. Unfortunately it only warms the eyes.
rows.text: Intaba ikhanya njengomlilo. Ngeshwa ifudumeza amehlo kuphela.
rows.back: The mountain glows like fire. Sadly it only warms the eyes.

rows.en: Free State dusk: the most beautiful ten minutes of the coldest night.
rows.text: Ukuhwalala eFree State: imizuzu eyishumi emihle kunayo yonke yobusuku obubanda kunabo bonke.
rows.back: Dusk in the Free State: the ten most beautiful minutes of the coldest night.

rows.en: The stars shine brighter when it's cold. The universe's way of apologising.
rows.text: Izinkanyezi zikhanya kakhulu uma kubanda. Indlela yendawo yonke yokuxolisa.
rows.back: The stars shine brightest when it's cold. The universe's way of apologising.

rows.en: Five minutes of stargazing. Then you run back inside. That's the deal.
rows.text: Imizuzu emihlanu yokubuka izinkanyezi. Bese ugijimela ngaphakathi. Yiso isivumelwano.
rows.back: Five minutes of stargazing. Then you run inside. That's the deal.

rows.en: Somewhere under those stars, someone is tiptoeing barefoot to the bathroom. Strength.
rows.text: Ndawana ngaphansi kwalezo zinkanyezi, umuntu uhamba ngamazwane engagqokile eya endlini yangasese. Amandla.
rows.back: Somewhere under those stars, someone is walking barefoot to the outside toilet. Strength.

rows.en: The chair is taken. The dog got there first. Rules are rules.
rows.text: Isihlalo sithathiwe. Inja ifike kuqala. Imithetho yimithetho.
rows.back: The seat is taken. The dog got there first. Rules are rules.

rows.en: Outside: 2 degrees. Inside: 9 degrees and a very good fire. SA homes, hey.
rows.text: Ngaphandle: ama-degree ama-2. Ngaphakathi: ama-degree ama-9 nomlilo omuhle kakhulu. Amakhaya aseSA, hey.
rows.back: Outside: 2 degrees. Inside: 9 degrees and a lovely fire. SA homes, hey.

rows.en: The last log is a decision, not an inventory item.
rows.text: Ugodo lokugcina luyisinqumo, hhayi into esesitokweni.
rows.back: The last log is a decision, not something in stock.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'esesitokweni' — not found in any external source; closest attested: 'esesikolweni' (2× leipzig, distance 2)

rows.en: Rain sounds lovely on the roof. Provided you are not in it.
rows.text: Imvula izwakala imnandi ophahleni. Inqobo nje uma ungekho ngaphansi kwayo.
rows.back: Rain sounds lovely on the roof. As long as you're not under it.

rows.en: Cape winter night: the mountain's still there, you'll see it again tomorrow.
rows.text: Ubusuku basebusika baseKapa: intaba isekhona, uzoyibona futhi kusasa.
rows.back: Cape winter night: the mountain is still there, you'll see it again tomorrow.

rows.en: The Berg is wearing snow tonight. Somewhere a farmer's dog has already moved indoors.
rows.text: I-Berg igqoke iqhwa namuhla ebusuku. Ndawana inja yomlimi isivele ithuthele ngaphakathi.
rows.back: The Berg is wearing snow tonight. Somewhere the farmer's dog has already moved inside.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'namuhla' means 'today' — nothing in the English source (time-of-day clash with 'tonight'); the source's 'moved' would normally be 'hamba' / 'gudluza', none present — but it does co-occur in corpus with 'ebusuku'

rows.en: Beautiful enough to climb out of the blanket for a photo. Almost.
rows.text: Kuhle ngokwanele ukuphuma engutsheni ukuze uthathe isithombe. Cishe.
rows.back: Nice enough to come out from under the blanket to take a photo. Probably.

rows.en: The town decided at seven that it's blanket time. The town is correct.
rows.text: Idolobha linqume ngo-7 ukuthi yisikhathi sengubo. Idolobha liqinisile.
rows.back: The town decided at 7 that it's blanket time. The town is right.

rows.en: Wet and cold is the Cape's winter recipe. Two ingredients, every time.
rows.text: Ukumanzi namakhaza yiresiphi yasebusika yaseKapa. Izithako ezimbili, njalo.
rows.back: Wet and cold is the Cape winter recipe. Two ingredients, always.

rows.en: Last one closing up, please leave the light on. It looks lovely.
rows.text: Owokugcina ovalayo, ngicela ushiye isibani sivuliwe. Sibukeka sihle.
rows.back: Last one to lock up, please leave the light on. It looks lovely.

rows.en: Ja, it's jersey weather. Double jersey.
rows.text: Ewe, lixesha lejezi. Ijezi ephindwe kabini.
rows.back: Yes, it's jersey time. A double jersey.
rows.note: 'ephindwe kabini' = doubled; could read as one jersey folded double or two jerseys

rows.en: Time to dig out that ugly beanie.
rows.text: Ixesha lokumba loo beanie imbi.
rows.back: Time to dig out that ugly beanie.

rows.en: Cold enough for soup. And a second soup.
rows.text: Kuyabanda ngokwaneleyo kwesuphu. Nesuphu yesibini.
rows.back: Cold enough for soup. And a second soup.

rows.en: Hot chocolate is not a want. It's a need.
rows.text: Itshokolethi eshushu ayikokufuna. Yimfuno.
rows.back: Hot chocolate isn't a want. It's a need.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'Itshokolethi' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source; closest attested: 'itshokholethi' (5× leipzig/dictionary, distance 1)

rows.en: Layer up like you're climbing Sani Pass.
rows.text: Fumbelo okungathi uzakunyuka intaba ye Sani Pass
rows.back: Wrap up as if you're about to climb the Sani Pass mountain.
rows.note: unsure: 'Fumbelo' - not a form I recognise; guessed 'bundle up'. Also 'intaba ye Sani Pass' calls a pass a mountain
rows.reason: 'Layer up' is carried by 'Fumbelo', which is not a recognisable isiXhosa verb, and 'intaba ye Sani Pass' turns the pass into a mountain.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'Fumbelo' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source

reasons: DRIFT: 'Layer up' is carried by 'Fumbelo', which is not a recognisable isiXhosa verb, and 'intaba ye Sani Pass' turns the pass into a mountain.

rows.en: Two-fleece minimum today.
rows.text: Ii-fleece ezimbini ubuncinane namhlanje.
rows.back: Two fleeces minimum today.

rows.en: The heater is your best friend. Your only friend.
rows.text: I-heater ngumhlobo wakho omkhulu. Enyanisweni, kuphela kwakhe
rows.back: The heater is your best friend. Actually, your only one.

rows.en: Even the Capetonians are admitting it's cold.
rows.text: Nditsho nabantu baseKapa bayavuma ukuba kuyabanda.
rows.back: Even Capetonians admit it's cold.

rows.en: Your breath is doing special effects.
rows.text: Umphefumlo wakho wenza i-special effects.
rows.back: Your breath is doing special effects.

rows.en: Blanket burrito mode: activated.
rows.text: Imowudi ye-blanket burrito: ivuliwe.
rows.back: Blanket-burrito mode: switched on.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'Imowudi' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source; closest attested: 'irowudi' (1× wiki, distance 1)

rows.en: This is not what the tourism brochure promised.
rows.text: Le ayisiyiyo into eyathenjiswa yibrochure yezokhenketho
rows.back: This is not what the tourism brochure promised.

rows.en: The duvet had the right idea this morning.
rows.text: I-duvet ibinombono ongcono kule ntsasa.
rows.back: The duvet had the better idea this morning.

rows.en: Why did you leave the house? Honestly.
rows.text: Kutheni ushiye indlu? Ngenene.
rows.back: Why did you leave the house? Seriously.

rows.en: Your hands are in your pockets and they're not coming out.
rows.text: Izandla zakho zisepokothweni kwaye aziphumi.
rows.back: Your hands are in your pockets and they're not coming out.

rows.en: Three pairs of socks and still not enough.
rows.text: Izibini ezintathu zee kawusi kodwa kunjalo azonelanga.
rows.back: Three pairs of socks and still not enough.

rows.en: The car seats are freezing. Everything is freezing.
rows.text: Izihlalo zemoto ziyabanda. Yonke into iyabanda.
rows.back: The car seats are cold. Everything is cold.

rows.en: Rooibos consumption just doubled.
rows.text: Ukuselwa kwerooibos kuphindaphindeke kabini ngoku.
rows.back: Rooibos consumption has doubled now.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'kuphindaphindeke' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source

rows.en: The dog refused to go outside. Fair.
rows.text: Nditsho nenja ayivumi ukuphuma phandle. Iyavakala loo nto.
rows.back: Even the dog refuses to go outside. Understandable.
rows.reason: Adds 'Nditsho' (even the dog), harmless.

rows.en: The cold front is here and it brought friends.
rows.text: Ingqele ifikile yaye ize nabahlobo bayo.
rows.back: The cold has arrived and it brought its friends.
rows.reason: 'cold front' rendered as 'Ingqele' (the cold); same joke.

rows.en: You're not cold, you're 'lekker koud'. Big difference.
rows.text: Awugodoli, u “lekker koud”. Mkhulu umahluko.
rows.back: You're not freezing, you're 'lekker koud'. Big difference.
rows.note: Afrikaans 'lekker koud' kept as quoted code-switch

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'koud' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source; closest attested: 'koue' (2× leipzig, distance 1)

rows.en: Getting out of bed was a mistake. A documented one.
rows.text: Ukuvuka yayiyimpazamo. Ebhaliweyo phantsi.
rows.back: Waking up was a mistake. One that's on record (written down).

rows.en: The duvet understood the assignment.
rows.text: I-duvet iyiqondile into efunekayo.

rows.note: 'ha li ea lekana' odd — expected 'ha di a lekana'; mixes li-/di-

rows.en: The car seats are freezing. Everything is freezing.
rows.text: Ditulo tsa koloi li a hatsela. Tsohle li a hatsela.
rows.back: The car seats are freezing. Everything is freezing.

rows.en: Rooibos consumption just doubled.
rows.text: Tšebeliso ea rooibos e sa tswa phethahala habedi.
rows.back: Rooibos use has just been completed twice.
rows.note: unsure: 'e sa tswa phethahala habedi' = 'has just been fulfilled/completed twice' — if 'doubled' was meant, it doesn't say it
rows.reason: 'doubled' becomes 'e sa tswa phethahala habedi' (has just been fulfilled/completed twice); the claim is muddied.
reasons: DRIFT: 'doubled' becomes 'e sa tswa phethahala habedi' (has just been fulfilled/completed twice); the claim is muddied.

rows.en: The dog refused to go outside. Fair.
rows.text: Ntja e hanne ho tswa kantle. Ho lokile.
rows.back: The dog refused to go outside. Fair enough.

rows.en: The cold front is here and it brought friends.
rows.text: Serame se fihlile mme se tlisitse metswalle.
rows.back: The cold/frost has arrived and it brought friends.

rows.en: You're not cold, you're 'lekker koud'. Big difference.
rows.text: ha wa hatsela fela ,o hatsetse haholo phapang e kgolo
rows.back: You're not just cold, you're very cold — big difference.
rows.note: 'fela' is the Setswana form (Sesotho 'feela'); loose punctuation, no capital
rows.reason: The 'lekker koud' punchline is flattened to 'o hatsetse haholo' (you're very cold), and the line uses the Setswana 'fela'.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'fela' is a tn function-word marker (tn 2556× vs st 232×)

reasons: DRIFT: The 'lekker koud' punchline is flattened to 'o hatsetse haholo' (you're very cold), and the line uses the Setswana 'fela'.

rows.en: Getting out of bed was a mistake. A documented one.
rows.text: Ho tsoha e ne e le phoso. E ngotsweng fatshe.
rows.back: Waking up was a mistake. One on record (written down).

rows.en: The duvet understood the assignment.
rows.text: Duvet e utloisitse mosebetsi.
rows.back: The duvet has made the job felt / hurt the job.
rows.note: unsure: 'e utloisitse mosebetsi' — 'utloisa' = make feel/hurt; if 'understood (the assignment)' was meant it would be 'utlwisisitse'. Meaning unclear
rows.reason: 'e utloisitse mosebetsi' says the duvet made the job felt/hurt it, not 'understood the assignment' (that would need 'utlwisisitse').

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'utloisitse' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source; closest attested: 'utlwisise' (26× leipzig/nchlt/morph/wiki/dictionary, distance 2)

reasons: MISMATCH: 'e utloisitse mosebetsi' says the duvet made the job felt/hurt it, not 'understood the assignment' (that would need 'utlwisisitse').

rows.en: Your jacket has a jacket. It's that kind of day.
rows.text: Jase ea hao e na le jase. Ke letsatsi le jwalo.
rows.back: Your jacket has a jacket. It's that kind of day.

rows.en: The kettle is working harder than anyone today.
rows.text: Ketlele e sebetsa ka matla ho feta motho e mong le e mong kajeno.
rows.back: The kettle is working harder than anyone else today.

rows.en: Nobody signed up for this temperature.
rows.text: Ha ho motho ea ingodisitseng bakeng sa mocheso ona.
rows.back: Nobody signed up for this heat.
rows.note: unsure: 'mocheso' = heat/warmth (also temperature) — in a cold line it reads as 'heat'
rows.reason: 'mocheso' can mean temperature; in a cold line some readers may take it as 'heat'.

rows.en: Your motivation froze on the way to the door.
rows.text: Khothatso ea hao e hatsetse tseleng ho ea monyako.
rows.back: Your motivation froze on the way to the door.

rows.en: The couch has made a compelling case for staying.
rows.text: Sofa e entswe nyewe e matla ea ho dula.
rows.back: The sofa has made (lit. 'was made') a strong case for sitting/staying.
rows.note: 'e entswe' is passive ('was made'); active 'e entse' expected
rows.reason: Passive 'e entswe' (was made) where active 'e entse' is needed, so the sofa is no longer the one making the case.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'Sofa' is an English word with no st attestation and is not in the English source line

reasons: DRIFT: Passive 'e entswe' (was made) where active 'e entse' is needed, so the sofa is no longer the one making the case.

rows.en: Outside is a test of character. You're failing.
rows.text: Kantle ke teko ea botho. O a hloleha.
rows.back: Outside is a test of character. You're failing.

rows.en: Hot water bottle is the real MVP today.
rows.text: Botlolo ea metsi a tjhesang ke mohale oa 'nete kajeno.
rows.back: The hot-water bottle is the real hero today.

rows.en: Why did past-you make plans? Past-you is the worst.
rows.text: Hobaneng uena-oa-nakong-e-fetileng o entse merero? Uena-oa-nakong-e-fetileng o mobe.
rows.back: Why did past-you make plans? Past-you is bad.

rows.en: The duvet is calling and the duvet is winning.
rows.text: Duvet e a bitsa mme duvet e a hlola.
rows.back: The duvet is calling and the duvet is winning.

rows.en: Even the geyser is putting in extra hours.
rows.text: Esita le geyser e sebetsa dihora tse eketsehileng.
rows.back: Even the geyser is working overtime.

rows.en: You miss your bed and you've been gone twelve minutes.
rows.text: O hopola bethe ea hao mme o tsoile metsotso e leshome le metso e 'meli.
rows.back: You miss your bed and you've been out for twelve minutes.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'tsoile' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source; closest attested: 'tsohle' (996× leipzig/nchlt/morph/wikt/wiki/constitution/dictionary, distance 1)

rows.en: The shower was the highlight. It is downhill from here.
rows.text: Shaoara e ne e le ntho e ntle ka ho fetisisa. Tsohle li theohela tlase jwale.
rows.back: The shower was the best part. It's all downhill from here.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'Shaoara' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source; closest attested: 'shawara' (3× leipzig/dictionary, distance 1)

rows.en: Your toes have filed a formal complaint.
rows.text: Menwana ea hao e tlisitse tletlebo ka molao.
rows.back: Your fingers have lodged a formal complaint.
rows.reason: English says toes; 'menwana' alone means fingers (toes would be 'menwana ya maoto'). This is a native-bank line.
reasons: DRIFT: English says toes; 'menwana' alone means fingers (toes would be 'menwana ya maoto'). This is a native-bank line.

rows.en: Coffee count: rising. Motivation count: still zero.
rows.text: Palo ea kofi: e nyolohang. Palo ea kgothatso: e ntse e le zero.
rows.back: Coffee count: rising. Motivation count: still zero.

rows.en: Outside has betrayed you and you went anyway.
rows.text: Kantle ho u eka empa u ile ha le jwalo.
rows.back: Outside it's as if you... but you went anyway (?)
rows.note: garbled: 'Kantle ho u eka empa u ile ha le jwalo' does not parse cleanly; 'ha le jwalo' may be a clipped 'leha ho le jwalo' (even so). Meaning unrecoverable
rows.reason: Garbled: 'Kantle ho u eka empa u ile ha le jwalo' does not say 'outside has betrayed you'; only a faint 'you went anyway' survives.
reasons: MISMATCH: Garbled: 'Kantle ho u eka empa u ile ha le jwalo' does not say 'outside has betrayed you'; only a faint 'you went anyway' survives.

rows.en: The fridge feels warmer than the lounge today.
rows.text: Fridge e ikutlwa e futhumetse ho feta lounge kajeno.
rows.back: The fridge feels warmer than the lounge today.

rows.en: The house is colder inside than outside. Architecture is a beautiful thing.
rows.text: Ntlo e bata ka hare ho feta kantle. Architecture ke ntho e ntle.
rows.back: The house is colder inside than outside. Architecture is a beautiful thing.

rows.en: Five more minutes. Okay ten. Okay until the sun reaches the bed.
rows.text: Metsotso e mehlano hape. Ho lokile e leshome. Ho lokile ho fihlela letsatsi le fihla bethe.
rows.back: Five more minutes. Okay, ten. Okay, until the sun reaches the bed.

rows.en: The dog looked out the front door, turned around, and went back to bed. Says it all.
rows.text: Ntja e shebile ka monyako, ea reteleha, ea kgutlela borokong. Ho bolela tsohle.
rows.back: The dog looked out the door, turned round, went back to sleep. That says it all.

rows.en: Frost on the grass, frost on the bakkie, frost on my will to live.
rows.text: Serame jwang, serame bakkie-ng, serame takatsong ea ka ea ho phela.
rows.back: Frost (on the) grass, frost on the bakkie, frost on my will to live.

rows.en: Most beautiful time of day. Say the people who stay inside.
rows.text: Nako e ntle ka ho fetisisa ea letsatsi. Ho bolela batho ba dulang ka hare.
rows.back: The best time of the day. Say the people who stay indoors.

rows.en: The gown is daywear now. We're calling it winter couture.
rows.text: Gown ke seaparo sa motsheare jwale. Re e bitsa winter couture.
rows.back: The dressing gown is daywear now. We call it winter couture.

rows.en: Somewhere out there people are going for a run right now. Strength to them.
rows.text: Kae-kae kantle batho ba ya matha hona jwale. Matla ho bona.
rows.back: Somewhere out there people are running right now. Strength to them.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'hona' means 'this; demonstrative pronoun this; it (absolute pronoun)' — nothing in the English source; it is 1 letter from 'tona', the usual word for 'right'

rows.en: Snow on the mountains means one thing: everyone is going to tell you about it today.
rows.text: Lehlwa dithabeng le bolela ntho e le 'ngoe: bohle ba tla o bolella ka lona kajeno.
rows.back: Snow on the mountains means one thing: everyone will tell you about it today.

rows.en: Getting out of bed was the hardest summit of the day.
rows.text: Ho tsoha bethe e ne e le thaba e boima ka ho fetisisa ho e hlwa kajeno.
rows.back: Getting out of bed was the hardest mountain to climb today.

rows.en: Two duvets and a prayer. That's the system.
rows.text: Di-duvet tse pedi le thapelo. Ke eona system.
rows.back: Two duvets and a prayer. That's the system.

rows.en: The sun is out. It means nothing. The sun is lying.
rows.text: Letsatsi le tjhabile. Ha le bolele letho. Letsatsi le bua leshano.
rows.back: The sun is out. It means nothing. The sun is lying.

rows.en: Highveld winter: sunburn and frostbite achievable on the same day.
rows.text: Mariha a Highveld: ho tjheswa ke letsatsi le ho longwa ke serame ka letsatsi le le leng.
rows.back: Highveld winter: sunburnt and frost-bitten on the same day.

rows.en: Joburg winter: jacket in the morning, T-shirt by two, jacket again by four.
rows.text: Mariha a Joburg: jase hoseng, T-shirt ka hora ya bobedi, jase hape ka hora ya bone.
rows.back: Joburg winter: jacket in the morning, T-shirt at two, jacket again at four.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'bone' is a tn function-word marker (tn 3286× vs st 207×)

rows.en: The flask of tea is the original social network.
rows.text: Flask ea tee ke social network ea pele.
rows.back: A flask of tea is the first/original social network.

rows.en: Sitting in the sun, complaining about the cold. National sport.
rows.text: Ho dula letsatsing, o tletleba ka serame. Papadi ea naha.
rows.back: Sitting in the sun, complaining about the cold. The national sport.

rows.en: The mountains got rain and now think they're in Scotland.
rows.text: Dithaba li fumane pula 'me jwale li nahana hore di Scotland.
rows.back: The mountains got rain and now they think they're Scotland.
rows.note: 'pula' = rain (not snow); 'li ... di Scotland' mixes li/di and lacks copula

rows.en: Rooibos was born for exactly this weather. Drink it where it grows.
rows.text: Rooibos o hlahetse boemo bona ba lehodimo hantle. O nwe moo o hlahang teng.
rows.back: Rooibos was born for this weather. Drink it where it comes from.
rows.note: unsure: 'O nwe moo o hlahang teng' — 'drink where it grows' or 'where you come from'

rows.en: Cold plus beautiful is an honest trade. We'll take it.
rows.text: Ho bata le botle ke kabelano e tšepahalang. Re tla e amohela.
rows.back: Cold and beauty is a fair trade. We'll take it.

rows.en: The washing is not going to dry. We hang it up for hope.
rows.text: Diaparo ha di na ho oma. Re di anega bakeng sa tšepo.
rows.back: The washing won't dry. We hang it out for hope.

findings: HIGH contamination: 'anega' is attested in nso (5× leipzig/dictionary) but in no external st source

rows.en: The sausage dog has a jersey. He didn't ask for it, but he wears it with dignity.
rows.text: Ntja e telele e na le jersey. Ha e a e kopa, empa e e apere ka seriti.
rows.back: The long (sausage?) dog has a jersey. It didn't ask for it, but wears it with dignity.

rows.en: The aloes are blooming. They're the only ones enjoying winter.
rows.text: Di-aloe di a thunya. Ke tsona feela tse thabelang mariha.
rows.back: The aloes are flowering. They're the only ones happy about winter.

rows.en: Even the plants have decided orange is the answer to cold.
rows.text: Esita le dimela di entse qeto ea hore orange ke karabo ea serame.
rows.back: Even the plants have decided orange is the answer to the cold.

rows.en: Dress like an aloe: layers on layers, and refuse to fall over.
rows.text: Apara jwalo ka aloe: diaparo holim'a diaparo, 'me o hane ho wa.
rows.back: Dress like an aloe: layers on layers, and refuse to fall over.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'hane' means 'demonstrative pronoun that (yonder)' — nothing in the English source; it is 1 letter from 'hana', the usual word for 'refuse'

rows.en: Snow on the mountains. Every family WhatsApp group now has the same photo.
rows.text: Lehlwa dithabeng. Group e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe ea lelapa ea WhatsApp jwale e na le foto e tšoanang.
rows.back: Snow on the mountains. Every family WhatsApp group now has the same photo.

rows.en: Close enough to admire, far enough that you don't have to shovel it. Perfect.
rows.text: Haufi ho lekana ho e shebella, hole ho lekana hore o se ke oa e chekella. Perfect.
rows.back: Close enough to watch it, far enough that you don't have to dig it out. Perfect.

rows.en: Someone is driving up there 'just to look'. They are going to sit in traffic.
rows.text: Motho o kganna ho ea hodimo 'ho ea sheba feela'. O tla dula sephethephetheng.
rows.back: Someone is driving up 'just to have a look'. They'll sit in traffic.

rows.en: The dog took the best spot. Nobody is brave enough to move him.
rows.text: Ntja e nkile sebaka se setle ka ho fetisisa. Ha ho motho ea sebete ho e suthisa.
rows.back: The dog took the best spot. Nobody is brave enough to move it.

rows.en: Fire lit before noon. We are no longer playing games.
rows.text: Mollo o tukile pele ho motsheare. Ha re sa bapala.
rows.back: The fire was lit before noon. We're not playing anymore.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'tukile' — not found in any external source; closest attested: 'takile' (1× leipzig, distance 1)

rows.en: The great debate: do we switch the heater on too, or are we not made of money?
rows.text: Ngangisano e kgolo: re bulela heater le eona, kapa ha re a etswa ka tjhelete?
rows.back: The big debate: do we switch on the heater too, or are we not made of money?

rows.en: So cold the frost stayed for lunch.
rows.text: Ho bata hoo serame se saleng bakeng sa lunch.
rows.back: So cold the frost is staying for lunch.

rows.en: Trout weather. Lovely for the fish. Character-building for the fisherman.
rows.text: Boemo ba trout. Bo monate ho tlhapi. Bo aha botho ho motshwasi wa ditlhapi.
rows.back: Trout weather. Lovely for the fish. Builds character for the fisherman.

rows.en: The water looks like glass. It feels like ice. Do not run the experiment.
rows.text: Metsi a shebahala jwalo ka kgalase. A utlwahala jwalo ka leqhwa. Se ke oa etsa teko.
rows.back: The water looks like glass. Feels like ice. Don't test it.

rows.en: Wet sea cold: the kind that gets through four layers and a good mood.
rows.text: Ho bata ho metsi ha lewatle: mofuta o phunyeletsang diaparo tse nne le boikutlo bo botle.
rows.back: Damp sea cold: the kind that goes through four layers and a good attitude.

rows.en: Today is a fish-and-chips-out-the-paper day. Doctor's orders.
rows.text: Kajeno ke letsatsi la fish-and-chips-ka-hare-ho-pampiri. Ditaelo tsa ngaka.
rows.back: Today is a fish-and-chips-in-paper day. Doctor's orders.

rows.en: The sun is leaving and taking all the degrees with it.
rows.text: Letsatsi le a tsamaya le nka li-degree tsohle le lona.
rows.back: The sun is leaving and taking all the degrees with it.

rows.en: You can watch the cold arriving. It's not even being subtle about it.
rows.text: O ka shebella serame se fihla. Ha se ipate le hanyane.
rows.back: You can watch the frost/cold coming in. It isn't hiding at all.

rows.en: Woodsmoke at dusk: the Highveld's winter perfume.
rows.text: Mosi oa patsi ha letsatsi le dikela: perfume ea mariha ea Highveld.
rows.back: Woodsmoke at sunset: the Highveld's winter perfume.

rows.en: Somebody's driving home right now with the heater on full and the seat warmer as a bonus.
rows.text: Motho o kgannela hae hona jwale ka heater e tletseng le seat warmer e le bonus.
rows.back: Someone is driving home right now with the heater on full and the seat warmer as a bonus.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'hona' means 'this; demonstrative pronoun this; it (absolute pronoun)' — nothing in the English source; it is 1 letter from 'tona', the usual word for 'right'

rows.en: The pass is beautiful. The pass is also the opening act for -2°C.
rows.text: Pass e ntle. Pass hape ke selelekela sa -2°C.
rows.back: The pass is beautiful. The pass is also the introduction to -2°C.

rows.en: Blanket around the shoulders on the stoep: national dress of winter.
rows.text: Kobo mahetleng stoep-ong: seaparo sa naha sa mariha.
rows.back: Blanket over the shoulders on the stoep: the national winter outfit.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'stoep-ong' — not found in any external source

rows.en: We're visiting outside in the cold because inside is, honestly, colder.
rows.text: Re etela kantle serameng hobane ka hare, ka nnete, ho bata le ho feta.
rows.back: We visit outside in the cold because inside, honestly, it's even colder.

rows.en: One brazier, three neighbours, zero hurry.
rows.text: Konka e le 'ngoe, baahisane ba bararo, ha ho potlako.
rows.back: One drum fire (konka), three neighbours, no rush.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'Konka' is attested in nso (dictionary) but in no external st source

rows.en: Snow on the Twelve Apostles. Cape Town will talk about this for a week.
rows.text: Lehlwa Twelve Apostles. Cape Town e tla bua ka sena beke eohle.
rows.back: Snow on the Twelve Apostles. Cape Town will talk about this all week.

rows.en: At least the cold front left a beautiful receipt.
rows.text: Bonyane cold front e siile receipt e ntle.
rows.back: At least the cold front left a nice receipt.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'cold' is core English weather vocabulary left untranslated

rows.en: Look quickly. By tomorrow it's gone and nobody will believe you.
rows.text: Sheba kapele. Hosane e tla be e fedile 'me ha ho motho ea tla o dumela.
rows.back: Look quickly. By tomorrow it'll be gone and nobody will believe you.

rows.en: The mountain glows like a fireplace. Unfortunately it only warms the eyes.
rows.text: Thaba e benya jwalo ka mollo. Ka bomadimabe e futhumatsa mahlo feela.
rows.back: The mountain glows like fire. Sadly it only warms the eyes.

rows.en: Free State dusk: the most beautiful ten minutes of the coldest night.
rows.text: Ho dikela ha letsatsi Free State: metsotso e leshome e metle ka ho fetisisa ya bosiu bo batang ka ho fetisisa.
rows.back: Free State sunset: the ten most beautiful minutes of the coldest night.
