rows.en: The stars shine brighter when it's cold. The universe's way of apologising.
rows.text: Dinaledi di benya haholo ha ho bata. Tsela ya bokahohle ea ho kopa tšoarelo.
rows.back: Stars shine brightest when it's cold. The universe's way of saying sorry.

rows.en: Five minutes of stargazing. Then you run back inside. That's the deal.
rows.text: Metsotso e mehlano ea ho shebella dinaledi. Ebe o mathela ka hare. Ke eona deal.
rows.back: Five minutes of stargazing. Then you run inside. That's the deal.

rows.en: Somewhere under those stars, someone is tiptoeing barefoot to the bathroom. Strength.
rows.text: Kae-kae tlas'a dinaledi tseo, motho o hata butle a sa rwala ho ea bathroom. Matla.
rows.back: Somewhere under those stars someone is tiptoeing to the bathroom without wearing (anything on their feet?). Strength.
rows.note: unsure: 'a sa rwala' — not wearing/carrying what? object missing
rows.reason: 'a sa rwala' (not wearing [shoes]) carries 'barefoot' elliptically.

rows.en: The chair is taken. The dog got there first. Rules are rules.
rows.text: Setulo se nkilwe. Ntja e fihlile pele. Melao ke melao.
rows.back: The chair is taken. The dog got there first. Rules are rules.

rows.en: Outside: 2 degrees. Inside: 9 degrees and a very good fire. SA homes, hey.
rows.text: Kantle: di-degree tse 2. Ka hare: di-degree tse 9 le mollo o hotle haholo. Malapa a SA, hey.
rows.back: Outside: 2 degrees. Inside: 9 degrees and a very nice fire. SA homes, hey.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'Malapa' means 'households' — nothing in the English source; it is 3 letters from 'mahae', the usual word for 'homes'

rows.en: The last log is a decision, not an inventory item.
rows.text: Patsi ea ho qetela ke qeto, eseng ntho ea inventory.
rows.back: The last log is a decision, not an inventory item.

rows.en: Rain sounds lovely on the roof. Provided you are not in it.
rows.text: Pula e utlwahala hamonate marulelong. Ha feela o le siyo ka hare ho eona.
rows.back: Rain sounds lovely on the roof. As long as you're not out in it.

rows.en: Cape winter night: the mountain's still there, you'll see it again tomorrow.
rows.text: Bosiu ba mariha ba Cape: thaba e sa ntsane e le teng, o tla e bona hape hosane.
rows.back: Cape winter night: the mountain is still there, you'll see it again tomorrow.

rows.en: Forgot to switch the electric blanket on in advance. Every. Single. Night.
rows.text: Lebetse ho bulela electric blanket esale pele. Bosiu. Bo Bong. Le Bo Bong.
rows.back: Forgot to switch the electric blanket on early. Night. Another. And another. (= night after night)

rows.en: The Berg is wearing snow tonight. Somewhere a farmer's dog has already moved indoors.
rows.text: Berg e apere lehlwa bosiu bona. Kae-kae ntja ea molemi e se e kene ka tlung.
rows.back: The Berg is wearing snow tonight. Somewhere a farmer's dog is already inside the house.

rows.en: That one little light is someone doing winter correctly: hut, fire, done.
rows.text: Lebone leo le le leng le lenyane ke motho ea etsang mariha hantle: mokgoro, mollo, ho fedile.
rows.back: That one small light is someone doing winter properly: a hut, a fire, done.

rows.en: Beautiful enough to climb out of the blanket for a photo. Almost.
rows.text: Ho hotle ho lekana ho tswa ka kobong bakeng sa foto. Hoo e batlang e le.
rows.back: Beautiful enough to come out of the blanket for a photo. Almost.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'kobong' — not found in any external source; closest attested: 'kabong' (12× leipzig/nchlt/morph, distance 1)

rows.en: The town decided at seven that it's blanket time. The town is correct.
rows.text: Toropo e entse qeto ka hora ea supileng hore ke nako ea kobo. Toropo e nepile.
rows.back: The town decided at seven o'clock that it's blanket time. The town is right.

rows.en: Last one closing up, please leave the light on. It looks lovely.
rows.text: Oa ho qetela ho kwala, ka kopo tlohela lebone le tuka. Le shebahala hamonate.
rows.back: Last one to lock up, please leave the light on. It looks lovely.

rows.en: Bloemfontein at 6am: jersey, gown, scarf, takkies, and a brave face.
rows.text: Bloemfontein om 6vm: trui, kamerjas, serp, takkies, en 'n gesig wat maak of alles fine is.
rows.back: Bloemfontein at 6am: jersey, dressing gown, scarf, takkies, and a face pretending everything is fine.

rows.en: The geyser tripped overnight. Of course it did.

rows.en: Coffee in the sun on the stoep. The whole reason we live here.
rows.text: Ikhofi elangeni ku-stoep. Yiso sonke isizathu esenza sihlale la.
rows.back: Coffee in the sun on the stoep. That's the whole reason we live here.

rows.en: The sun has arrived. It has not yet started working.
rows.text: Ilanga selifikile. Aliqali ukusebenza.
rows.back: The sun has arrived. It isn't starting work.

rows.en: The prettiest lie you'll see all day.
rows.text: Amanga amahle kunawo wonke ozowabona usuku lonke.
rows.back: The prettiest lie you'll see all day.

rows.en: The lawn caught frost overnight. You're next.

rows.back: The grass caught frost overnight. You're next.

rows.en: Zero wind. Zero clouds. Zero mercy.

rows.back: No wind. No clouds. No mercy.

rows.en: Somebody left the freezer door open overnight.

rows.back: Someone left the freezer door open all night.

rows.en: Gorgeous, right? Do not trust it.
rows.text: Kuhle, akunjalo? Ungakuthembi.
rows.back: Beautiful, isn't it? Don't trust it.

rows.en: Looks like a tourism ad. Feels like the inside of a fridge.
rows.text: Kubukeka njenge-ad yezokuvakasha. Kuzwakala njengaphakathi kwefriji.
rows.back: Looks like a tourism ad. Feels like the inside of a fridge.

rows.en: That first breath of air will wake you better than coffee.

rows.back: That first breath of air will wake you better than coffee.

rows.en: Sunshine: 10/10. Feels-like: don't ask.

rows.back: Sunshine: 10/10. How it feels: don't ask.

rows.en: Snow on the mountains means socks in bed. That's the law.

rows.back: Snow on the mountains means socks in bed. That's the rule.

rows.en: Today's sky: freshly washed, ice-pressed.
rows.text: Izulu lanamuhla: lisanda kuwashwa, licindezelwe ngeqhwa.
rows.back: Today's sky: freshly washed, pressed with ice.

rows.en: Even the dog's breath is showing. That's the reading.

rows.back: Even the dog's breath is visible. That's the reading.
rows.note: unsure: 'okufundekayo' = 'what is readable/legible'; 'that's the reading' is a stretch
rows.reason: 'Yilokho okufundekayo' (that's what is readable) is awkward but carries 'That's the reading'.

rows.en: Frost on the fence, sun in your eyes, feeling in zero fingers.
rows.text: Isithwathwa ocingweni, ilanga emehlweni, awukho umuzwa eminweni.
rows.back: Frost on the fence, sun in your eyes, no feeling in your fingers.

rows.en: Clear skies, open roads, running nose. The full winter set.

rows.back: Clear sky, open roads, runny nose. The complete winter set.

rows.en: The sun is doing summer. The air didn't get the memo.
rows.text: Ilanga lenza ihlobo. Umoya awuyitholanga i-memo.
rows.back: The sun is doing summer. The wind didn't get the memo.

rows.en: Full sunshine, full jacket. Both are non-negotiable.

rows.back: Full sunshine, full coat. Both non-negotiable.

rows.en: It's a beautiful day to stay indoors.

rows.back: A beautiful day to stay indoors.

rows.en: The water is so clear you can basically see the cold.

rows.back: The most beautiful day of winter. Feels like the coldest one.

rows.back: Sunglasses and a scarf. That kind of day.

rows.back: Sunny, with a 100% chance of shivering.

rows.en: Orange flowers, blue sky, blue lips.

rows.back: Orange flowers, blue sky, blue lips.

rows.back: In the sun: bearable. Two steps to the left: Antarctica.

rows.back: Padstal coffee is working as central heating today.

rows.back: The Karoo doesn't lie about the weather. It brags about it.

rows.back: Picnic weather to your eyes. Soup weather to everything else.

rows.en: The sun is heading home now, taking the last three degrees with it.
rows.text: Ilanga liya ekhaya manje, lithathe ama-degree amathathu okugcina kanye nalo.
rows.back: The sun is going home now, taking the last three degrees with it.

rows.back: Look quickly. In ten minutes it'll be night and the North Pole.

rows.back: The fire isn't for atmosphere. The fire is for survival.

rows.text: Hlala eduze. Cha, eduze kakhulu. Yebo, cishe emlilweni.
rows.back: Sit close. No, closer. Yes, almost in the fire.

rows.text: Jabulela imibala. Izinga lokushisa selivele lahamba laya emotweni.
rows.back: Enjoy the colours. The temperature has already gone to the car.

rows.en: The brighter the stars, the harder your blanket has to work.
rows.text: Uma izinkanyezi zikhanya kakhulu, ingubo yakho kufanele isebenze kanzima kakhulu.
rows.back: The brighter the stars, the harder your blanket has to work.

rows.en: Free planetarium tonight. Admission: your toes.

rows.back: Free planetarium tonight. Entry fee: your toes.

rows.back: The universe is showing off tonight. Look quickly, freeze a little.

rows.text: Imizuzu emihlanu yokubuka izinkanyezi. Bese ubuyela ngaphakathi unomphelo.
rows.back: Five minutes of stargazing. Then back inside for good.

rows.text: Isithwathwa sesivele saqala i-shift yaso. Ngovivi utshani buzoba yingilazi.
rows.back: The frost has already started its shift. By dawn the grass will be glass.

rows.en: Rooibos in hand, blanket to the ears. Full kit.
rows.text: I-rooibos esandleni, ingubo kuze kube sezindlebeni. I-kit egcwele.
rows.back: Rooibos in hand, blanket up to the ears. The full kit.

rows.en: The city only looks this sharp when it genuinely hurts outside.
rows.text: Idolobha libukeka licace kangaka kuphela uma kubuhlungu ngempela ngaphandle.
rows.back: The town only looks this clear when it's truly painful outside.

rows.en: No wind, no clouds, no excuse for that thin jacket.
rows.text: Awukho umoya, awekho amafu, ayikho izaba yalelo jazi elincane.
rows.back: No wind, no clouds, no excuse for that thin little jacket.

rows.en: Breathing like a dragon, view like a dream.
rows.text: Uphefumula njengodrako, umbono onjengephupho.
rows.back: You breathe like a dragon, a view like a dream.

rows.en: Nobody's standing at the coals for the food. We're here for the heat.
rows.text: Akekho omile emalahleni ngenxa yokudla. Silapha ngenxa yokushisa.
rows.back: Nobody is standing at the coals for the food. We're here for the heat.

rows.text: Iqhwa ekukhanyeni kwenyanga: lihle entabeni, linonya emoyeni.
rows.back: Ice in the moonlight: beautiful on the mountain, cruel in the air.

rows.text: Uhlelo bekuyimizuzu eyishumi. Amakhala anikela ngemva kwemibili.
rows.back: The plan was ten minutes. The noses gave up after two.

rows.en: Clear nights are winter's way of apologising.

rows.back: A clear night is winter's way of apologising.

rows.en: The farm is still there. We're all just taking each other's word for it.
rows.text: Ipulazi lisekhona. Sonke sithembela nje ezwini lomunye nomunye.
rows.back: The farm is still there. We're all just taking each other's word for it.

rows.en: Your GPS says you have arrived. Your GPS is lying.
rows.text: I-GPS yakho ithi usufikile. I-GPS yakho iqamba amanga.
rows.back: Your GPS says you've arrived. Your GPS is lying.

rows.en: Snoek weather, say the uncles. The uncles have never once been wrong.
rows.text: Isimo sezulu se-snoek, kusho o-malume. O-malume abakaze benze iphutha nakanye.
rows.back: Snoek weather, say the uncles. The uncles have never once been wrong.

rows.en: The horizon took the day off.
rows.text: Umncele wezulu uthathe usuku lokuphumula.
rows.back: The horizon (lit. 'the edge of the sky') has taken a day off.
rows.note: unsure: 'umncele wezulu' is a descriptive phrase, 'boundary of the sky'; the usual word for horizon is 'umkhathizwe'
rows.reason: 'umncele wezulu' is a descriptive phrase for horizon

rows.en: The sea mist clocked in before everyone else.
rows.text: Inkungu yaselwandle ifike emsebenzini ngaphambi kwabo bonke.
rows.back: The sea fog got to work before everyone else.

rows.en: The cows know exactly where they are. Which is more than the rest of us can say.
rows.text: Izinkomo zazi kahle ukuthi zikuphi. Okungaphezu kwalokho thina esingakusho.
rows.back: The cows know exactly where they are. Which is more than we can say.

rows.en: Everything under the blanket is officially not today's problem.
rows.text: Konke okungaphansi kwengubo ngokusemthethweni akuyona inkinga yanamuhla.
rows.back: Everything under the blanket is officially not today's problem.
rows.note: 'okungaphansi kwengubo' = 'under the blanket'; the joke would make more sense as 'beyond the blanket'

rows.en: In the Karoo, fog is an event. The whole district will be talking about this tomorrow.
rows.text: EKaroo, inkungu ngumcimbi. Sonke isifunda sizokhuluma ngalokhu kusasa.
rows.back: In the Karoo, fog is an event. The whole region will be talking about it tomorrow.

rows.en: The silence put on a blanket this morning.
rows.text: Ukuthula kwembathe ingubo namuhla ekuseni.
rows.back: The silence has put on a blanket this morning.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'namuhla' means 'today' — nothing in the English source (time-of-day clash with 'morning'); the source's 'put' would normally be 'beka' / 'faka' / 'gaxa', none present — but it does co-occur in corpus with 'ekuseni'

rows.en: Even the plains are keeping secrets today.
rows.text: Ngisho namathafa agcina izimfihlo namuhla.
rows.back: Even the plains are keeping secrets today.

rows.en: The sea is down there. Probably.
rows.text: Ulwandle lungaphansi laphaya. Cishe.
rows.back: The sea is down there. Probably.

rows.en: Chappies is asking for faith this morning, not just a licence.
rows.text: I-Chappies icela ukholo namuhla ekuseni, hhayi nje ilayisensi.
rows.back: Chappies asks for faith this morning, not just a licence.
rows.note: 'I-Chappies' read as Chapman's Peak Drive, since the licence points to driving

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'namuhla' means 'today' — nothing in the English source (time-of-day clash with 'morning') (source: chappies, licence) — but it does co-occur in corpus with 'ekuseni'

rows.en: Drive like your mother is watching.
rows.text: Shayela sengathi umama wakho uyabuka.
rows.back: Drive like your mom is watching.

rows.en: The neighbourhood is gone. Coffee first, then we'll check again.
rows.text: Umphakathi usunyamalele. Ikhofi kuqala, bese siphinda sibheke.
rows.back: The neighbourhood has disappeared. Coffee first, then we look again.
rows.note: 'umphakathi' = community (the people), not really the physical suburb
rows.reason: 'umphakathi' leans 'community' rather than 'neighbourhood'; still reads

rows.en: You can hear the hadedas but you can't see them. Ominous? No. Just Tuesday.
rows.text: Ungawezwa ama-hadeda kodwa awuwaboni. Kuyethusa? Cha. NgoLwesibili nje.
rows.back: You can hear the hadedas but you can't see them. Scary? No. Just Tuesday.

rows.en: Visibility: zero. Mood: surprisingly at peace with it.
rows.text: Ukubona: okungelutho. I-mood: ngokumangalisayo unokuthula ngakho.
rows.back: Visibility: nothing. Mood: surprisingly, you're at peace with it.
rows.note: doubtful morphology: 'unokuthula' takes a 2nd-person/class-1 concord, but I-mood (class 9) would need 'inokuthula'; so it reads as 'you are calm'
rows.reason: meaning holds; 'unokuthula' concord for I-mood is doubtful ('inokuthula' expected)

rows.en: There's a view here somewhere. The brochure promised.
rows.text: Kukhona umbono lapha ndawana. Incwadana yethembisile.
rows.back: There's a view here somewhere. The brochure promised.
rows.note: unsure: 'ndawana' is colloquial; could be 'somewhere' or 'a little spot'

rows.en: This morning's rush hour: one canoe.
rows.text: I-rush hour yanamuhla ekuseni: isikebhe esisodwa.
rows.back: This morning's rush hour: one boat.
rows.reason: 'isikebhe' (boat) for 'canoe' is an equivalent image

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'yanamuhla' means 'today' — nothing in the English source (time-of-day clash with 'morning's'); the source's 'hour' would normally be 'ihawa' / 'ihora' / 'amahora', none present

rows.en: Visibility: poor. Vibes: untouchable.
rows.text: Ukubona: kubi. Ama-vibes: awathinteki.
rows.back: Visibility: bad. Vibes: untouched.

rows.en: The fog is borrowing the colours. It'll return them in the morning.
rows.text: Inkungu iboleka imibala. Izoyibuyisa ekuseni.
rows.back: The fog is borrowing the colours. It'll bring them back in the morning.

rows.en: The fog says stay. Who are we to argue?
rows.text: Inkungu ithi hlala. Singobani thina ukuze siphikise?
rows.back: The fog says stay. Who are we to argue?

rows.en: Nobody is driving home in this. That's not laziness, that's science.
rows.text: Akekho oshayela eya ekhaya kulokhu. Akulona ubuvila, kuyisayensi.
rows.back: Nobody's driving home in this. It's not laziness, it's science.

rows.en: Fireplace weather showed up without even asking.
rows.text: Isimo sezulu somlilo sivele safika singaze sabuza.
rows.back: Fire weather just showed up without even asking.
rows.note: unsure: 'isimo sezulu somlilo' could mean fireplace weather or fire-danger weather
rows.reason: 'Isimo sezulu somlilo' = 'fire weather', which loses 'fireplace' and can read as fire-danger weather
reasons: DRIFT: 'Isimo sezulu somlilo' = 'fire weather', which loses 'fireplace' and can read as fire-danger weather

rows.en: The whole town just switched itself to whisper volume.
rows.text: Lonke idolobha lisanda kuzishintshela ku-volume yokuhleba.
rows.back: The whole town just switched itself to whisper volume.

rows.en: Every streetlamp thinks it's the moon tonight.
rows.text: Sonke isibani somgwaqo sicabanga ukuthi siyinyanga namuhla ebusuku.
rows.back: Every streetlight thinks it's the moon tonight.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'namuhla' means 'today' — nothing in the English source (time-of-day clash with 'tonight') (source: ) — but it does co-occur in corpus with 'ebusuku'

rows.en: The whole street smells like someone else's dinner and the fog won't say whose.
rows.text: Wonke umgwaqo unuka njengesidlo sakusihlwa somunye umuntu futhi inkungu ayifuni ukusho ukuthi ngesikabani.
rows.back: Every street smells like somebody else's supper and the fog won't say whose.

rows.en: Let's call it atmosphere and go inside.
rows.text: Asiyibize nge-atmosphere bese singena ngaphakathi.
rows.back: Let's call it atmosphere and go inside.

rows.en: Highveld fog: rare enough that everyone's photographing it.
rows.text: Inkungu ye-Highveld: iyivelakancane kangangokuthi wonke umuntu uyayithwebula.
rows.back: Highveld fog: so rare that everyone photographs it.

rows.en: Ice swimmers don't check the weather. The weather checks them.
rows.text: Abadadi beqhwa abasibheki isimo sezulu. Isimo sezulu siyababheka.
rows.back: Ice swimmers don't check the weather. The weather checks them.
rows.note: unsure: 'abadadi' comes from -dada 'swim/float', a rare noun that leans isiXhosa (Zulu usually uses -bhukuda); 'beqhwa' = of ice/frost
rows.reason: 'abadadi beqhwa' = ice swimmers; rare noun, Xhosa-leaning -dada, worth a native glance

rows.en: Visibility is for people who turn back.
rows.text: Ukubona kungokwabantu abaphindela emuva.
rows.back: Visibility is for people who turn back.
rows.note: meaning unclear: 'abaphindela emuva' = those who go back/return, perhaps 'quitters'

rows.en: The sea has vanished but the tannies are here. Priorities.
rows.text: Ulwandle lunyamalele kodwa o-anti balapha. Okubaluleke kakhulu.
rows.back: The sea has disappeared but the aunties are here. Priorities.
rows.note: 'Okubaluleke kakhulu' is literally 'the most important thing'

rows.en: You can't see the house. You believe the house.
rows.text: Awukwazi ukubona indlu. Uyayikholwa indlu.
rows.back: You can't see the house. You believe in the house.

rows.en: The mountains went to bed early tonight.
rows.text: Izintaba ziye zolala kusenesikhathi namuhla ebusuku.
rows.back: The mountains went to bed early tonight.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'namuhla' means 'today' — nothing in the English source (time-of-day clash with 'tonight'); the source's 'bed' would normally be 'umbhede' / 'imibhede', none present — but it does co-occur in corpus with 'ebusuku'

rows.en: Last one through closes the gate. Even if nobody can see it.
rows.text: Owokugcina ukudlula uvala isango. Noma ngabe akekho olibonayo.
rows.back: Last one through closes the gate. Even if nobody can see it.

rows.en: The Heads are closed. The evening is open.
rows.text: I-Heads ivaliwe. Kusihlwa kuvuliwe.
rows.back: The Heads are closed. The evening is open.

rows.en: Somewhere a dog is barking and everyone's pretending they know where.
rows.text: Ndawana inja iyakhonkotha futhi wonke umuntu wenza sengathi uyazi ukuthi kuphi.
rows.back: Somewhere a dog is barking and everyone is pretending they know where.

rows.en: The fog came early to gift-wrap the evening.
rows.text: Inkungu ifike kusenesikhathi ukuzogoqa kusihlwa njengesipho.
rows.back: The fog came early to wrap the evening like a present.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'ukuzogoqa' — not found in any external source; closest attested: 'ukuzoqoqa' (1× leipzig, distance 1)

rows.en: The city pulled up its duvet. Leave it alone.
rows.text: Idolobha lidonse i-duvet yalo. Liyeke.
rows.back: The town has pulled up its duvet. Leave it be.

rows.en: From up here everyone's problems look out of focus. Works for me.
rows.text: Ukusuka lapha phezulu izinkinga zabo bonke zibukeka zingacaci. Kuyangisebenzela.
rows.back: From up here everyone's problems look blurry. Works for me.

rows.en: Somewhere the foghorn moans and a thousand people say 'ag nee' at exactly the same time.
rows.text: Ndawana i-foghorn iyabhonga futhi abantu abayinkulungwane bathi 'ag nee' ngasikhathi sinye ncamashi.
rows.back: Somewhere a foghorn bellows and a thousand people say 'ag nee' at exactly the same time.

rows.en: Seventeenth floor, zero view, one hundred percent snug.
rows.text: Isitezi seshumi nesikhombisa, awukho umbono, i-snug ngekhulu lephesenti.
rows.back: Seventeenth floor, no view, a hundred percent snug.

rows.en: Night fog in the vineyards: spa night for the grapes.
rows.text: Inkungu yasebusuku ensimini yamagilebhisi: ubusuku be-spa bamagilebhisi.
rows.back: Night fog in the vineyard: spa night for the grapes.

rows.en: Everything you can hear tonight is one owl with strong opinions.
rows.text: Konke ongakuzwa namuhla ebusuku yisikhova esisodwa esinemibono eqinile.
rows.back: All you can hear tonight is one owl with strong opinions.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'namuhla' means 'today' — nothing in the English source (time-of-day clash with 'tonight') (source: everything, opinions) — but it does co-occur in corpus with 'ebusuku'

rows.en: The gable has seen worse in three hundred years. Sleep easy.
rows.text: I-gable ibone okubi kakhulu eminyakeni engamakhulu amathathu. Lala kahle.
rows.back: The gable has seen far worse in three hundred years. Sleep well.

rows.en: The dog doesn't understand where the world went. Same, boy. Same.
rows.text: Inja ayiqondi ukuthi umhlaba uye kuphi. Nathi, mfana. Nathi.
rows.back: The dog doesn't get where the world went. Us neither, boy. Us neither.

rows.en: Ten pm fog turns every street into a film set.
rows.text: Inkungu yango-10 ebusuku iphendula wonke umgwaqo ube i-film set.
rows.back: 10pm fog turns every street into a film set.

rows.en: Joburg does fog so rarely it feels like a limited edition.
rows.text: IJoburg yenza inkungu ngokuyivelakancane kangangokuthi kuzwakala njenge-limited edition.
rows.back: Joburg does fog so rarely it feels like a limited edition.

rows.en: Slap chips taste better when the world ends at the harbour wall.
rows.text: Ama-slap chips anambitheka kangcono uma umhlaba uphela odongeni lwechweba.
rows.back: Slap chips taste better when the world ends at the harbour wall.

rows.en: The sea is still out there. You can smell it, but it can't see you.
rows.text: Ulwandle lusekhona laphaya. Ungaluhogela, kodwa alukwazi ukukubona.
rows.back: The sea is still out there. You can smell it, but it can't see you.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'Ungaluhogela' — not found in any external source; closest attested: 'ungahogela' (1× leipzig, distance 2)

rows.en: Four friends, one parcel of chips, zero visibility. Perfect evening.
rows.text: Abangane abane, iphakethe elilodwa lama-chips, awukho ukubona. Kusihlwa okuphelele.
rows.back: Four friends, one packet of chips, zero visibility. The perfect evening.
rows.reason: meaning holds; 'awukho ukubona' concord slip ('akukho' expected)

rows.en: The stars took a night off. Even them.
rows.text: Izinkanyezi zithathe ubusuku bokuphumula. Ngisho nazo.
rows.back: The stars have taken the night off. Even them.

rows.en: Karoo night fog: rare enough that it'll get mentioned in church on Sunday.
rows.text: Inkungu yasebusuku yaseKaroo: iyivelakancane kangangokuthi izophathwa esontweni ngeSonto.
rows.back: Karoo night fog: so rare it'll be mentioned in church on Sunday.

rows.en: The nearest neighbours are thirty kilometres away and tonight they can see you even less.
rows.text: Omakhelwane abaseduze bangamakhilomitha angamashumi amathathu kude futhi namuhla ebusuku bakubona kancane nakakhulu.
rows.back: The nearest neighbours are thirty kilometres away, and tonight they can see you even less.
rows.note: 'bakubona' = 'they see you' (the neighbours are the subject)

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'namuhla' means 'today' — nothing in the English source (time-of-day clash with 'tonight') (source: nearest, neighbours, thirty) — but it does co-occur in corpus with 'ebusuku'

rows.en: Deep in the forest, deep under a blanket — exact same energy.
rows.text: Phakathi ehlathini, phakathi ngaphansi kwengubo — amandla afanayo ncamashi.
rows.back: Deep in the forest, deep under the blanket: exactly the same energy.

rows.en: No streaming service has a genre for this.
rows.text: Ayikho i-streaming service ene-genre yalokhu.
rows.back: No streaming service has a genre for this.

rows.en: Tonight the forest is telling its stories in a whisper.
rows.text: Namuhla ebusuku ihlathi lixoxa izindaba zalo ngokuhleba.
rows.back: Tonight the forest is telling its stories in a whisper.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'Namuhla' means 'today' — nothing in the English source (time-of-day clash with 'tonight'); the source's 'telling' would normally be 'ukuxoxa' / 'ukulanda' / 'ukutshela', none present — but it does co-occur in corpus with 'ebusuku'

rows.en: Can't see a thing. Not a thing.
rows.text: Andiboni nto. Nento encinci.
rows.back: I can't see anything. Not even a tiny thing.

rows.en: Driving slow is not a suggestion.
rows.text: Ukuqhuba kancinci akusosiphakamiso.
rows.back: Driving slowly isn't a suggestion.

MEDIUM semantic: 'Ukuqhuba' means 'continuation; progress; steer' — nothing in the English source; the source's 'driving' would normally be 'indlela', none present

rows.en: Silent Hill vibes. Without the monsters. Hopefully.
rows.text: I-Silent Hill vibes. Ngaphandle kwezidalwa. Sinethemba.
rows.back: Silent Hill vibes. Minus the monsters. We hope.

rows.en: Visibility: basically zero.
rows.text: Ukubonakala: phantse kungabikho.
rows.back: Visibility: almost none.

rows.en: Even your GPS is confused.
rows.text: Ne-GPS yakho iyadideka.
rows.back: Even your GPS is confused.

rows.en: The world just... disappeared.
rows.text: Ihlabathi nje... lanyamalala.
rows.back: The world just... vanished.

rows.en: Perfect weather for a horror movie.
rows.text: Yimozulu efanele ifilimu eyoyikisayo
rows.back: It's weather made for a horror film.

rows.en: Ghost town. But it's just Tuesday.

rows.back: It's like a ghost town. And it's just Tuesday.

rows.en: If you can read this, you're too close.
rows.text: Ukuba uyakwazi ukufunda oku, ukufutshane kakhulu.
rows.back: If you can read this, you're very close.

rows.en: Table Mountain? What Table Mountain?
rows.text: I-Table Mountain? Yiyiphi i-Table Mountain?
rows.back: Table Mountain? Which Table Mountain?

rows.en: The fog ate the neighbourhood.
rows.text: Inkungu itye indawo.
rows.back: The fog has eaten the place.

rows.en: Your car is out there. Somewhere. Probably.
rows.text: Imoto yakho ikhona ngaphandle. Ndaweni ithile. Mhlawumbi.
rows.back: Your car is outside. Somewhere. Probably.

rows.en: The world got a soft filter this morning.
rows.text: Ihlabathi lifumene ifilitha ethambileyo ngale ntsasa.
rows.back: The world got a soft filter this morning.

rows.en: Walking the dog has become a trust exercise.
rows.text: Ukuhambisa inja kusanda kuba ngumdlalo wokuthemba.
rows.back: Walking the dog just became a game of faith.

rows.en: The streetlights are trying their best.
rows.text: Izibane zesitalato zizama ngako konke ezinako.
rows.back: The streetlights are trying their very best.

rows.en: Somewhere out there is the road. We think.

rows.back: Somewhere out there, there's a road. Probably.

rows.en: Everything looks like a film scene. A creepy one.
rows.text: Yonke into ibonakala njengomfanekiso wefilimu. Oyoyikisayo.
rows.back: Everything looks like a still from a film. A scary one.

rows.en: Your high beams are making it worse, boet.

rows.en: Save this one in the memory bank.
rows.text: Boloka letsatsi lena mohopolong.
rows.back: Keep this day in your memory.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'Boloka' means 'bless; invest; invested' — nothing in the English source; it is 3 letters from 'banka', the usual word for 'bank'

rows.en: The kind of day you text someone about.
rows.text: Mofuta oa letsatsi oo o romelang motho molaetsa ka lona.
rows.back: The kind of day you send someone a message about.

rows.en: Africa's sky just hits different.
rows.text: Lehodimo la Afrika le fapane feela.
rows.back: The African sky is just different.

rows.en: Take a moment. Look up. You're welcome.
rows.text: Nka motsotso. Sheba hodimo. Kea leboha.
rows.back: Take a moment. Look up. Thank you.
rows.reason: Punchline flipped: 'Kea leboha' = 'thank you', not the cheeky 'You're welcome' (same error as st-0723).
reasons: DRIFT: Punchline flipped: 'Kea leboha' = 'thank you', not the cheeky 'You're welcome' (same error as st-0723).

rows.en: The Helderberg is showing off today.
rows.text: Helderberg e iponahatsa kajeno.
rows.back: The Helderberg is showing off today.

rows.en: Days like this should come with a soundtrack.
rows.text: Matsatsi a tjena a lokela ho tla le soundtrack.
rows.back: Days like this should come with a soundtrack.

rows.en: Your vitamin D levels are thanking you.
rows.text: Maemo a hao a vitamin D a a leboha.
rows.back: Your vitamin D levels thank you.

rows.en: The fynbos is loving it. You should too.
rows.text: Fynbos e e rata. Le uena o lokela.
rows.back: The fynbos loves it. You should too.

rows.en: Blue sky, warm breeze. The simple stuff.
rows.text: Lehodimo le letala, moya o futhumetseng. Dintho tse bonolo.
rows.back: Blue sky, warm air. Simple things.

rows.en: The sky's giving everything today.
rows.text: Lehodimo le fana le tsohle kajeno.
rows.back: The sky is giving it everything today.
rows.note: grammar: 'fana le tsohle' - expected 'fana ka tsohle'

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'fana' means 'furnish; render; supplied' — nothing in the English source; it is 1 letter from 'fang', the usual word for 'giving'

rows.en: This is the weather you'll miss in December traffic.
rows.text: Lena ke lehodimo leo o tla le thella sephetphetheng sa Tšitoe.
rows.back: This is the sky you'll slide on in December traffic.
rows.note: unsure: 'thella' = slip/slide, sense unclear; 'sephetphetheng' misspelt (sephethephetheng); 'Tšitoe' Lesotho spelling (SA Tshitwe)
rows.reason: 'o tla le thella' = 'you'll slide/slip on it', not 'you'll miss'; the December-traffic joke is lost ('sephetphetheng' also misspelt).

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'sephetphetheng' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source; closest attested: 'sephethephetheng' (0× dictionary, distance 2)

reasons: MISMATCH: 'o tla le thella' = 'you'll slide/slip on it', not 'you'll miss'; the December-traffic joke is lost ('sephetphetheng' also misspelt).

rows.en: Even the parking lot looks pretty today.
rows.text: Esita le sebaka sa liphakinki se bonahala se setle kajeno.
rows.back: Even the parking lot looks pretty today.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'liphakinki' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source
MEDIUM semantic: 'sebaka' means 'area; distance; scene' — nothing in the English source; it is 3 letters from 'sheba', the usual word for 'looks'

rows.en: No filter needed. Just look outside.
rows.text: Ha ho hlokahale filitha. Sheba kantle feela.
rows.back: No filter needed. Just look outside.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'filitha' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source
MEDIUM semantic: 'Sheba' means 'to look for; look; look (v.)' — nothing in the English source; it is 2 letters from 'sefa', the usual word for 'filter'

rows.en: The type of day that makes people text 'lekker dag hey'.
rows.text: Mofuta oa letsatsi o etsang batho ba romele 'letsatsi le letle hey'.
rows.back: The kind of day that makes people send 'nice day hey'.

rows.en: Take your coffee outside. You deserve it.
rows.text: Nka kofi ea hao o ee kantle. O e tšoanetse.
rows.back: Take your coffee outside. You deserve it.

rows.en: Everything looks 4K today. The sky's in ultra mode.
rows.text: Tsohle li shebahala 4K kajeno. Lehodimo le ultra mode.
rows.back: Everything looks 4K today. The sky is in ultra mode.

rows.en: This is the day the brochure was talking about.
rows.text: Lena ke letsatsi leo brosure e neng e bua ka lona.
rows.back: This is the day the brochure was talking about.

rows.en: Your excuse to stay inside just expired.
rows.text: Lebaka la hao la ho dula ka hare le sa tswa fela.
rows.back: Your reason for staying inside just ran out.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'fela' is a tn function-word marker (tn 2556× vs st 232×)

rows.en: This is the stuff. Right here.
rows.text: Ke sona sena. Mona feela.
rows.back: This is it. Right here.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'sona' means 'it (absolute pronoun); possessive pronoun' — nothing in the English source; it is 1 letter from 'tona', the usual word for 'right'

rows.en: A proper good one. Don't waste it.
rows.text: Le letle ka 'nete. Se ke oa le senya.
rows.back: It's truly beautiful. Don't spoil it.

rows.en: The kind of sky that makes you grateful for free things.
rows.text: Mofuta oa lehodimo o etsang hore o leboge dintho tsa mahala.
rows.back: The kind of sky that makes you grateful for free things.

findings: HIGH contamination: 'leboge' is attested in nso (6× leipzig/nchlt) but in no external st source (only in this app's own copy)

rows.en: Pour the coffee outside. Trust us.
rows.text: Tšolla kofi kantle. Re tšepe.
rows.back: Pour the coffee outside. Trust us.
rows.note: 'Tšolla kofi kantle' can read as pouring the coffee out (throwing it away)

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'Tšolla' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source; closest attested: 'tsoela' (64× leipzig/wiki, distance 1)

rows.en: Africa showing off again. Quietly devastating.
rows.text: Afrika e iponahatsa hape. Ka kgotso ka ho qhibilihisang.
rows.back: Africa is showing off again. Peacefully, in a melting way.
rows.note: unsure: 'ka ho qhibilihisang' = meltingly - odd image
rows.reason: 'Quietly devastating' becomes 'ka kgotso ka ho qhibilihisang' ('peacefully, meltingly') - awkward, the punch is gone.

findings: MEDIUM lexical: 'qhibilihisang' — seen only in this app's own copy, in no external source; closest attested: 'qhibidihisang' (1× leipzig, distance 1)
MEDIUM semantic: 'kgotso' means 'peace; also used as form of greeting' — nothing in the English source; it is 2 letters from 'kgutsa', the usual word for 'quietly'

reasons: DRIFT: 'Quietly devastating' becomes 'ka kgotso ka ho qhibilihisang' ('peacefully, meltingly') - awkward, the punch is gone.

rows.en: This is the weather we brag about overseas.
rows.text: Lena ke lehodimo leo re le iponelang ditjhaba.
rows.back: This is the sky we see for ourselves [before] the nations.
rows.note: unsure: 'iponela' = see for oneself, not 'show off to'; line unclear
rows.reason: 're le iponelang ditjhaba' = 'we see for ourselves ... nations'; 'brag about overseas' is not said (ipontsha would be show off).
reasons: DRIFT: 're le iponelang ditjhaba' = 'we see for ourselves ... nations'; 'brag about overseas' is not said (ipontsha would be show off).

rows.en: Feels like the country is on its best behaviour.
rows.text: Ho utlwahala eka naha e maemong a eona a matle.
rows.back: It feels like the country is at its best.

rows.en: Bottle this one. Open it in winter.
rows.text: Beha lena ka botlolong. Bula nakong ea mariha.
rows.back: Put this in a bottle. Open in winter.

rows.en: The sun clocked in before your alarm even tried.
rows.text: Letsatsi le clock-ile pele alarm ea hao e leka.
rows.back: The sun clocked in before your alarm even tried.

rows.en: Air this clear should come with a warning: plans will be made.
rows.text: Moya o hlakileng hakana o lokela ho tla le temoso: merero e tla etswa.
rows.back: Air this clear should come with a warning: plans will be made.

rows.en: This is leave-form weather and HR knows it.
rows.text: Bona ke boemo ba foromo ea phomolo 'me HR e a tseba.
rows.back: This is leave-form weather and HR knows it.

rows.en: 'Quick dip before work.' Nobody in history has been quick.
rows.text: 'Ho ina kapele pele ho mosebetsi.' Ha ho motho historing ea kileng a potlaka.
rows.back: 'A quick dip before work.' Nobody in history has ever hurried.

rows.en: Zero mistakes from today so far. Sky included.
rows.text: Ha ho diphoso ho tloha kajeno ho fihlela jwale. Ho kenyeletswa lehodimo.
rows.back: No faults from today until now. The sky included.
rows.note: 'ho tloha kajeno ho fihlela jwale' = 'from today until now' - awkward

rows.en: Highveld mornings: freezing, gorgeous, zero apologies.
rows.text: Meso ea Highveld: e hatselang, e metle, ha ho boitšoarelo.
rows.back: Highveld mornings: freezing, beautiful, no apologies.

rows.en: Inbox: 47. Sky: flawless. Priorities: sorted.
rows.text: Inbox: 47. Lehodimo: le hlwekile. Dintho tsa bohlokwa: di lokisitswe.
rows.back: Inbox: 47. Sky: clean. Priorities: sorted.

rows.en: Weather this well-behaved is definitely up to something.
rows.text: Boemo ba lehodimo bo itšoereng hantle hakana ehlile bo rera ho hong.
rows.back: Weather behaving this well is definitely planning something.

rows.en: Mornings like this are why Capetonians never stop mentioning it.
rows.text: Meso e jwalo ke lona lebaka leo batho ba Cape Town ba sa kgaotseng ho bua ka lona.
rows.back: Mornings like this are exactly why Cape Town people never stop talking about it.

rows.en: The sun took its time this morning. Worth the wait.
rows.text: Letsatsi le nkile nako ea lona hoseng bona. Ho loketse ho emela.
rows.back: The sun took its time this morning. Worth waiting for.

rows.en: Signal: weak. Views: unfair. Deadlines: whose?
rows.text: Signal: e fokolang. Dipono: ha di lokang. Di-deadline: tsa mang?
rows.back: Signal: weak. Views: not okay. Deadlines: whose?
rows.note: unsure: 'ha di lokang' reads as 'not right/not okay' - grammar doubtful
rows.reason: 'Dipono: ha di lokang' reads 'views: not okay/not right' - the literal 'unfair' loses the 'unfairly good' compliment.
reasons: DRIFT: 'Dipono: ha di lokang' reads 'views: not okay/not right' - the literal 'unfair' loses the 'unfairly good' compliment.

rows.en: One of those days the group chat will hear about for years.
rows.text: E 'ngoe ea matsatsi ao group chat e tla utlwa ka oona ka dilemo.
rows.back: One of those days the group chat will hear about for years.

rows.en: Enjoy it. There's a cold front out there doing warm-ups.
rows.text: E natefelwe. Ho na le cold front kantle e etsang di-warm-up.
rows.back: Enjoy it. There's a cold front outside doing warm-ups.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'cold' is core English weather vocabulary left untranslated

rows.en: One perfect day issued. Non-transferable. Spend it wisely.
rows.text: Letsatsi le le leng le phethahetseng le fanwe. Ha le fetisetswe. Le sebedise ka bohlale.
rows.back: One perfect day has been given. It is not transferable. Use it wisely.

rows.en: The sun woke up and chose glorious.
rows.text: Letsatsi le tsohile la kgetha kganya.
rows.back: The sun woke up and chose brightness.

rows.en: Small-town quiet: you can actually hear yourself think. Terrifying.
rows.text: Kgutso ya toropo e nyane: o ka utlwa mohopolo wa hao. Hwa tshosa.
rows.back: Small-town quiet: you can hear your own thoughts. It's scary.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'nyane' means 'little; small; least' — nothing in the English source; it is 3 letters from 'nahana', the usual word for 'think'

rows.en: Out here even the sun refuses to rush.
rows.text: Mona kantle esita le letsatsi le hana ho potlaka.
rows.back: Out here even the sun refuses to hurry.

rows.en: Even Monday looks photogenic in this light.
rows.text: Esita le Mantaha o shebahala hantle leseding lena.
rows.back: Even Monday looks good in this light.

rows.en: 'One hour at the beach.' History's most confident lie.
rows.text: 'Hora e le 'ngoe lebopong.' Leshano le nang le boitshepo ka ho fetisisa historing.
rows.back: 'One hour at the beach.' The most confident lie in history.

rows.en: Atlantic rule: the water is freezing and everyone lies about it.
rows.text: Molao oa Atlantic: metsi a hatsela 'me bohle ba bua leshano ka hona.
rows.back: Atlantic rule: the water is freezing and everyone lies about it.

rows.en: Weather this perfect is on loan. The southeaster keeps receipts.
rows.text: Boemo ba lehodimo bo phethahetseng hakana ke kadimo. Moya oa borwa o boloka li-receipt.
rows.back: Weather this perfect is a loan. The south wind keeps the receipts.
rows.note: 'moya oa borwa' = south wind (not specifically the south-easter); Lesotho 'li-receipt'

rows.en: Tidal pool water: instant regret, then instant youth.
rows.text: Metsi a tidal pool: maswabi hang-hang, ebe botjha hang-hang.
rows.back: Tidal-pool water: instant regret, then instantly reborn.

rows.en: All meetings moved to the shallow end.
rows.text: Dikopano tsohle di fallisetswe karolong e sa tebang.
rows.back: All meetings have been moved to the shallow end.

rows.en: Highveld winter flex: laundry dry before the kettle's even done.
rows.text: Flex ya mariha ya Highveld: diaparo di omile pele ketlele e qeta.
rows.back: Highveld winter flex: the washing is dry before the kettle finishes.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'omile' is attested in zu (36× kaikki/leipzig/wiki/dictionary) but in no external st source

rows.en: Clear sky, clear diary. One of those is a lie.
rows.text: Lehodimo le hlakileng, diary e hlakileng. E 'ngoe ea tseo ke leshano.
rows.back: Clear sky, clear diary. One of those is a lie.

rows.en: The weather made the plans. We just RSVP'd.
rows.text: Boemo ba lehodimo bo entse merero. Rona re mane ra RSVP feela.
rows.back: The weather made the plans. We just RSVP'd.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'RSVP' is an English word with no st attestation and is not in the English source line

rows.en: You don't waste a sky like this on being sensible.
rows.text: Ha o senye lehodimo le tjena ka ho ba le kelello.
rows.back: You don't waste a sky like this by being sensible.

rows.en: Padkos hits different under infinite sky. That's just science.
rows.text: Padkos e latsweha ka tsela e fapaneng tlas'a lehodimo le sa feleng. Ke saense feela.
rows.back: Padkos tastes different under an endless sky. It's just science.

rows.en: The mountain skipped the tablecloth today. Full outfit reveal.
rows.text: Thaba e tlodisitse lesela kajeno. Ho iponahatsa seaparo sohle.
rows.back: The mountain has flicked off its cloth today. Showing off the whole outfit.

rows.en: Days like this aren't earned. They're issued.
rows.text: Matsatsi a tjena ha a fumanwe ka ho sebetsa. A a fanwa feela.
rows.back: Days like this aren't earned by working. They're simply given.

rows.en: Cancel everything. This is THE day winter was hiding.
rows.text: Hlakola tsohle. Lena ke LONA letsatsi leo mariha a neng a le patile.
rows.back: Cancel everything. This is THE day winter was hiding.

rows.en: Off-season beach: same ocean, zero fight for parking.
rows.text: Lebopo ka ntle ho sehla: lewatle le tšoanang, ha ho ntwa ea parking.
rows.back: The beach out of season: same sea, no parking war.

rows.en: 'Just one sundowner' — famous last words, every single time.
rows.text: 'Sundowner e le 'ngoe feela' — mantswe a ho qetela a tummeng, nako e 'ngoe le e 'ngoe.
rows.back: 'Just one sundowner' - famous last words, every time.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'tummeng' means 'renowned' — nothing in the English source; it is 2 letters from 'tumileng', the usual word for 'famous'

rows.en: The sun is really milking this exit. Honestly, deserved.
rows.text: Letsatsi le hlile le nka nako ho tswa. Ka nnete, le se tšoanetse.
rows.back: The sun is really taking its time to come out. Honestly, it deserves it.
rows.note: 'ho tswa' = come out/leave - rising or setting unclear; 'le se tšoanetse' concord doubtful
rows.reason: 'ho tswa' most naturally reads 'come out' (sun appearing), so 'milking this exit' (lingering sunset) becomes ambiguous.
reasons: DRIFT: 'ho tswa' most naturally reads 'come out' (sun appearing), so 'milking this exit' (lingering sunset) becomes ambiguous.

rows.en: Nobody's leaving early under a sky like this.
rows.text: Ha ho ea tsamayang pele tlas'a lehodimo le tjena.
rows.back: Nobody leaves early under a sky like this.

rows.en: When the weather behaves this well, so do we. Roughly.
rows.text: Ha boemo ba lehodimo bo itšoara hantle hakana, le rona rea itšoara. Hoo e ka bang.
rows.back: When the weather behaves this well, we behave too. More or less.

rows.en: A day so good even rush hour felt optional.
rows.text: Letsatsi le letle hoo esita le sephethephethe se neng se utlwahala e le boikgethelo.
rows.back: A day so beautiful that even the traffic felt optional.

rows.en: Highveld golden hour: costs nothing, upstages everything.
rows.text: Golden hour ea Highveld: ha e lefise letho, e feta tsohle.
rows.back: Highveld golden hour: costs nothing, beats everything.

rows.en: Golden hour runs daily. Attendance still somehow optional.
rows.text: Golden hour e etsahala letsatsi le leng le le leng. Ho ba teng ho sa ntse ho le boikgethelo.
rows.back: Golden hour happens every single day. Being there is still optional.

rows.en: The evening showed up in its Sunday best.
rows.text: Mantsiboya a fihlile a apere seaparo sa oona se setle sa Sontaha.
rows.back: The evening has arrived wearing its Sunday best.

rows.en: Verandah weather. The couch will understand.
rows.text: Boemo ba stoep. Sofa e tla utloisisa.
rows.back: Stoep weather. The sofa will understand.

findings: MEDIUM contamination: 'Sofa' is an English word with no st attestation and is not in the English source line

rows.en: Best seat in the house isn't in the house.
rows.text: Setulo se setle ka ho fetisisa ka tlung ha se ka hare ho ntlo.
rows.back: The best seat in the house isn't inside the house.

rows.en: Last swim of the day always feels like a secret.
rows.text: Ho sesa ha ho qetela ha letsatsi ho dula ho utlwahala jwalo ka sephiri.
rows.back: The last swim of the day always feels like a secret.

rows.en: Suspiciously calm out there. We'll allow it.
rows.text: Ho kgutsitse ka mokgwa o belaetsang kantle. Re tla e dumella.
rows.back: It's suspiciously quiet outside. We'll allow it.

rows.en: House rules: last over when the streetlights win.
rows.text: Melao ea ntlo: over ea ho qetela ha mabone a seterata a hlōla.
rows.back: House rules: last over when the streetlights win.
rows.note: 'hlōla' = win/overcome - 'when the streetlights win' rather than 'come on'

rows.en: Small town, giant sky, zero rush.
rows.text: Toropo e nyane, lehodimo le leholo, ha ho potlako.
rows.back: Small town, big sky, no rush.

rows.en: Every so often Cape Town explains itself. No notes.
rows.text: Ka nako le nako Cape Town e itlhalosa. Ha ho dintlha.
rows.back: Every now and then Cape Town explains itself. No notes.

rows.en: Dinner tastes better when the walk there looks like this.
rows.text: Dijo tsa mantsiboya di latsweha hamonate ha tsela e leng teng e shebahala tjena.
rows.back: Supper tastes better when the road there looks like this.
rows.note: unsure: 'ha tsela e leng teng' - 'the road that is there', vague

rows.en: Someone turned the stars up to full volume.
rows.text: Motho o phahamiselitse dinaledi ho volume e tletseng.
rows.back: Someone turned the stars up to full volume.

rows.en: Coals fading, stories only warming up.
rows.text: Mashala a a tima, dipale di sa qala ho futhumala.
rows.back: The coals are dying, the stories are only starting to warm up.

rows.en: City folk pay good money for this ceiling.
rows.text: Batho ba toropong ba lefa tjhelete e ngata bakeng sa siling ena.
rows.back: City people pay a lot of money for this ceiling.

findings: MEDIUM semantic: 'Batho' means 'people; human beings; humans' — nothing in the English source; it is 2 letters from 'batle', the usual word for 'good'

rows.en: Sky this clear means tomorrow's a scorcher. Stay a while.
rows.text: Lehodimo le hlakileng hakana le bolela hore hosane ho tla tjhesa. Dula nakwana.
rows.back: A sky this clear means it will be hot tomorrow. Stay a while.

rows.en: Stars out, load shedding can't touch this.
rows.text: Sterre uit, beurtkrag kan dit nie raak nie.
rows.back: Stars out, load-shedding can't touch them.

rows.en: Night shift weather: approved.
rows.text: Nagskof weer: goedgekeur.
rows.back: Night-shift weather: approved.

rows.en: Dark outside, bright tomorrow.
rows.text: Donker buite, helder môre.
rows.back: Dark outside, clear tomorrow.

rows.en: Even Table Mountain's called it a day.
rows.text: Selfs Tafelberg het dit 'n dag genoem.
rows.back: Even Table Mountain has called it a day.

rows.en: Nothing a cup of rooibos won't fix.
rows.text: Niks wat 'n koppie rooibos nie kan regmaak nie.
rows.back: Nothing a cup of rooibos can't fix.

rows.en: The neighbourhood cats have taken over.
rows.text: Die buurt se katte het oorgevat.
rows.back: The neighbourhood cats have taken over.

rows.en: Perfect weather for pretending you'll go to bed early.
rows.text: Perfekte weer om voor te gee jy gaan vroeg slaap.
rows.back: Perfect weather for pretending you're going to bed early.

rows.en: The owls are judging your screen time.
rows.text: Die uile oordeel jou skermtyd.
rows.back: The owls are judging your screen time.

rows.en: Cape Town's twinkling. Probably.
rows.text: Kaapstad glinster. Waarskynlik.
rows.back: Cape Town is sparkling. Probably.

rows.en: The frogs have entered the chat.
rows.text: Die paddas het die gesprek betree.
rows.back: The frogs have entered the chat.
rows.note: 'die gesprek betree' = entered the conversation (calque of 'entered the chat')
rows.reason: 'die gesprek betree' is a stiff, word-for-word calque of 'entered the chat', and the meme register does not carry over.
reasons: DRIFT: 'die gesprek betree' is a stiff, word-for-word calque of 'entered the chat', and the meme register does not carry over.

rows.en: Warm enough to leave the window open. Brave enough?
rows.text: Warm genoeg om die venster oop te los. Dapper genoeg?
rows.back: Warm enough to leave the window open. Brave enough?

rows.en: Stars out, load shedding can't touch this.
rows.text: Izinkanyezi zikhona, ukucisha akukwazi lokhu.
rows.back: The stars are out; switching off can't do this.
rows.note: unclear: 'ukucisha' = switching off (a power cut / load shedding?)
rows.reason: 'ukucisha' (switching off) blurs 'load shedding' (kept as 'i-load shedding' elsewhere), and 'akukwazi lokhu' ('can't do this') loses 'can't touch this'
reasons: DRIFT: 'ukucisha' (switching off) blurs 'load shedding' (kept as 'i-load shedding' elsewhere), and 'akukwazi lokhu' ('can't do this') loses 'can't touch this'

rows.en: Perfect night to actually see the Milky Way.
rows.text: Ubusuku obuhle bokubona iNdlela yoSisi.
rows.back: A good night to see the Milky Way ('the Sisters' Road').
rows.note: unsure: 'iNdlela yoSisi' reads as 'the sister's road'; the standard Zulu name for the Milky Way is 'uMthala'
rows.reason: 'iNdlela yoSisi' is a doubtful name for the Milky Way (standard is 'uMthala'), so a reader may not recognise it; 'perfect' also became 'good'
reasons: DRIFT: 'iNdlela yoSisi' is a doubtful name for the Milky Way (standard is 'uMthala'), so a reader may not recognise it; 'perfect' also became 'good'

rows.en: Quiet out there. Almost suspicious.
rows.text: Kuthule ngaphandle. Cishe okusolisayo.
rows.back: It's quiet outside. Almost suspicious.

rows.en: The hadedas are sleeping. Finally.
rows.text: Ama-hadeda ayalala. Ekugcineni.
rows.back: The hadedas are asleep. Finally.

rows.en: Night shift weather: approved.
rows.text: Isimo sezulu sangobusuku: samukelwe.
rows.back: Night-time weather: approved.
rows.reason: 'Isimo sezulu sangobusuku' = 'night-time weather', which loses 'night shift'
reasons: DRIFT: 'Isimo sezulu sangobusuku' = 'night-time weather', which loses 'night shift'

rows.en: Dark outside, bright tomorrow.
rows.text: Umnyama ngaphandle, ukukhanya kusasa.
